review: love child is much more than just a yoga studio. the team go above and beyond to create a community that makes every member feel valued and supported. they helped me navigate through each stage of pregnancy and new motherhood with such care and kindness. through the pandemic they've continued to provide a five star service; all yoga, community and kids classes moved seamlessly online, and recordings are available so you can join when time / baby allows! i cannot recommend love child enough for yoga, support groups, pregnancy and childcare education and as a way to meet other parents; it's a very special place - either at 1 horatio street or on zoom!

if you enjoy waiting in a crowded waiting room, this is your place. if you like monthly visits, which takes hours, for medication refills- no matter how sick you might be, opposed to the every 3 month visit any other considerate doctor, per state law, schedules, this practice is for you.

consideration, maybe some compassion, for a chronically ill patient. what a freaking concept. 

how about a doctor who makes you feel like a criminal for having rheumatoid arthritis? 
argues with you about diagnoses??
tells you "it isn't that bad" when you are in tears over the pain??

yes to all? then boy is this your place.

after being a patient of dr. desilva's for over 2 years, going every single month (27 appts so far), i've realized these things. that sign which states "we take time for you, because we care"- complete bs.

half the time she argues with me about meds she herself has rx'd me- "you don't take that". uh, yes, i do, have been for years- here's the bottle.
(oh- always bring your med bottles to avoid this).

fills you with faith, yes?

the only reason i have continued going to this practice is because florida is a royal pita when it comes to certain, necessary medications. when someone has a condition that causes them chronic pain, sometimes pain meds are the only thing that works.

sorry my body didn't accept the "conventional treatments", and that i can't afford the $700 plasma therapy, not covered by insurance.

this does not make me a bad person, and it doesn't mean i am not in pain.

yet, she acts as if the ra is a façade, to the point where i feel like i should apologize to her for having a flare up. due to covid i was finally allowed to do a telephone visit. i expressed to dr. desilva that i was having one of the worst flare ups i have had to date, 10+ years, stating i would not have been able to drive to the office, had we not been able to do a telehealth visit.
unable to move my right arm/elbow/shoulder, it went all the way into my back, to my ankle....i was clear about the agony.
i was in tears.
what did she do? 

rolled her eyes and asked me to lift my arm.
i couldn't. 

my punishment? 
cut meds, not only the pain ones, but other ones too.  
??
(and she argued about my lyrica dosage, i showed her the bottle, she still cut the rx.)
did she rx anything else in place? nope. didn't even have the common courtesy to tell me my meds were being decreased, a pleasant shock when i went to the pharmacy for pick up.

she orders tests, labs, images, then doesn't take the time to review them. she has no clue i have a mass the size of a flipping baseball attached to my spine, from an mri in december, that she ordered. 

luckily, i have a primary who is on the ball.
sadly, i do not have a rheumatologist who cares.

allergy & rheumatology forces people to come to their office monthly, no matter how much pain and suffering a patient might be in (even the state says every 3 months is sufficient). 
$$it's all about$$

side bitch- desilva flat out fibbed to me, saying the state requires monthly face to face visits- why lie? i know i'm an insurance gold mine to you, $267 for 10 minutes, + my $40 co-pay, is that the reason? money?? not concern for your patient's care??

indeed. 

the only ones who truly care are jennifer and grace, the front desk compadres. the new np is ok, but it simply isn't worth the stress and upset each visit brings.

i'm a good patient who does not miss any appointments, tests, or other demands they force upon me. i don't pester them with anything, i abide by what they tell me to do, and remain in constant pain, miserable all the time.
i do not deserve to be treated this poorly. no one does.

do no harm, doctor.

people with progressive, chronically painful conditions, have breaking points. many times, those pain pills are the only thing that gives me the ability to do the bare minimum. that is what they are supposed to do, make life, at the very least, tolerable.
screwing around with a patient's rx, then not having the decency to return the call when the patients notices and inquires about it, shows you don't care, and severely impedes any faith patients might have.

to summarize (tl/dr friends)

this practice doesn't give one crap about you or your condition. they care about collecting the co-pay and belittling you as a wuss, as they act holier than thou.

they will argue with you about things like "your joint isn't hot, so it must not be that bad", or my personal favorite, "it's not bilateral, so it cannot be ra".

i am not kidding, that was said to me. 
it's ra, you fool. i have the tests you ordered showing it.
i qualified for disability because of it.
what am i missing here? 
it seems to peeve desilva because i want to be out of pain and functionable??

go anywhere else. sorry. i know it's an easy place to get to, convenient for many in our area, but it is not worth the stress, and you don't get the care you need.

might as well go to a vodoo doctor, probably have better luck.

i have had a number of bartholins cysts on my left labia for a few years. they tend to blow up overnight and are extremely painful, this most recent happened on a saturday and i was happy to be seen by mom doc instead of going to the emergency room in the middle of the covid19 pandemic since i could not be seen by my regular doctor until monday. this has been, without a doubt, the absolute most traumatic medical experience i've ever had. my pain tolerance is low and the insertion of the required catheter for this cyst to heal makes it intolerable- my regular doctor always prescribes a minor pain medication to assist me in sleeping and moving, let alone going to work. the np that assisted me (teresa i think) adamantly refused to give anything other than a topical lidocaine cream - this did nothing to ease any pain. i was told it would be taken out the following saturday and i would be given no pain relief- i had been bed ridden with fever nausea and pain for a week waiting for this appointment only to arrive this morning and have the medical doctor advise that the catheter must stay in place for at least an additional week - news to me. i asked about pain relief to assist, doctor said motrin and tylenol, both of which i have already been taking. then, without consent, pushes the other half of the catheter into my vaginal cavity and immediately triggers the ptsd i have surrounding an assault, and causing infinitely more pain than what i had already been experiencing. i called the number for assistance, anything, and was told i either must come back in or see a virtual doctor since no one could prescribe me anything without me reappearing in person. i know i maybe could have pressed harder but it is so humiliating to beg for what you need in the presence of a doctor who claims they know your body and pain better...
i feel violated and humiliated. i'm in crippling pain and i'm terrified to go to the emergency room because i also have asthma and am high risk for covid19. meanwhile my boyfriend can walk into his regular doctor and be given horse narcotics without even dropping his pants. 


this is not a safe place for people with vaginas. please protect yourself and go somewhere else. wait for your regular doctor. my safety and my body feel completely compromised.

review:
short version: phenomenal clinic. i gave birth 8 weeks ago, right when covid-19 was squeezing ny by the throat. it was a natural birth, my baby is healthy, and my body is basically back to normal - all things made possible by the expert care and support of dr brennan and his partner jais. the cliff notes on this clinic are that it is exceptional - immaculate, outstanding patient care, quirky and kind bedside manners all round, and connected to the best hospital in nyc. i cannot recommend the practice highly enough. long version: i was recommended to dr brennan by my boss (an experienced attorney who doesn't suffer fools), after i lamented the prevalence of arrogant, impersonal doctors. "you will love the brennans," my boss said. "they are eccentric, experienced, won't push an agenda, they'll give you all the time in the world, and will make you feel like family." she was right on all counts. the brennans invest seriously in their patients. throughout my pregnancy, they discussed each decision point in depth, teasing out the best path forward. perhaps because i'm a lawyer, i saw the fact that they would discuss pros and cons in front of me as a sign of true professionalism - they weren't arrogant enough to think there was one right path, and they weren't afraid to test one another's views to make sure we got it right. no question was stupid, and even if my appointment was initially 15 minutes long, they would keep answering my questions for an hour if needed. dr brennan is permanently on call for his patients, and i contacted him regularly with concerns that usually amounted to nothing but which he treated with the utmost seriousness. yes, the flipside of this kind of personal care is that appointments sometimes start late, but i would rather wait for an appointment and have this level of attention than efficiently get bad service. (and to be fair, people like me regularly rock up 45 minutes late and throw their whole schedule out of whack...).

another important plus is that dr brennan is the only doctor. in so many practices you never see the same doctor more than twice, so when you are sick they don't have a point of comparison. (nothing like being told you're fine when you feel like death). this meant that when i showed up at dr brennan's office late at night in serious pain from my contractions, he could trust right away that i wasn't playing around and needed pain relief stat. he could also read me like a book during labour - eg he suggested i use a mirror because i'm goal-orientated (and yes, it was a huge motivator!), and he knew when he could push me to the next level during delivery and when i truly needed a break from the pain. i'll always be grateful to dr brennan for staying so in tune with me. i trusted him, and if he'd said i needed a c-section i would have gone with that whether i'd wanted to or not - childbirth is full of risks and curveballs, and that's why we have experts like him to give us their best bet.

dr brennan's connection to lenox hill hospital is also a major drawcard. the staff are extremely supportive and professional, and that was so important since i was only allowed one support person (because of corona). a few days after my birth i had to go to the er at a brooklyn hospital on a non-birth related matter, and the staff were horrific - cold, unprofessional, no ppe, and the only way i got through that was because dr brennan coordinated with the er doctors (and calmed me down!). 

post-partem, the brennans have also been incredible. they have seen me by zoom, and started me on treatment on magnetic chair that gives a bajillian pelvic floor exercises in a short amount of time - well worth it!

i was horrified to read a review that dr brennan is a 'yeller' and jais tries to cover up - what bizarre accusations. nothing could be further from the truth. dr brennan is calm, kind, and nothing is too difficult. jais is also a delight - hilarious and incredibly supportive. they are cautious but not overzealous with testing, and they never pressured me - eg i decided not to get the amnio or the late term scans, and there was never any pressure to do the contrary. i was bemused by the reviewer who questioned the regular internal and external ultrasounds - how do you think dr brennan is supposed to see what's going on? holistic fortune-telling? x-ray vision? psychic ability? (side note: i loved these ultrasounds - hearing my baby's heart beat each week was the most incredible part of pregnancy. why would anyone not want that??) 

thank you, dr brennan and jais, for being with me on this remarkable journey. if i have another baby i want you by my side again every step of the way!

review:
i've done a lot of research on personal trainers in northern virginia and brian is top notch! i stumbled upon brian's business (bowtai fitness) on reddit and reached out via email to ask some questions about his process. he got back to me quickly and answered my bajillion questions very thoroughly. he also suggested setting up a time to meet so i could tell him a bit more about my fitness goals and check out the gym. 

through our chat, it became clear that brian takes a scientific approach to pt, is very safety conscious/is a stickler for form, and is very results-oriented. we also clicked on a personal-level, which is always nice to have with a trainer! i've been training with him for a few months and am very happy. i'll go into a bit more detail below.

approach:
brian created a custom program for me based on my fitness goals. it's all tracked and shared with me via google docs. every few weeks he switches up the program. i told brian i also want to train a few days a week at home and he was extremely accommodating. he asked me to take a picture of my gym and equipment and he created workouts that worked for me and my situation. this is above and beyond in my opinion! i also appreciate that he takes a holistic approach by incorporating nutrition into the program. he gives me my macros and updates them every so often depending on my progress.  

facilities:
i really like brian's gym! it's called district barbell and it's located very close to the mosaic district. it's very private. usually there are only a couple of other people in there during my sessions. he has all the equipment i could ever want - and more. it's very clean and parking is easy.

flexibility and availability:
brian is really flexible. it's truly a personal training program and he is happy to adjust the schedule, training, nutrition, etc. to you and your unique needs. he's also really accessible. he's very open to communicating via text if you have questions about nutrition or training!
obviously things are different now in the times of covid19. however, brian's flexibility is even more apparent during these times. he definitely has options to help you on your fitness journey remotely! he offers virtual pt sessions as well as killer group training sessions via zoom a few times a week. he is also still helping me write custom programs for my home gym and checking in every now and then to see how i'm doing.

i highly recommend training with brian!

let me start by saying bristol and his wife kenyatta have changed my life. i was at a point in my life where i had gained an unhealthy 50 pounds, every fad diet i tried was no longer working for me and i couldn't motivate myself to get through tougher workouts. i found them on yelp and was directed to there website where i was able to fill out a form to request more info. bristol contacted me right away and we scheduled my free in-person consultation for the next day. when we met at the gym, he showed me around, walked me through his fitness/nutrition plans and then had me complete a functional movement screening test to gauge my fitness level. because i liked the vibe of the gym, i signed up for a 3 month, 3x a week 30-minute 1-1 training program that came with customized bi-weekly meal plans (really great, easy recipes btw). 

in october, my first month, following the meal plan and working out with kenyatta 3x a week i lost 12.04 pounds and 9 inches around my body! in november i lost 10 pounds and 8 inches around body. in december, my last month of the program, i lost 9 pounds and 7 inches around body. it still shocks me how month after month, even through thanksgiving and christmas "off days", i still saw such a huge transformation in the way i look but most importantly the way i feel about myself. i still workout 3x a week with kenyatta because i love there programs so much; it has been 6 months in total at bbb and i still see my body transforming every week. i'm stronger, i no longer run out of breath going up the stairs, i'm down pant/dress and generic sizes in clothes. grateful is an understatement! 

i also want to mention bc of covid-19 concerns, bbb launched online workouts using zoom video so there are no excuses to delay your fitness goals.  if you are ready to put in the work and change your life - they'll get you to where you need to be!

the only good thing i have to say is that they are now participating in telehealth which hopefully will be efficient. hope they will continue this even after covid so patients' time is not wasted and they don't have to go into their building!

i feel like there are many improvements that they still need to make if they expect to grow.

the most unprofessional doctor's office i have had the misfortune to come across.

it took a long time to get a referral from my pcp and insurance to see an endocrinologist. they ultimately referred me to dr. jelen. after seeing the reviews here, i was worried, but made my appointment anyways, hoping for the best.

the doctor's office sent out multiple text messages and phone messages, all of which i answered in order to confirm my appointment. the morning of my appointment, i called to ask if the doctor was running on time (due to reviews here on yelp that reported her running two to three hours late). the receptionist said sorry, but my appointment had to be canceled because of "covid19." i asked why this wasn't the case the day before (when i confirmed my appointment), but she just reiterated that it was unforeseen until that very morning. that didn't make sense, but whatever.

she rescheduled me to a telemedicine appointment the following week, which i said was fine, even though i was already 9 month pregnant and the appointment was on my due date. a week later, i call thirty minutes before my appointment to make sure it was a telemedicine appointment, and not in the office, in order to make sure everyone was on the same page. she confirmed the telemedicine format to be the case, and confirmed the time of my appointment (11:45am). i wait. and wait. and wait ... i call again, to make sure they have my number right. yes, they have my number, but the doctor is running late. the receptionist said i was the first patient she would call when back in the office.

ok, so i wait longer, glued to my phone so i don't miss the call. after 2pm (2.5 hours after my appointment was supposed to start), i call again. they say they were canceling my appointment and i would have to reschedule, because of technical issues with telemedicine. i say i don't want to reschedule since my baby is due any day now, please can i talk to the doctor on the phone, like the receptionist and i were doing? she said no, and then seemed to perk up when i reminded her i was pregnant, and told me that the doctor doesn't see pregnant patients! dr. jelen's office and the referring office both knew i was pregnant, i mentioned it repeatedly. anyways, it barely matters because as i'm due any day now, i obviously won't be pregnant for long. i pleaded to speak with the doctor, or at least a manager. after a significant time on hold, i was transferred to "james" who refused to give me his last name and claimed to be the office manager. he talked over me, told me my opinion of their office didn't matter because i wasn't an "established patient," said in an accusatory way that all the bad reviews online were from people "like me" (whatever that meant, i just want health care, which i pay for). i couldn't get a word in; i tried repeatedly to please speak with the doctor, but he told me to get a different doctor and hung up on me!

now i don't know what to do except to complain to my insurance. i have been hypothyroid over a year, and have been trying this whole time to be worked up, but still haven't been seen. even if i get referred to another doctor's office, i'll have to wait months again to get an appointment. i'm an md (not an endocrinologist) and can't imagine treating patients this way. as a patient, you're powerless to get seen by this doctor. unbelievably unprofessional.

tl; dr: at the time of this writing, over 88% of her yelp reviews are 1-star. there is a serious problem here. run!

i am so disappointed in this place and almost tempted to leave a zero-star review. but i've gotten better service here in the past and hope they improve upon their service in the future. i called earlier because i was having some painful symptoms in my ear, nothing to do with coronavirus at all. i was told by the representative over the phone that the doctors were not seeing patients. but that the doctor would do a phone visit with me. i would like to know how the doctor can look inside of my ear properly over the phone? i understand that the dodgers do not want to catch coronavirus. but what about those of us who actually have other health issues that need to be addressed and looked at in person? now i have to go to an urgent care and hope that my insurance will cover the cost. an urgent cares centers are a nightmare to deal with, especially waiting for hours and hoping you will get some type of good service. also the person who took the phone call put me on hold and never came back. get some better phone service people please

i've been seeing dr. durrani for about 6 months now, and he has been great. understanding, knowledgeable, very receptive to patient needs and his office staff has been incredibly helpful. during covid-19, of course appointments are via zoom, and i've always been able to get a quick appointment without having to wait weeks like at other offices. i see him at prosperity wellness center which is in va, far from where i am in maryland, but it's always worth the trip, even before the zoom appts were in effect. his office staff at prosperity are incredibly helpful and polite, which you don't find everywhere.

i've had a poor experience with almost each appointment. i called to see if i could get a refill on an inhaler prescription that i've had for years, and they won't refill it because i haven't been in the office in the last six months. 6 months? this is what i heard last time when i needed a birth control refill. i'm not asking for pain medication.... these are non-addictive medications that overall healthy people are on. i have no real complications with my asthma, and all i wanted was to make sure i had an emergency inhaler at my dispowith the virus going around. i'm trying to be responsible by not exposing myself or other people unnecessarily at this point, yet i can't even get the right medication for my own well-being. i will be switching primaries as soon as possible. 

updating to state i was told i could not use telemedicine.

beware: these people will charge you for things they shouldn't and ghost your calls when they don't refund you as promised. i went for a covid-19 test and was required to do a free telehealth screening prior to making the appointment. this was a 2 minute video call that i was automatically charged $100 for (i did not authorize this charge). i called and they said once it goes through my insurance it will be refunded. (the owner specifically stated this service was free.) regardless, it went through my insurance and my explanation of benefits stated that i owed nothing. my card has still not been refunded. i have been calling their office the last two days and nobody answers, and the owner never responded to my email from april 30th. this place is a fraud and i would like to be contacted to remedy this issue asap. never going back here again, and would not recommend to anyone.

be aware of the bait and switch happening here. i've been sick for 2 weeks and wanted a covid 19 test because i have the symptoms except my fever wasn't that high. they charge 100$ for a two minute video conference call, well they agreed i should come in for a covid 19 test and told me they would bill my insurance. i had filled out all the information about my insurance before the video conference. the next day i went there for the test and they told me they don't take my insurance but i could pay 250$ for the test! are you kidding me? they refuse to refund my 100$.  this place is a ripoff.

just thought it might be useful to some for me to update my review, as i just came back from bringing my son here for his 9 month checkup. as i'm sure many of you can relate, i felt a little nervous about coming into a doctor's office given everything that's currently going on, but i am happy to report that cap is clearly doing everything they can to reassure patients and keep things as clean and disinfected as possible.

there was only one other family in the waiting room that i saw, everyone was wearing masks (including parents -- there's a sign on the door asking everyone over the age of 2 to wear a mask, and to ask at the front desk if you don't have one), the girls behind the desk asked if i needed to borrow a pen to fill out some paperwork and then assured me that they had been cleaned before handing it to me. the nurse wiped down the measuring mat after my son used it, and then, of course, there's hand sanitizer everywhere (as there was before.)

they also told me that while i will need to come back in for my son's 12 month appointment in 3 months, if there are ever any issues that creep up between now and then that they're doing telemedicine appointments on zoom, so just call and we can set that up. all in all, i felt reassured and safe bringing my baby in for his checkup even with all the pandemic-related stuff going on, and i just thought that might be helpful info for some parents to know! thanks cap!

covid-19 has made it difficult for the normal functions of society to carry on, however women's health and menopause center has made this transition easy for patients. i just wanted to say that i genuinely enjoy the option of telehealth and would love to see it incorporated into the practice after this is all over as well. i believe it is easy for both the doctors and patients, as we can discuss health matters from comfortable places. additionally, it is extremely time efficient. i had a telehealth appointment with dr. marcotte that took less than 15 minutes, whereas driving to the office, sitting in the waiting room, waiting for the doc, then the exam, yada yada yada, it can take a lot longer! it also limits the possibility of spreading illness if someone is sick - they can stay at home instead, which is how it should be from now on as well. i've been coming to this practice for at least 5 years now, and this new addition as been great. i hope it is as convenient for the health staff and doctors as it is for the patients. 

just an idea: i think conducting a telehealth survey would be a great idea. i don't think i am the only one who enjoys this method of health communication, and sending a survey out to patients via text or however would be a great way to assess the overall opinions of telehealth. or even after a telehealth session, maybe there could be an option to fill out a survey of how it went after the call ends, something like that. honestly i would offer to help construct a survey if people at the office are busy!! but regardless i think this would help the practice gauge how the patients feel about it.

also shoutout dr. marcotte, she's the best.

i first started with janet 16 years ago and was with her for a few years; she was instrumental in my growth at that time. i had a change in health insurance and could not see her for 10 years. i was able to get my insurance to accept outside providers and my luck had it that her name was on the list. i returned within the last two years and it has made a huge difference in my life.

i have always enjoyed our visits and am thankful to have someone who cares as much as she does. she is open minded and supportive. her approach has always been one of care and encouragement, but she won't let me run from reality either or lie to me. sometimes the truth hurts and what what must be said to me isn't what i want to hear at that moment. but it has always proven to be the right thing for me. if i don't like what i am hearing it's typically because i'm fighting it myself; not that it isn't true.

i am grateful to her guidance and constant support. she has been a blessing in my life and i don't know how things would look for me without her, but fortunately i still see her (well, phone visits while in quarantine ) regularly. she has guided me through some major moments in my life and i am happy she is back in my life during this time when i have completely different major changes happening.

this review doesn't do her justice; as my words fall short of describing how i feel. she's been exactly the person i have needed by my side in life and has exceeded my hopes for the role she fills. i'm so grateful!

be very careful regarding billing for this facility. my husband scheduled an appt, as he was having covid sx. the front desk insisted that he fill out paperwork for our entire family (4 people). we never discussed our children, just to say they barely had any sx. they were sleeping during our virtual visit, so the dr never even saw them. they never collected any data on them, never asked anything outside of this. nothing.
a few weeks later we get four bills for four copays. i called and they said "well, we have paperwork for 4 people so you have to pay for 4 people." they never did anything with our children! the dr was nice, but this is insane. they scammed us from the start.
i do not recommend going to this urgent care!

my husband and i have had two prior experiences with couples counseling that didn't do much to help us resolve our issues or bring us to deeper connection.  our experience with karen gordon at empathi counseling has brought us farther into connection than we have ever been before, and we couldn't be more thankful that we found her!  karen is warm and empathetic, and creates such a beautifully welcoming and safe space to really help couples search deep within themselves and fully open up and engage in the healing process, together.  we leave every session feeling more connection and love, and through our sessions have developed a strong framework for working through our issues at home as they arise in daily life.  

since the start of the shelter in place orders in sf for the covid-19 pandemic response we have had online sessions via zoom.  the team at empathi has been vigilant at providing their patients with options for telemedicine sessions and sharing the information needed to make these sessions happen.  we felt just as comfortable having our session with karen via zoom from the comfort of our own home, and are very grateful we can continue our work as a couple - even if we can't meet face to face!  

all our thanks to karen and the whole empathi team!  

-sarah (and dave)

other than dr.cox, the rest of the staff both medical and admin suck and are liars. we have been going there since their old small office and we realized that if you don't double-check the bill, they will play around with medical codes and charge you for things that you never requested. it's true. again this is not for dr. cox who is an amazing guy!. also, just recently, we called bc we thought one of us has  covd19 so they just asked us few questions on the phone and told us to go to another facility for testing. this morning, we get a bill for telemedicine for $200?! i mean really, you are gaming the system? since when a simple call to see if you are conducting tests become telemedicine. thieves! the min dr. cox leave, we will leave!

i am currently positive for covid 19 and am experiencing tremendous muscle spasms that are not allowing me to sleep. i called care now for a virtual visit and explained my issue, i was immediately met with, "if you're feeling that bad, you need to go to the er, we can't help you". as someone who works in the hospital, i can assure you that the last thing an er needs right now is someone covid positive coming in for back pain needing a muscle relaxer and taking up room in the er and vital ppe and cleaning supplies. that is exactly why we have care now's. quite frankly, this response was lazy and irresponsible. hca is better than this quality of patient care.

i have been a member at mhop for almost three years and i have to say it is the best gym i have ever belonged to.  they always have been amazing but with this covid thingy they have really stepped up to the plate.  this whole time they have made sure that monday through saturday there are multiple exercise  programs for us members, both live zoom and recorded.  coaches check up on us multiple times a week to make sure we are staying active and to see how we are doing.  vince also has 2-3 live chats per week.  he keeps us informed and motivated.  vince and the coaches, who are all trained, knowledgeable and caring, have gone way above and beyond to keep us strong and moving!  love this place!

absolutely the worst . simply interested in making their money. sometime ago, they stopped accepting insurance for office visits. $190 to walk in the door. when i ran out of my medication, and simultaneously lost all income due to the pandemic i asked if they would kindly refill my meds and when i could afford a visit, i would be back. nope! they said they would be happy to schedule a virtual visit for $95 (plz send cc info) and bill my cc another $95 next month. thx a lot. no help. we are in a crisis here. all i needed  was for them to call the pharmacy. pitiful, greedy and shameful.
address: 777 S New Ballas Rd Ste 100E Ste 100 E

review:
i am so happy to be a member here.  with everything that is happening right now in the world with covid-19/coronavirus/sars-cov-2 much has been completely shut down and shattered.  
while times continue to get more tough crossfit flood exists to improve the quality of lives of its members.  
mike the owner has shut down the gym however he continues to have group classes as well as 1 on 1 via the zoom app.  its really a lifesaver and helping me keep my eyes focused on self improvement which will only help me get through this difficult time as well as what comes after.  thank you crossfit flood, coach mike and all of the coaches

i recently had my first session with dr. walker via zoom. he's very affable, calm, kind and easy to talk to. upon initially seeing him on my computer screen, he immediately exuded a calming and safe atmosphere that enabled me to candidly discuss everything with him. 

also, unlike my prior psychiatrists, dr. walker takes great care when ordering prescriptions and closely monitors the dosage, earring on the side of caution. i welcome and appreciate this approach, since over-medication continues to be a problem in the healthcare industry. 

i look forward to my future sessions with dr. walker and would highly recommend him. 

just to note: his assistant, caroline, is very pleasant--she has been very helpful and responsive with scheduling my first appointment.

you know what is worse than being stuck at home with this pandemic? being stuck at home with back pain! i'm limiting how much i'm going out so i didn't really feel comfortable about going to an office for physical therapy treatment. my cousin said i should contact healthfit because they were offering a telehealth option. i was a little weary at first but my cousin had been to them before and said they were really good and thorough. i ended up booking a session with dr. daphne and wow... i never thought i could learn so much from a session. she looked at the way i was sleeping, my desk setup and gave me strategies to do throughout the day. since i'm at home, i really have no excuses not to do the exercises. i've had two sessions so far and she's also given me lots of tips for running because now my knees hurt from running outside. overall, i'm super happy i contacted them because they are keeping me going during this stressful time. can't wait till this stay at home order is lifted so i can see them in person!

i was trying to schedule a telemedicine appt to speak to my physician that had prescribed me meds that i had critical questions regarding and sara the manager personally disregarded my appointment and told me to follow up with woundcare. when she is well aware of my circumstances and that it takes time to get authorizations and appointments, especially due to covid. everyone at burbank urgent care is exceptional and provides wonderful service. this review is regarding sara. she was rude to me and denied my scheduled appt and gave me a huge anxiety attack.

i will not go anywhere else when i am not well.  this location has a great staff.  once i find a doctor that understands me, i stay with that doctor.  i have been requesting for dr. devaraj.  it seems the more i see him the more he understands my symptoms.  the chart helps, but i think putting the chart and the face helps better.  today i used their online service due to the coronavirus.  i self-quarantined as i didn't feel like exposing myself in person.  dr. devaraj and i had a video appointment via zoom.  he asked the same questions he always asks when i visit.  it was so convenient.  i like the staff.  i like the attentiveness.  thanks you for the service.

i have been working with nataly the past few months and the decision to hire her as my health coach has been one of the best decisions ever. i wasn't really sure what to expect but the second i started talking to her, i immediately felt at ease and excited. she has helped me work through some anxiety i have around food and has really helped me realize why i would do certain things. in addition to the actual health/food help and insight, she has also helped me learn about the different parts of myself and how to let them all co exist so i'm the best version of myself. nataly is the best - she has been extremely flexible during this (pandemic) and has made sure my sessions continued via phone/video chat so we don't lose cadence and progress. i will be bummed when my sessions are over but also very thankful for the amazing experience she has provided. i highly recommend her yoga classes as well!

i was very nervous to take my 3 year old son to an urgent care during this pandemic but i chose this urgent care because they did virtual visits. i had mine online and the doctor suggested i come instead so they can check my sons throat and ears. again i was nervous but at this point he was on 2nd day of fever and sore throat and wasn't wanting to eat. i knew i needed to get him on antibiotics asap. i came in and i was so happy that i did ! besides us there were only 2 other ppl waiting & it was so nice and clean. we got seen right away , like legit the whole visit took less than 15 min . we got seen and the pa checked out my sons throat and right away told me he has strep throat & even shined the light in the back of his throat and showed me what she saw. she told be she'd be sending in the prescription right away. another 10 min gone by and i had a text that my sons medicine was ready for pick up . so happy with this urgent care!

as a pa-c i am usually the one people write reviews about.  it's totally weird to be on the opposite side and be a patient.  i had to come to the clinic with my husband to be tested for covid19.  i developed symptoms a week ago that progressively worsened and i finally broke down and scheduled an appointment to be evaluated for covid19.  i've been home for two weeks as part of a rotating provider time-off related to the slowdown caused by the pandemic.  nonetheless, cece (cecily aguirre, ma), janet (janet muratalla, office mngr & ma), and connie (constance bouvier, pa-c) were all amazing.  cece did an excellent job at contacting me to do my virtual visit right on time as well as getting my hpi (history of present illness).  she was sweet, professional, and expedient.  connie was compassionate, treated me with respect as a patient, and helped allay my anxieties regarding my symptoms and their implications for what could be going on in my body.  when i arrived at the clinic to get swabbed, janet was amazing.  she accommodated myself and my husband even though we were running late.  she thoroughly explained the procedure, explained the discomfort that was likely to be experienced (there's a reason they call this nasopharyngeal swab the "brain biopsy"), and then apologized for the discomfort experienced during the procedure.  this team is truly world class.  i would normally say that as their coworkers.  but now having been on the patient side of things and having experienced it first hand, i can definitely say they are amazing.

dr. coppas took over from another physician at primary care of the treasure coast so had to make appointment with her. her receptionist megan said regardless of the fact of patient health conditions and that we are in a nationwide and statewide state of emergency due to covid-19, they do not do virtual visits nor give an emergency supply of medications if the patient feels it is too risky for their health to come into the office. megan re-iterated that they never have sick people in the waiting room which is of course unbelievable. she has a lot of faith in people recognizing they might infect someone and calling first despite the fact that people are flying everywhere and knowingly carrying the infection to their destination. the woman in south korea considered the vector there had over 1,000 contacts by the time she became ill and was identified. medicare instructions for providers are to institute virtual visits and emergency supplies of medications when possible.
fac_name: Primary Care of the Treasure Coast

review: i am giving them 2 starts because our initial experience was okay and i also realize they are trying to operate during a pandemic with that being said, i took my son in for individual counseling shortly before the holidays. his first therapist was okay and did an good job of focusing on him as the patient and not me during the assessment. he was an older gentleman and kind of hard for my teenage son to relate to but over all not bad. he quit at the first of the year and transferred him to another therapist which was also older. we requested a younger therapist or someone that specializes in adhd. he was assigned a new therapist that was extremely overbooked and very difficult to get regular appointments with. between jan and march he was only scheduled for 2 sessions when he was previously getting weekly counseling. then the pandemic happened and his session were moved to telehealth which did not work so after a lot of back and forth with the front office i was told that he would have a phone session but that never happens. i would get calls from the office stating that the therapist said the phone was going straight to voicemail mail. they had no way off connecting the call if we called into the office. today i get a bill for $155 for no show fees. i don't see how they can justify charging a no show fee in the middle of a pandemic when they do not have the proper platform in place to provide telehealth. i understand that this is unprecedented but i think charging clients extra fees during this time is abhorrent practice.

i have been a patient of dr. hoelchers' for several years and have seen several concerning patterns within his practice.

this dr. does not respect the time of his customers (patients). i went in for my annual checkup having labs done two weeks prior and was told during my appointment that i needed to schedule another appointment to review my lab work. i would have appreciated a phone call stating that my labs were not available and that i would need to reschedule my appointment if it was a requirement that my labs were reviewed with me in person so that i could schedule another appointment. this no doubt could have been uploaded to my patient portal and discussed with me over the phone, saving me from paying for another office visit and the time that it takes out of my busy schedule to go to another appointment. nevertheless as requested i scheduled another appointment.

on the date of the subsequent appointment i was 12 minutes late due to being required to fill out paperwork at my job (dod) before i left for the day due to contingency situations with covid 19. i was then told that it was their policy that a $45 no show fee is charged if the customer is more than 10 minutes late for their appointment and there was no way that they could remove the charge. i stated that i would gladly wait for my appointment that same day because all we were doing was going over labwork. i was then told that i needed to either reschedule or i could get a telemedicine appointment the next day where i will no doubt be charged for another appointment and an additional fee for telemedicine.

in my most recent appointment, i was also informed that i was being charged for something over a year later that was covered under my insurance plan.

additionally, you do not see the dr. at all you see a pa where previously i was seeing dr. hoelscher directly. the pa is nice, thorough, and takes the time to answer any questions that you have, but  i may not be receiving the level of care that i previously had been receiving. 

furthermore, the front office staff have no empathy for their customers at all and act like mindless automata. all forms are printed and as a blind person, i have requested numerous times that my forms be sent in an accessible format or to be filled out prior to the appointment via the patient portal so that i can fill them out myself. why in 2020 are they still using a paper questionnaire when all of this information is then typed into a computer later on? i have informed the staff about how to make these forms accessible and more convenient for their patients time and time again, but i keep getting told that "there is no way for us to accomplish that." this has the alternative benefit of minimizing the spread of microorganisms, etc. i am sure that other offices have no doubt figured it out.
address: 250 E Basse Rd Ste 208 Alamo Heights Primary Care

review:
i called to schedule a covid-19 test for multiple reasons: 
- i am a nurse currently working in a long term care facility.
- i have been exposed to and in direct contact with multiple people who tested positive for covid-19.
- i have a doctor's order for the test from a physician in which i had a virtual visit.
- i have experienced tightness of the chest in the past week.
- i had a cough & sore throat several weeks ago.

they denied me for testing. unreal. 
the place where i work has had 14 positive cases of covid-19 and i live with someone who has two autoimmune diseases, which i stated over the phone, yet they still will not let me get tested at their facility.

i highly recommend insite digestive health care and dr. chen.  dr. chen and his staff has been caring for my mom for two years.  during the pandemic, we were able to schedule a telehealth appt with dr. chen.  the front desk was very responsive and prompt about setting up the appt for us, and dr. chen was very caring and patient to my mom during her first telehealth session.  dr. chen and his staff are whom i would highly recommend and refer to for anyone who ask me about gastrointestinal problems.  two thumbs up!
fac_name: inSite Digestive Health Care - San Gabriel
address: 207 S Santa Anita St Ste P15

review: i had my first visit with dr. gilligan last week via a telemedicine app due to covid. she seemed very nice and really on the ball. she discussed testing options for possible conditions, let me know how likely those seemed, and what treatment would look like after, should any of them pan out. it only took a week to get an appointment and her staff was great about helping me set up the app for the visit. i never felt rushed and she took a lot of time to address my concerns.
address: 35 Collier Rd NW Ste 775 Piedmont Healthcare

review: my child is currently working with erika for ot. i have had a wonderful experience with multiple provider's at the northborough location. we began therapy in 2019 and have already noticed leaps and bounds with my child's emotional regulation and overall functionality. since covid-19, they have integrated therapy via telehealth and it has provided normalcy and structure for my child. they've been looking forward to their appointments weekly and they're still receiving the quality care that they need. i highly recommend the personable, efficient and compassionate staff that work for barrett family wellness center.

i've been going to michigan ave. primary care for about 2 years since i relocated to chicago.  everyone is kind, helpful, thorough, and their urgent care equivalent is a few floor down.  when you can't get in to a dr. with the practice, this is an option. my favorite is dr. kupkowski, but pas jocelin and erin are also great.  with the covid-19 situation going on, i had something i needed to see someone for a few weeks ago before all of this started up.  they got me in when i needed and although they would have preferred that i did a telemedicine call, i really wanted to go in person and they understood and accommodated.  thank you mapc!

leaving the house with a toddler during a pandemic is frightening, but having to go to an urgent care that is also a covid testing site is the last place a parent wants to be. 

my child fell and needed stitches. i called ahead and was told to come in. although the place was empty i waited to be seen by the physician almost a half hour because he was on a telemedicine call. 

the nursing assistant that came to take vitals did not wash her hands and only did so after i asked. i asked her to clean the oxiometer and she refused saying it was done and they didn't have a lot of patients that day, however i told her that i didn't feel comfortable unless i cleaned it so i pulled a lysol wipe out of my bag and cleaned it myself. 

dr. chao came in (also did not wash his hands as he was wearing gloves, and did put on a fresh pair when i asked) and looked at my child's wound and said my child may need stitches, he said that it was my call to make, however, he did recommend it.

i went with his advice and decided to proceed. he brought in an assistant and i asked if it possible to do this alone as i wanted to minimize risk. he said no. 

i saw that the physician and assistant were only equipped with a surgical mask, and would need to be within inches of my child, so i asked if it was possible that he wore a respirator or n95, to which he replied "i don't have one would you like to donate some to us" in a condescending tone.

i cannot believe that this is the level of ppe this facility has. i understand there is a shortage of ppe however, this should be standard for a facility that is a pediatric covid testing site. how is a covid testing site not equipped with n95's?! especially when the parent requests it. 

furthermore, he did not inform me until during the procedure that stitches raises the chance of infection. i was upset and told him that he should have disclosed this prior so that i could have made a more inform decision. he told me that there must have been miscommunication because he did (i assure you he did not). 

i really wonder if i made the right choice. it's not easy to decide if going to an urgent care is the right thing to do, and i really hoped that i would have had a better experience. 

i do believe it's important to be forthcoming with patients and let them know prior to coming that there is no proper ppe, especially when a medical supply company down the street sells n95's. (pico medical).

i called the office to report this incident and the office manager was friendly however i gave this some thought and wanted to be fully transparent so that other parents can make an informed decision on coming here. i wish i would have known i wouldn't have come here during a pandemic. now i'm left wondering did i do the right thing? would the ceo bring his child there with no ppe? it's a sad thing that this corporation hasn't outfitted its staff with the proper protection. 

fair warning for a parent. this is definitely something to consider. 

the one star was for the receptionist who was kind and made the check in process at the front desk go smoothly.

this review is specifically for the echn birthing center at manchester hospital. i had my son in december and still think about what amazing care i received throughout my two day stay at the hospital. my heart goes out to all of the incredible nurses and hospital staff as they work bravely and tirelessly during this horrifying coronavirus pandemic. the nurses were so incredibly supportive, helpful and caring as my husband and i navigated the first few days of parenthood and all the accompanying challenges. 

a few things to note:
-the hospital/echn has excellent prenatal and postpartum programming, from their pregnancy/infant care class and prenatal fitness to their new mothers' group that meets weekly (currently virtually on zoom!). they've also got a remarkable doula program (shannon made a huge difference in my birth experience, she's amazing). 
-delivery & recovery are in the same room which i found to be a total asset. plus, the room is huge with plenty of room for nurses, bags, partners, visitors, etc without feeling cramped. 

i live in the hartford area but my midwife practice only delivers at manchester hospital, which is how i ended up here. it really made all the difference in having such a supportive experience.

i really love the care i receive at physicianone. i always get taken in very fast and receive ample care. with the covid-19 pandemic going on, i decided to seek care virtually. it took me only 10-15 minutes to be seen which is very fast compared to other telehealth sites that i was referred to. i received helpful and honest care with pa anna k. i'll continue to highly recommend physicianone in chestnut hill to anyone! both virtually & in-person!

i can't believe how easy this was. 

i'm on my last bottle of a prescription med that i need to take daily, and i'm out of refills. i had my pharmacy try to reach my pcp to issue an extra refill just to get me through the craziness of this current pandemic, but she never responded. i'd been having issues with my regular doc anyway (she lost my last lab results and has a habit of not calling me back), and this is not the time for me to visiting any doc's office in-person... or looking for a new doc.

so i was stuck on getting this prescription filled to get me through the next few months, but in my search i stumbled across plushcare. i tried it based on its online reviews and figured there was no harm if it didn't go well -- it couldn't be worse than my current situation with my m.i.a. doc.

the site was easy to use and i got an appointment in the timeframe i wanted with no problem -- though i booked it just the night before. the interface during the video chat worked well and i really liked dr. leung, who was conscientious and had a good bedside manner. i can't believe what we accomplished so quickly -- and from the comfort of my own couch!

i got notified right away that she'd called the prescription in to my pharmacy, which filled it immediately. now i can breathe easy for at least the next 3 months.

easiest doctor's visit ever!

i have to say this was the best doctor visit i have had.  dr. riad abdelkarim video call was outstanding.  he talked to me in a very friendly and professional way.  he even took the time to listen to one of my boring health story which concerns my son.  an never made me feel i was wasting his time.  he answers all my questions about covid-19 and antibody an let me know how we, noticed i said we, were going to proceed and how the follow-up would occur.  this is my first time using a service like this,i.e., video chatting for medical consultation.  but i may use this all the time.  great job plushcare & especially dr. riad abdelkarim

their service is fantastic!  this was my first experience with telemedicine and it was seamless.  they have an excellent platform.  easy to sign up and register.  i was looking for an antibody test for covid-19 and they were advertising this ability using quest diagnostics and labcorp locations around the country.

i spoke with dr. david dantes.  he was awesome!  thorough, caring and professional.  i chose him for his excellent reviews, 5 star rating, and over 40 years of experience.  i give him 5 stars too!

made an appointment with quest around mid day, brought them my printout with the order for the test, and they took a blood sample... sent it off to their lab.  the next morning received an email with the test results from plushcare.  

very highly recommended

i can't say enough good things about jeff and solutions pt. a few months ago, i tore my hamstring and couldn't run without serious pain. after a few sessions with jeff, covid-19 hit and i was unable to have in-person appointments. thankfully, solutions started offering telehealth appointments. i wasn't sure how this would work, but jeff figured out ways to incorporate the limited equipment i have at home and modify exercises so they still worked. i'm slowly easing back into running and am so excited to get back out there! if you need pt during the pandemic, this is your place.

did you know that heart disease is the leading cause of death for men, women, and people of most racial and ethnic groups in the united states? another staggering fact is one person dies every 37 seconds in the united states from cardiovascular disease.  but, even more, frightening to me is knowing that heart disease is the leading cause of death in women.   just knowing these facts, i'm glad that dr. yamada is on my healthcare team at queens medical center.   i regard him as progressive, knowledgeable, compassionate yet straightforward with his explanations to me and i have been under his care for at least the past decade or longer.  

my scheduled annual office visits may include in-office treadmill stress tests or ekg in addition to getting my basic vital signs.  dr. yamada has also prescribed other diagnostic tests to help him to decide if he needs to recommend changes in my lifestyle or medication.  this time around, during pandemic restrictions, i participated in a telehealth visit.  this was my first-time using hmsa's online care application.  after registering for the application (on friday, in preparation for my monday appointment), i found this application easy-to-use and quite intuitive.   on monday morning, about 20 minutes prior to my designated appointment time, i signed in to the app's "waiting room".  then, about 3 minutes prior to my appointment time, dr. yamada's nurse signed me in to my appointment and dr. yamada made his appearance on-time as he usually does for office visits.

the telehealth visit was just as good as an in-person visit except that i had taken my own blood pressure and weight at home.  yeah, yeah... unfortunately, i had to report the "corona pounds" gains.  dr. yamada had reviewed the results of the blood draws that i had taken a couple of days prior to this appointment.  i guess that because of the pandemic concerns, he and his nurse were wearing face masks even for this session.  i liked that their office takes this pandemic seriously and takes all possible precautions to not only protect themselves but to protect their patients.    i sort of like this telehealth application as it was easy to use and i didn't even have to leave the comfort of my home.

anyway, i've already scheduled my next office visit in 2021 and look forward to the continued maintenance of good heart health through dr. yamada's recommendations.

why are you denying patients access to telehealth appointments? i was flatly denied one this morning with no reasoning given. you want an 80 year old with respiratory issues to come in to your office to get test results during the coronavirus???

i'm a stickler for quality having been trained by the best quality engineer in the country so when i go to a provider or restaurant and see nothing but professionalism, cleanliness, courtesy it makes an impact to me. from making my appointment to greeting me, 5 stars. tony and his apprentice alisa have helped me overcome my back injury from a mva and have been so accommodating to me with the highest level of expertise. i was seriously wowed by them and that's rare for me. most places i message owners rather than leaving crappy reviews to offer improvements. i can't think of any improvements except maybe more patronage during covid 19. there office is now doing virtual visits. tony and staff thank you!

this was my first visit to alta vista dermatology.  because of the coronavirus pandemic it had to be a telehealth consult.  we were really impressed with the receptionists at the front desk.  i called about 5:00 p.m. as i had a question about forms, etc, that needed to be filled out and even at 5:00 one answered and was very polite in helping out.  dr. draper was patient and warm.  fortunately i didn't have anything serious but it was nice to have a doctor that seemed to really care.

i had a shoulder pain that required physical therapy.  but because of the coronavirus lockdown, i only had remote appointments through their telemedicine service.  i was thoroughly surprise how remarkably convenient and effective it was.  all my appointments were on time. i didn't have to commute.  i just stayed in living room.   most important of all,  i felt that treatment was just as good as in person visit.  harris was outstanding in guiding me through the exercise and stretches and making sure i follow the proper form.  in a few sessions my shoulder was noticeably better.

i highly recommend physical therapyworks and their telemedicine option -- lockdown or no lockdown.

i was looking into the possibility of getting plastic surgery, but was worried about how to obtain a consultation and get some questions answered during the covid-19 pandemic.  i saw that cosmeticare, who i already knew was highly regarded in the area, was offering "virtual consultations," so i inquired about setting one up.  within minutes a representative obtained my information and set me up for a zoom call with jennifer (assistent practice manager and consultant) and dr. von maur the following morning.  in advance of the call, jennifer was able to obtain "before" photos from me and provide me with simulated "after" photos to discuss with dr. von maur during our call.

the zoom call was great - jennifer, dr. von maur and i were all at our respective homes, but were able to walk through all of my options and answer any questions i had.  could not have been an easier process and really put my mind at ease.

since then, i worked with jennifer on scheduling and pricing for my surgery ... and she has been there every step of the way since -- 24/7, including weekends -- to answer any questions or concerns i might have to put my mind at ease.  

went in for my pre-op appointment last week and was beyond impressed with the office and staff - both relaxing, friendly and inviting.  surgery on the 18th and i cannot wait to see the results!

this cvs is just around the corner from me (and apparently very close to where joe exotic from tiger king used to run a pet store?!???!).... anyway, i find myself here pretty often just because it's so close, you know? it's not my pharmacy either, but they do have all the basic groceries and goodies i tend to need last minute when i'm out and about. i'm happy i can walk in and very quickly grab my favorite mascara, a gallon of milk, a phone charger, and a bottle of ibuprofen all at once, in and out in few minutes without the distractions of target or the lines at kroger. i'm also so happy to see cvs taking precautions concerning covid-19 as well as offering virtual doctors appointments. 

there is a great team of employees here and i'm always warmly greeted and assisted!

i have been working with mindful therapy group for 4 years, and the leadership and flexibility of mindful therapy group over the last month has blown me away. with the covid-19 outbreak there was a lot of uncertainty in regards to what the best path forward would be, but mindful therapy group waylaid those fears for me. leadership and a willingness to try new things has led mtg to be able to support all of their employees working remotely, as well as offering remote telehealth services to all current and new clients looking to continue their regular sessions with providers. knowing that my workplace cares for my and the community's wellbeing and is willing to put in the hardwork i see daily has given me new insight into the type of work environment i treasure and will work to maintain for the future

choosing a nursing home is hard.  a year ago my grandmother was living alone in her house and as the dementia was getting worse we began the process of looking for a memory care facility.  we toured several and none of the options were great.  then grandma fell and broke both her arms and we were forced to find an acute rehab facility that also had memory care capabilities.  the list of options is short, and we selected marquis.  i cannot recommend them enough.  the food sure wasn't great but that's the only negative thing i could say.  the staff is absolutely amazing.  they were able to prevent my grandmother from needing the memory care protections by simply interacting with her.  they were able to help this fiercely independent woman transition to a situation that she never wanted to be in, and to thrive in that space.  during the covid pandemic they were very accomodating about zoom calls and facetime to replace in-person visits, and did everything right to prevent covid from entering the facility.  my grandmother had a heart attack last  week and moved to hospice.  due to covid they would only allow two visitors in total, so my sister and i spent 40 hours at my grandmother's bedside.  the staff was so caring and supportive it was incredible - especially catherine and kayla.  the whole team made this difficult period much easier and my very grateful to how great they treated my grandmother.  i cannot recommend this place enough!

immediately following this incident, i called a local health quest practice and was able to schedule a telehealth appointment within 2 hours. i was able to speak with a wonderful doctor who was compassionate and thorough. the doctor gave me great advice on how i could alleviate my pain and help me heal. thank you so very much health quest!!!

my son has been a patient of dr hu since his birth 4.5 years ago. this morning he woke up with possible pink eye symptoms. we have self quarantined since suggested in ca due to corona virus. dr hu office refused to see him as it wasnt just a wellness visit and suggested we take him to urgent care exposing him to all the other illnesses floating around. disappointing....they didnt offer telemedicine or any proactive solution to help treat or protect our child as we have.

dr. allen is a wonderful, caring, upbeat, terrific, educated, and knowledgeable doctor, that not only is a caregiver, and healer, but is a teacher in that he takes the time with you as a patient to explain, educate, and teach you about why you're feeling the way to feel, and how the things he prescribes or treatments he advises you to do will help your health and life. 

today of all days, march 19th - admits all the chaos we as americans are undergoing hourly to adjust to social distancing, and living during this pandemic that is coronavirus, i had scheduled an upper gi test. i followed through with the test this morning at 9am, the dr. that did the test let me know he would be sending his results to dr. allen this afternoon. at 11am this same day, march 19th, i got a call from dr. allen's office letting me know that dr. allen had the results of my test, and due to the coronavirus, he would like to schedule with me a telemedicine call to chat about these results. his secretary told me to go to there website which i did, and i found the link to schedule the tele-appointment.

i pulled up the link on my iphone, and in an instant, it should on my phone a video chat, and read on-screen "your appointment will begin shortly". in less time i wait signing in at a waiting room, bing, dr. allen popped up on my screen. 

he explained to me he got my results, and the office was trying to do these tele-appointments were they could now. all from the comfort of my home dr. allen read and explained my test results, he prescribed me medication which was sent over to my pharmacy, and we set a future tele-appointment to follow up on how i was feeling. in less than 2 hours i had all my answers, without having to run all over the valley (risking exposure). it was not only convenient and safe, but dr. allen still provided me with the same great personal care that makes me feel like i am a member of his family.

thank you so much dr. allen for helping me get healthy and providing me with such great care.

sincerely,

sammy

from my wife: judy is amazing.  typically, we would have met in person.  given the situation with covid-19, she was extremely flexible and has been able to communicate with me via zoom, calls, and text.  her knowledge is tremendous and she is open to sharing it and educating you.  not only can she help with lactation, but her expertise also extends to other areas of caring for a newborn, like reviewing sleep schedules and expectations.  i, 100%, without reservation, recommend judy.  she is extraordinary.  a+

unorganized staff pretty much sums it up. my first visit i paid my $40.00 copay and then waited 2.5 hours past my appointment time with no explanation or apology from the office staff. my second visit went better though i was again charged a $40.00 copay even though my insurance only calls for one charge per referral. my third visit was rescheduled due to covid-19 which was fine. they then called me on my reschedule day  and told me the doctor was only doing virtual visits but i would now have to get another referral as they had dragged out my visits more than 3 months which is the insurance companies time limit. if you have a lot of time to waist and are in no hurry to get better i highly recommend castle orthopaedics.
friendly and efficient office, awesome telemedicine visits with good followup. highly recommended, especially during coronavirus sequestration when some pcps are not available.

in the midst of this covid-19 scare, i want to thank david zarian for taking the correct precautionary measures to prevent the spread of the virus. he has accommodated my appointment by hosting a video meeting through zoom and was able to refill my prescription over the phone. i did not need to risk being around sick people in the doctors office because of this!

i started going to this studio last fall, a few months after my wife recommended it. she had been there for some injury rehabilitation and then general mobility and strength. i studied and taught martial arts and fitness for many years, and enjoyed doing a variety of other fitness modes including trx, cross fit, cycling, yoga and some pilates. in so doing i accrued a fair amount of knowledge and scar tissue to go along with it. with the work i'm doing here, i feel like once again i am expanding my capabilities rather than just fighting not to lose them.

we have worked with jenna and julia, but more recently has been primarily julia due to schedules. she is a great instructor, very knowledgeable, patient and thorough. i look forward to every class, and afterwards always feel like i've done valuable work to improve my mobility, body awareness and core strength. since the covid-19 situation they made a transition to online lessons and those have been great as well. we miss the springboards but they lent equipment out to those who needed it, and we all work on matts in our homes while julia presides over a small group on zoom and keeps a close eye on each of us. we have enjoyed adapting to this new situation with her. whether its in the studio once we can do that again or online, i highly recommend corpo kinetic.

we started coming here in january for my 2 year old daughter then covid hit and we started taking zoom classes with tiffany. as you can imagine, this presented many challenges in learning but we evolve. i mention tiffany specifically because she deserves the spot light. she is energetic, excellent with young ones, and she never takes her foot off the learning/progress pedal. we are now almost 6 months later and my daughter is hitting her language milestones and is talking up a storm. 

in the beginning i was sad and discouraged and i want others who might be where i was in january to "trust the process" and know that there is a light at the end of the tunnel.
fac_name: Let's Talk Speech and Language Therapy

review: this is beyond disappointing. granted i will take fault in not coming into the doctor prior to the pandemic but to not provide a telehealth option to prescribe asthma medication that i have been on for well over 10 years is outrageous. i used to love this place when dr. melis was there but i truly feel this facility does not care about there patients any longer. if i could give 0 stars i would.

i've been here a couple of times and they have been great! i've had ethmoid sinusitis and it very painful. today i felt the symptoms and called for a telehealth appointment. i didn't feel like sitting in a waiting room during this covid pandemic. i was able to obtain medications and instructions. within the hour, picked up my medicine from the drive thru at cvs and now resting at home. i've felt confident with the medical decisions made here.

review: my wife recommended me to dr. silva because i had an allergic reaction on my face using a over-the-counter product i bought at the store.  during this time of quarantine, i didn't want to rush off to the emergency room for obvious reasons (covid-19) dr. silva was more than helpful, and the staff was very proactive and quick to help me too.  they were very attentive and made me feel comfortable.  i am very satisfied because telemedicine was just one way dr. silva is able to communicate to patients.  i am grateful this service is available because it not only did it kept me safe from going to the emergency room (and save my time from the wait) it also kept my family safe during this time.

not sure what's going on here, but my son went for an evaluation. we waited over an hour for the social worker and then they realized they forgot to give us all the forms to fill out.  social worker was nice, seemed competent. he referred us  to the iop. we show up for his first session and find out we were given the "old" information and the times were incorrect. made it in for the next one ok. then came back for family night only to be informed it was going to be patients only due to covid-19. that's fine, but we took off work to be there and would have appreciated a heads up. then they switched to telemedicine. ok, no problem with that. first one went fine. second one he didn't get the meeting code. we tried calling, emailing and couldn't get anyone to help him. after three calls and my son emailing he finally got the code an hour into the session. not impressed , especially for a place helping people with mental health needs. you'd think they would have their act together. hoping things improve from here on out.

i moved a few months back and was looking for a new ob to go to and decided to make a visit at the practice here. very shortly after my initial office visit, i found out that i was pregnant with my first child! i have been coming here for my regular prenatal visits since then and have had a pleasant experience each time. i've also had bloodwork done several times and found that the lab's check in process is quick and efficient and i've never had to wait more than 5 minutes or so before my name is called, even when i don't have an appointment and i go in the middle of the day. 

my husband has also transferred his own medical care to this facility and has had no complaints with the quality of service received. utilizing my health online makes it really easy for us to receive test results and send messages to our care team whenever we need. this is especially handy with the current covid19 situation and all regular visits being changed to virtual visits. 

the only department that could use some sprucing up is the cafeteria. my husband recently had a treatment that required me waiting around for several hours for him to finish so i could drive him home. i got hungry midway through and went to the cafeteria to grab a bite to eat. i decided to get a breakfast burrito from their cafe. the burrito comes cold and you have to heat it up yourself in the one microwave they have in the entire cafeteria. i felt bad using the microwave when there was a line of nurses behind me waiting to heat up their own lunch. the burrito itself turned out to be abysmal and barely edible. for someone who is not a picky eater, this is saying something. 

other than the food though, everything about this hospital has been great so far!

i am thoroughly impressed!

this morning, i had a video chat with exer's receptionist and was then transferred to a doctor within 2 minutes. i discussed getting a covid-19 antibody test and the doctor set up the appointment. 

upon arriving at the facility, i was greeted at the door and whisked directly into the exam room. my blood was immediately taken and i was amazed to know i was finished 3 minutes after my arrival. i left literally five minutes after arriving. 

every step in the process was amazing! the receptionist, ivanna, was friendly with a great smile. she was happy to answer all of my questions and was super professional. when she passed me on to the doctor, he was also kind and friendly. the nurse at the facility was also super professional and informative. 

definitely looking to exer for all of my future urgent care needs. i'm so impressed!

i will start off by saying i was very nervous when i booked my appointment at early options because i've had a horrible experience in the past. after my video chat with dr. fleischman i felt more at ease just seeing how pleasant she was  that relaxed me and made me feel comfortable. the office was neat and tidy i felt safe especially during a time like this with the world dealing with covid 19. the procedure was very quick a few seconds of pain i won't say it didn't hurt because it was a bit uncomfortable but nothing i couldn't handle the idea of being awake during a procedure like this is scary for any woman. but i didn't feel alone she talked me through every step and let me know when i would feel a bit of pressure then it was over i felt cramping for about 15 minutes then i was surprised when they began to ease and i was able to go home and continue my day with 2 busy children. i would recommend early options to any woman it's private safe and the support you get helps you understand your not alone and you do have options
