cannot recommend this class or lisa enough. i searched for hours for a comprehensive birth+newborn virtual class and so happy with my decision. what i loved about this course is i was guaranteed to get lisa as the instructor, who is knowledgeable, funny, warm, flexible and empowering (whereas with other courses, there's not always a guarantee who will be teaching you).

review:
my husband and i took lisa's class virtually, due to the covid19 citywide shutdown. i was initially skeptical when the class was converted to virtual. i've been taking other classes (yoga, etc) from providers moving offline to online, and the experience has been so-so. but lisa's course, both content and virtual delivery, really blew me away!

first, the content - lisa is clearly super knowledgeable about all things birth and newborn care. her course was chock full of useful information, as are the many supplemental materials and resources she provides. i went into the class feeling clueless and scared and came out feeling much more prepared! 

second, the delivery - as mentioned, i was really surprised by how smoothly the class went virtually. lisa set up a zoom, and i could clearly see her, her presentation slides and the other participants in the class. lisa herself was very articulate, has a great sense of humor, and honestly it was pretty fun and entertaining for my husband and i to participate in. the only thing we regret about the virtual experience is that we didn't get to try lisa's home-baked cookies!

i highly recommend lisa's class, including the virtual experience!

review: during a time of crisis with covid 19, my husband and i went through drastic changes in our lives just as i was about to begin my third trimester. at the same time, lisa taylor made the switch for our birth class to zoom, and her ability to facilitate personal relationships with the group alongside top tier education was a bright light through a trying time. despite stress from the world situation, lisa's constant presence and birth class was an uplifting and expansive experience that we looked forward to every wed & thursday night. the class absolutely helped us prepare for labor, but even more, was a steady guiding light through pregnancy and the covid crisis. i know the knowledge my husband and i learned will be with us throughout our entire experience giving birth to our first child. i also truly admire lisa as woman whose passion infuses her skill and expertise - a true heartfelt, master teacher!

review: i was in a car accident late january and began attending physical therapy for my lower back when the covid-19 pandemic/quarantine began to take over everything. despite the many challenges cvpt has had to overcome they have definitely stayed focused on providing good patient care. i love the staff and really enjoy my sessions. i recently started doing telehealth and i have to say it's amazing! love that i can do it in the comfort of my own home and still interact with staff. i'm making steady progress thanks to cvpts commitment to helping me get better....even in the middle of a pandemic! thanks so much guys! i really appreciate you!!!

jana's class was incredible. there were so many unknowns going into pregnancy etc, and this class was recommended by a friend. it saved us! answered all the questions, scenarios, fears, etc that had been on our mind. jana has so much experience, and i had complete confidence in her. the information put me at ease, and let us know that we are not alone as new parents to be! feeling as prepped as one can for birth! the odd thing that happened to us, was the stay at home order issued for covid-19 in the 3rd week of class. she transitioned us all to zoom and it was incredible. we were able to pick up right where we left off, interact with her and the other couples, watch all of the films, have discussions, etc. she was able to adapt on the fly and we are so grateful! my sister in law is pregnant and i can't wait for her to take it and learn all that we did- so so so helpful and so grateful for all of this!

dr. daneshvar is my favorite gynecologist that i have ever been to. her bedside manner is warm and she makes you feel comfortable. she take the time to listen and explain.

during there covid-19 outbreak i needed medical attention: she was available by video chat the same day and she made me feel so well taken care of! i wanted a follow up call on a friday, and i was scared about what to do if my symptoms worsened over the weekend. she called me back within an hour, didn't charge for a visit, and assured me if i needed her over the weekend she was there for me. never have i felt such compassion and willingness to be available from a doctor. she told me not to worry. a huge load of stress was lifted from me and this  made all the difference in my successful recovery.

dr. daneshvar really stepped up to the plate for her patients during a stressful time of the coronavirus. i have much respect her!

meanwhile my family doctor left me out at pasture. will be writing a terrible review for him. these difficult times show you a person's true character.

thank you dr. daneshvar!

during covid-19, right after the travel ban, i was on quarantine for 14 days since i arrived from europe on vacation.  during that time, i fell ill and after a few days under virtual care, my doctor advised me to go to the er.  i chose memorial hermann sugar land thinking i would get good care.  i was totally wrong.

once in the er, which was set up efficiently because of the virus, the er doctor immediately explained to me that they will not send my covid-19 test off to be tested unless i was admitted to the hospital.  his main concern was not diagnosing my problem but explaining that i would have to go somewhere else to get tested for covid-19.

i was advised to go the the er by my doctor because i was coughing excessively, barely able to breath, experiencing pain in my back when breathing and coughing, wheezing and extreme shortness of breath even with using an inhaler.  my temp stayed below 100.4 so it wasn't considered a fever.

the er began to run tests:  chest x-rays, ct scan, urine-analysis, blood-work, i.v., etc.

i waited about 45 minutes for all the test results to return and during that time, i suffered and tried to breath over and over in spite of the difficulties i was experiencing.  finally, the er doctor returned (dr. b. parker) and said that my lungs were clear and that the covid-19 swab would not be sent to the lab because i'm not being admitted to the hospital.  i stated that i understood about the swab but i didn't understand what was going on with my breathing so i asked him again about my lungs.  dr. parker repeated that my lungs were "all clear" and that there was no sign of the virus in my lungs. 

i asked the doctor what was he diagnosing me as having. since we know there's no sign of covid-19 in my lungs, what is it then and what was he going to give me to help me breath.   dr. parker turned the paper around and it read, "cough - adult".  i asked, "so you're diagnosing me as having a cough?"  he replied yes.  i was dumbfounded.  i came to the er with a cough and shortness of breath and now the dr. was telling me that i had a cough.  wow!  

i asked him what was he going to do about helping me?  he stated that he was calling in prescriptions to my pharmacy to take but to act like i had covid-10 and still isolate.  he stated that he believed it was just an allergy infection and that these meds would clear it up.  i informed him that i don't typically suffer with allergies and that i had been taking zyrtec because the virtual doctor i spoke to recommended it but i wasn't getting any better.  he reemphasized again that the test would not be sent and that if i wanted a covid-19 test, i needed to go to another site.  i asked about an antibiotic to clear up the infection and he said the meds he prescribed would clear up the infection.  i later learned that the meds were regular over-the-counter stuff that i had already been using that wasn't effective:  tylenol, mucinex and claritin-d.

i believe dr. parker's only concern was covid-19 and not finding the real source of my problems.  i asked my discharge nurse again about my lungs being "all clear" and she said well they are not all clear and that they had a haze over them.  i asked what does a haze mean.  she informed me that the doctor believes the haze is possibly from a bacteria infection from allergies so he's prescribed some meds to help.  i again said i don't suffer with allergies but ok the pollen is high so i guess.  

i was discharged and walked to my car still struggling to breath just the same way as i walked into the hospital.   

that was saturday, march 21st. fast forward to wednesday, march 25th and i was not feeling any better, in fact, i felt worse. i called my doctor both the 25th and 26th and left messages. her nurse called my back on the 27th and informed me to stop taking all allergy meds immediately and that she had reviewed the labs and x-rays and they believe that haze over my right lung is pneumonia.

pneumonia?!!  so i had pneumonia in the right lung for an additional 6 days without any treatment?!  why would dr. parker say i was "all clear" and ignore the haze?  i had to take additional time from work to heal whereas if dr. parker would have just taken the time to explore my results for something more than covid-19, he could have treated me correctly and i could have returned back to work without taking additional time.  

lastly, once i got the bill, i saw that i was billed $273.50 for a pregnancy test!!!  the admitting nurse asked if there was anyway i could be pregnant, i immediately answered no and explained why i couldn't be.  so why would you give me, a 49 yr old woman with a valid reason a pregnancy test?  especially for $273.50.  over billing???   yes!

i will never go back to memorial hermann sugar land emergency room.  the care of the treating physician was below sub-par and i could have saved way more time and money going to another facility.

the clinic is taking every precaution between patients. they even wipe down the entrance handles (just saw them). all staff are masked up and they ask customers to mask up, too. dr. norcom is as kind and patient as ever.  so happy to get my botox for the unrelenting back-to-back zoom meetings i'm in for work. be sure to pre-book so you can save a little extra cash.

highly recommend!

during the coronavirus quarantine, i was outside the united states. i developed a potentially serious condition and wanted a second opinion from an expert us-based clinician who was open to telemedicine. i found dr. rapoport via an interview on allaboutvision.com and i'm so glad that i did.

the north star centre has been an incredible support system during this crazy time for me. their staff is always so welcoming, professional and dedicated - i would recommend to anyone looking into therapy. i think their professionalism is proven even further given their immediate response to covid-19 with their whole staff offering telehealth sessions to any and all patients. feeling very grateful for the north star centre and their services.

this lady can save lives.... erica rescued me and my monster baby during delivery... and get this...all by phone! (i didn't have a doula and called her at 4am...sorry erica). i was amazed at what she could do without even having to be present. makes me think about how all these mamas who need to go virtual during covid-19 pandemic with their doulas are going to be just fine and erica can do a lot in emergent situations where a baby is in danger even if she isn't physically there. i didn't even get a video of her so if i got to zoom with her, it would have been even more epic! knowing this now...i would pay her $4000 just for one video call if she were my doula during all this. i called her in an emergency, even though i didn't have a contract with her or any doula. she was a sweet heart and helped me at 4am in the morning! and guided me through labor to get my baby out when the doctors were trying to force me into c-section (and i was being extremely stubborn saying no to docs) becuase my baby was big and was stuck, and not coming. without her, my son would either not be here right now, or i would have been rushed into emergency c section. 

the nurse said i could try one more time before making me go into labor (telling me there was absolutely no way the baby could get out) but 5 minutes  on the phone with erica, and her guiding  me and the  nurse what to do... becuase the nurses didn't know about the positions she was telling me about and that baby slid out immediately!!!! it was some lateral, side laying yoga ball  roll thing...so literally they started screaming for the doctor to  come back because the baby started coming- and i pushed for just 10 minutes and birthed a 10 1/2 pound monster baby). the doctor came back in the morning 
and told me she admitted she was mad at herself becuase she was wrong about this baby, after 40 years of delivering....and said i have an absolutely amazing doula. and she didn't even charge me a dime for any of that.... she's the most selfless person i know. i do not recommending anyone do this to her, call her without a contract at 4am, but just shows she really cares so much. she was following up with me as well after the baby was born for weeks. 
this lady rocks!  even by phone! these doulas work so hard and earn every penny (in fact they barely make much for all the hours they work) and do way more than just have to come to the hospital... they can't go on vacation and have to put their whole lives on-call for us mamas to be ready at any moment. let's keep the doula's out of the hospitals, right now and let's pay them even more now than ever during the pandemic.

oc physical therapy is great -  would highly recommend to anyone who needs help.  victor is incredibly knowledgeable , and you can have confidence in the entire staff.  once covid happened i started doing zooms with victor , works really well !  so if you are locked in and need some help -  u don't have to wait -  just set up a video session and you will be on your way to feeling better.

i am so grateful for kristina's help with breastfeeding!!  i wish i could leave more than 5 stars.  i utilized her teletherapy for a virtual lactation consult and couldn't be happier.  my son was having issues with latching and feeding initially, and she set up a zoom virtual consult to provide lactation support (which was especially helpful since we were quarantined at home with a newborn in the setting of covid-19 and unable to access in person lactation services).  we were struggling through every feed prior to the consult, and our baby was losing too much weight despite our very best efforts.  she gave new, individualized, and unique tips/techniques to try, which all worked!  he latched and fed perfectly during our consult and with every subsequent feed!!!  i appreciated that she provided real-time personalized advice and tips during the consult.  she is clearly extremely knowledgable about lactation and genuinely cares about her clients!  she is a miracle worker, and i (as well as my now happy and chunky 5-week-old son) could not recommend her more!

review:
i've had aud (alcohol use disorder) for about 40 years. i've tried everything: hypnosis, acupuncture, years on antabuse, 6 months and then 7 years sober in aa in 2000s. each relapse turned into a several weeks long binge, forcing me to seek help again. finally, in 2014 i discovered sinclair method (https://www.the-sinclair-method.com/), which turned out to be a lifesaver. my drinking quickly went down to safe limits and i started to have alcohol free days several times a week. for 5.5 years i was a social drinker, a "normie" in aa speak - until covid struck. 

i live alone, the lockdown made me seriously depressed. all my routines and nearly all social contacts were broken and it felt like a solitary confinement. at some point in april, i stopped taking my medication as prescribed by the sinclair method. from there, my drinking quickly escalated and turned into a heavy 6 weeks binge. by may 13 i had to go to er and then to a 10 days detox in holister; spent the first night in icu nearly having a heart attack. after i got back home on sunday may 24, i wanted to make sure that sinclaire is still working (i still had some meds left from my last refill); i had 3 drinks on the first day, then it went 1, 1, 0, 1, 0 - amazing, considering my condition before the detox. 

in the meantime, my gf discovered the intensive outpatient program (iop) at good sam behavioral. i was surprised to learn that dr cecil a. bradley, who prescribed me naltrexone all these years, is the medical director of this program. the program seemed very useful since a) it is in person, no zoom, b) i got a double diagnosis and could address my underlying emotional issues and c) i could get an extended medical leave, since i was not feeling up to getting back to work immediately. on thursday, may 28 i was there and talked to marcella (admissions) dr khan (sp? md), nurse diane and some other people. i was very open about what i've been doing before, what brought me there and about my intentions (go back on sinclaire, since it works great and aa stopped working for me at some point). everybody seemed to be open-minded, accepting and approving of my course of treatment. some even wrote down the name of my method and said they were curious and want to learn more about it.

thursday and friday sessions were pretty nice, with meditation, some cbt and open discussions on topics suggested by patients themselves. and then, on friday noon dr bradley showed up, took me to his office and told me that their program is based on full abstinence and if i keep up the  controlled drinking, i have to leave. he said there are alternatives to aa and suggested some other program - he just could remember it's name. he is in his 80s and seems to forget things. i promised to think about it over the weekend and tell him about my decision on monday. after all, at this point i could easily refrain from drinking for the duration of the program.

however, on monday my case manager handed me a recovery plan with mandatory conditions: attend at least 3 meetings a week, find a sponsor and report progress at each morning session. i told her i don't do aa, and i was told to go talk to dr bradley, and again he gave me a dilemma: full abstinence and meetings or leave the program. "there is this other program - can't remember it's name... rational recovery?" "- smart recovery?" "- yes, this must be it". "- i researched it, and it has about the same success rate as aa - which is in single digits - whereas sinclair method has success rate near 80%". "- i don't care. this program requires full abstinence and meetings". so i informed him that i'm quitting and went home.

there are several things that really upset and anger me. 
1) why did dr bradley prescribe my medicine all these years and even wrote me another 3 refills on that monday if he disapproves on sinclair method so much? 
2) how does a doctor refer a patient to some program the name of which he can't even remember? does he know anything about it? or he just doesn't care?
3) why did they admit me at all, knowing full well my intentions, knowing dr bradley's views and giving me false hopes? 
4) what kind of doctors put a patient into completely unscientific, faith-based programs with abysmal success rate and force him to abandon something that is proven to work for 80% and this patient in particular?

so i googled dr bradley and discovered that the medical board of california twice has suspended his license, once in 1990 and second time in 2007 (5 years probation). he also was known to be sending referrals to and working at a couple of shady rehabs ran by an uncertified drug addict.

makes you wonder, how does a doctor like cecil bradley ends up a medical director at well-respected hospital like good sam? i would not recommend going to good sam in- or outpatient behavioral programs until they replace him. the rest of staff seems to be ok, but there is nothing they could do to help me under current leadership.

review:
an adult relative of mine has had an excellent experience with myofunctional therapy (mft) here.  the problems isabel treated with mft were tongue tie, snoring, obstructive sleep apnea, and chronic neck and shoulder tightness/discomfort.  

momentum therapy center isn't just for kids!  excellent for adults too.

isabel has been very thorough.  the initial evaluation was in person, as well as some of the weekly follow-up visits.  once the coronavirus pandemic started our local stay-at-home orders, isabel did virtual visits, which were also excellent.

within weeks of starting myofunctional therapy here, there was marked improvement in symptoms.  eventually, the neck tightness/discomfort was 100% better, and the shoulder/trapezius area issues were 70-80% better.  snoring was also improved.

visits were in network with insurance, so that's another plus.

overall, highly recommended!

the staff have been very helpful with allowing me to teach out to my mother via zoom curing the covid lockdown.  at least my mother gets an opportunity for us to see each other and maintain social distancing.

review: my doctor referred me to a pelvic floor physical therapist, but after not being able to get an appointment (covid-19 quarantine), i made an appointment with dr. dominick. we just had our first virtual visit (on a hipaa compliant platform, thank you!) and i'm extremely impressed! i am almost three months postpartum and had several issues to discuss. she took plenty of time to listen to each of my concerns and give feedback about what is likely going on, along with giving me suggestions for how to begin addressing each one. she did demonstrations and watched me try exercises as well, to be sure i am on the right track. in addition, she sent me an email with the exercises right after our visit so that i have something to reference. i am looking forward to continuing my healing and i appreciate her support along the way. if you're looking for a knowledgeable and caring provider that truly takes the time to address your needs, look no further!

you need some debra in your life!! i was referred to debra by a friend after she found out i was struggling with breastfeeding issues with my newborn baby. in a nutshell, debra is awesome. i only wish i would have met her earlier to partner with her before bringing my baby home and to have been able to prepare for a rough breastfeeding journey. debra is very knowledgeable, down to earth and more importantly supportive of what works best for baby + mom. she was super accessible via text and email. given the current covid situation we had to do our session virtually rather than in person, but it will still effective and totally helpful. debra provided me with guidance on how to build my milk supply - after a few days my supply did go up. she's continuing to provide support to new moms via weekly zoom meetings and i am soo grateful for them. it takes a village! and in this lockdown environment, support is crucial and debra is more than willing to help. call debra if you need help with lactation, feeding, newborn needs!! you will be grateful you did

i found this practice on zocdoc & i booked due to the good reviews. what a mistake! this place is terrible- disorganized, changing appointment times & not calling to inform you of the change. and every time you schedule an appointment, you get a different provider, even if you schedule your appointment with a specific provider. there is no continuity of care. most recently i had a coloscopy & i had an appt scheduled to discuss the results. it has been difficult to get in to the office with the current pandemic. i cancelled my appointment, but the doctor called and left a message with the results. i didn't speak the doctor at all. and i was billed for a virtual visit!! i contacted the office twice & was told they would take care of it. well, as of today, i'm still getting bills sent to my email. if i could give negative zero stars i would. stay away!!

all in all, if you want in depth care you go to the hospital. this is a work place medical facility and they do a good job achieving that directive. the doctor i've seen there on all my visits is nice as is his staff.

long and lengthy but honest review:


results at week 1: 
today marks one week that i got prk eye corrective surgery and i am in the office for my first vision check with dr. law. she is amazing, kind and extremely knowledgeable. i asked her several questions and she was able to give me exact and detailed responses without me feeling rushed in any way. she preformed my eye exams twice. before removing my contacts and again after they were removed. my appointment lasted about 20 minutes and was over before it was even scheduled to start!(since i was early) i learned that my vision is at a (blurry) 20/25 and i was also cleared to drive. that's amazing improvement and i'm very pleased with my results thus far! 

for those worried about getting surgery during a pandemic: (because i was too) 
the office does a great job with cleanliness. there are very few patients in the waiting room at the same time, everyone sits at least one seat apart and they take your temperature as soon as you walk in! they are only allowing patients in the office and any family is asked to wait outside. they offer seating and the downstairs lobby also has a seating area if you wish to wait. (i live very close and always just got dropped off and picked up.) they also have lysol and hand sanitizer everywhere and definitely keep all areas very clean. everyone wears a face mask at all times and all fully cover their mouth and nose. covid-19 doesn't stand a chance! 

about the staff:
i've got to admit, i was very nervous about this surgery and still do not have crystal clear vision but the staff here is just amazing. they are so kind comforting, and welcoming. the doctor that preformed my prk surgery was dr. january and he is just amazing. the staff morale is above par, and it's clear that everyone not only loves their job here but they also love each other! i loved seeing them interact with one another in such a friendly yet professional manner. 

communication with the doctor is super important:
first day i met dr. january he gave me his personal cell phone number & he actually answers very promptly! i sent him texts with questions before surgery and i always got very prompt and detailed replies that made me feel more comfortable and always fully answered my question. after surgery my mom called him on a different phone number, on a sunday morning, and he answered right away. that definitely won over my moms heart and comforted her a lot(and she's never met him).  just goes to say this doctor really cares and is here for all of his patients, and i've never seen this down at such a high level before. there is no lack in communication at this office which is 10/10 in my book. 

about prk:
(i'm not a dr this is my general knowlage) 
prk is different from lasik in that there is no "flap" being made on the cornea. instead, the top layer is painlessly brushed off before being treated by the laser and then they put a prescription-less contact lens in your eye. this is less invasive than lasik but does have a greater and more painful recovery time. (pain only lasts about 2-3 days) there are other pros & cons & i recommend researching it, or asking your doctor about the differences. 

my statistics:
my left eye was at -3.5 and right was at -4.0 with astigmatism. i'm 23 years old, am a masters of accounting student and i am taking an online class through out all of this. (and live & home) 

my personal experience: 
(everyone's eyes are different & your experience could differ from mine!)

day 1 i didn't feel much pain and even managed to finish up a little discussion for school before sleeping the rest of the day. (don't recommend using a computer that early on but i didn't have a choice) my most painful days were days 2(night) till day 4 (morning) & i slept a majority of the day though days 1-4. (if i wasn't sleeping i stayed in a dark room and would ice my eyes & listen to music or funny podcasts) the xanax they gave me honestly didn't work and i had to resort to taking other medications that did give me great relief! the "pain" for me was a constant burning feeling and was more bothersome and annoying than "painful". but once it's gone, it's gone. by day 5-6 i would get headaches from straining to see because of my blurry vision but it's normal and extra strength tylenol helps a lot!! 
i recommend taking 5-7 days off of work/ school for less stress and so you can give your eyes the best ability to heal (my personal opinion) but by day 5 i was already comfortably looking at my zoomed in computer screen. i have not experienced any dry eye issues yet, and am very good at keeping up with my drops.

i was referred to dr. armin by my health care clinic in west hollywood. i'm used to going to cedars for my back and spine consultations, but i decided to give dr armin in a try. i've read some of the other reviews posted here and they are completely contrary to the experience that i had with the doctors staff. nancy, at dr. armin's office, was as kind, hospitable and responsive as i could ask for. she responded to phone calls and particularly emails with shockingly fast precision. 

in fact, nancy responded to emails both on the weekend and after hours. this is something i have never encountered with any doctors office or medical service provider. ever. she stayed in constant contact with me about getting me in to see the doctor, this time because of covid-19 via a telemedicine call. 

my first appointment with dr armin was thorough in that he asked a wide range of questions regarding my previous spinal health, going back almost 30 years. based on the information i gave him about my recent injury, he scheduled an mri which, being in a considerable amount of pain, happened within one week. after we received the mri results, nancy was quick to schedule a follow-up appointment for dr armin to review the mri with me. 

i have had spinal surgery, and have had chronic back issues for the best part of my life. i'm an active person and re-injure my back about once a year. this time was different, extraordinarily painful. the doctor reviewed the mri with me in a way that was completely and utterly thorough. we discussed each vertebrae and each disc. he reviewed the health of each vertebrae and each disc with me in detail that was almost exhausting, but it was extraordinary. he gave me a very clear and concise picture of the health of my spine, and gave me advice on how to proceed forward that was very clear. the medicine he prescribed when i first injured my back, and the follow-up appointment to review my mri seem to be completely on point. i am able to function with much less pain and for now, he said that he recommends i avoid any surgery. he recommended a wide variety of preventative procedures and that i stay away from my very favorite activity, doing sit-ups! 

his friendliness, kindness and seemingly genuine concern for the state of my health was quite refreshing. i did not feel like just another patient, or like a faceless person sitting in a waiting room waiting for 5 minutes with a doctor that rushes through his examination. i felt a genuine concern from him for the state of my health and the health of my spine.

i'm not usually moved to write reviews like this, especially one this long. but in the world of overbooked, over taxed, underpaid people, this doctor showed up for me as did his assistant nancy. that is rare and it's deeply appreciated!

i am a physician who also has a family member at this facility and i am appalled by the way they have handled the care of my aunt in her dying days. i am very disappointed at poor care and lack of compassion and empathy by the staff at this facility. interestingly, my aunt was thriving when my family was allowed to visit daily and feed and clean her on their own.. now i understand that there is a global pandemic but this only leads me to believe that the care she was getting subsequently was sub par if the family wasn't there to suggest that the staff actually do their job. 
as my beloved family member has now reached her final hours, we are not even allowed to say our final goodbyes, through video calling for that matter. 
unfortunately, this is how we will remember the end of my aunt's life and the struggle we had to go through just to say goodbye. all thanks to lieberman nursing home... very unfortunate!!
as a physician, i have also been video conferencing with my own patients in other nursing homes and find it rather questionable that you don't allow family members to video conference their loved ones in your facility. 
i hope that this facility can change their tune before it is too late.

i'd like to take a moment to simply offer my feedback on this facility. my situation is different given that i've not been able to visit my brother as the hospital is taking great measures to protect the patients from covid-19 which in my opinion is commendable. what the staff has done, is accommodate me with video conferences which have helped eased my families anxiety.

the staff is excellent in that they provide me with absolute detail regarding care, medication administered, and overall treatment. i am fortunate in that both the patient advocate and social worker are the epitome of top notch professionals. they are effective in their communication, and quite reliable in their service to others.

my brother has gone through extensive medical treatment which i won't disclose, but i will say that since being at kindred, he's alert, and getting stronger each day. the medical team there doesn't give up easily, and for that i am pleased.

a special thanks to keisha silva who goes above and beyond to ensure that i remain in contact with my brother, and she lets me know when i need to motivate my brother to play a role in his recovery. 

needless to say, i am pleased with our selection of kindred ladera. we looked at other facilities, and they don't compare to the excellence provided at this facility. 

i'd rank them a 10 all day long.

been going to dr joe for 4 years or so.  we needed a prescription refilled and called to do telehealth.  they informed us that they don't do it and we had to come in.  our son has asthma and we want to avoid taking him to public places with the current pandemic. luckily my brother is a dr. and called in the prescription for us.  when dr. joe found out he had his assistant call us to tell us that he would no longer be our pediatrician.  good.  i'm glad i know his true self now and we can find a better pediatrician.

i had a video consult with dr savur this morning for a colonoscopy via zoom video.  she was outstanding. given a previous horrible experience with a different doctor 12 years ago i swore i would never ever have a colonoscopy again. 

since then my brother had colon cancer discovered at his first colonoscopy at the age of 50. so i have rethought my reluctance to have another one. my md referred me to dr savur. 

dr savur spent over 30 minutes with me this morning. i was a sweaty nervous wreck just making the call. she really calmed me down and explained everything given my previous experience and my overall medical issues. 

just waiting now for covid 19 to subside in society so i can make an appointment for the procedure.

been with this group for many years now.  very responsive to all of my calls and inquiries.  a busy office at times, they try their best with seeing appointment on time but never cut the visits short and attentively listens to concerns.  during covid-19, they have virtual visits which are extremely helpful.  when needing documents, the office has been seamless in their response.  most of all, i trust the practitioners as they explain why they come to their decisions and welcome dialogue.  i am grateful for their services, both when i want to see them and when i need to see them.  dr. smith and dr. yee are standout practitioners, but i like them all.  i never wait to see our pcp when sick; they will all see you when required, and i appreciate that.

our "frontline workers"?! i did my homework and read all the reviews i could find that were published for dr. donald cassaday on different physician grading sites (healthgrades, vitals, etc.) they stated over and over that the office staff for this doctor was rude and unresponsive (just look at these reviews on yelp!), but i decided to take a chance when looking for a new pcp lately because dr. cassaday weren't too bad on other review sites. whoa! i'll relate what happened in my interactions with this office in the hope that you won't be subjected to the same kind of treatment i was. 

before calling, in an effort to make it easier for them to make an appointment for me, i sent in a fax which included my medical background and my current medications, even though all my records had already been transferred to their office. 

there was no response to my fax, so a couple of days later i called and left a detailed message with an "erica." there was no response to my first call, so after two days i called again and left another message with erica. this went on for over a week, with my leaving messages every one to two days, leaving a total of five detailed messages. no one ever answered the calls in person when i placed them despite calling only during office hours--i only got recordings each time. and no one returned my repeated calls. 

i finally got through to a "kim" and asked her if i could conduct my first visit with the doctor via video conference because i was afraid to come in due to covid-19 and the fact i was a senior and had chronic medical conditions. i was terrified of contacting the virus, but kim said that this was not their "protocol" and kept talking over me. she then told me to find another doctor and eventually actually hung up on me despite my being as polite as humanly possible considering her attitude.

i was so shocked at her behavior that i sent an overnight letter to dr. cassaday asking for some intervention. he never responded. when i called again a couple of days later, kim again told me dr. cassaday would not be seeing me and she hung up on me again.

i can't help but think about the hundreds of our other "frontline workers" and the dedication and care they have shown their patients during this very difficult time. it's too bad this office doesn't have even a fraction of their empathy or willingness to serve.

i had an appointment with this doctor yesterday through telemedicine. the appointment was at 9:20.  they wanted me to check into the portal at 9 am.  i did so and waited and waited and waited.  at 10:10 i got a call from a blocked number.  i almost didn't answer figuring it was a robocall. it was the doctor who blamed his staff for him being late and refused to take responsibility.  first strike.  who knows what happened with their supposed telemedicine.  it seems they don't know how to work the system.  he or any one of his staff could have checked in at any time to let me know there was a delay or a technical problem, but that didn't happen. beyond that i found him to be less than compassionate, low in skill, low in social skills and incredibly unhelpful.  if he were a front line worker working with covid19, i'd give him a pass. but he's in gastroenterology where its business as usual (aside from virtual visits).  save your money and time.  go elsewhere where patients are respected and the doctor has a level of skill and knowledge.  i've gotten far better and more in depth information from simple google searches.

their teleconference appointment was so convenient and easy to schedule. now with corona-mania i am so happy that i didn't have to go in to an office full of sick people. also, i didn't have to pay a babysitter to watch my kids so that i could go to the clinic. kim was able to address all my concerns via video chat and sent my prescriptions electronically to my local pharmacy.  the staff is super friendly and accommodating. it was an overall great experience.

dr presken has gone above and beyond during these difficult covid19 times. when aetna dropped my doctor right before the pandemic, and i couldn't find a doctor that would "establish care" until the pandemic is over, she accepted me, established care through video conference, with a detailed interview. in the past 6 weeks, i have gone through most likely covid 19 with an er visit for respiratory distress, a breast cancer scare & biopsy, a rash, and kidney stones. she has called me to discuss my test results each time, and has shown she truly cares for me as a patient. from our conversations i can tell she has been educating herself with the latest information about covid19, and strives to give patients the best care. thank you, dr. presken!

we also love the pediatric center! started coming here 6 years ago and just realized it has never occurred to me to look elsewhere. the doctors are each different personalities and i've seen them all. bottom line is very practical, accessible and consistent care. you can call and actually speak with your doctor the same day and they have walk in every day. with the coronavirus i guess that has changed but i see they are offering telemedicine now! i was just thinking about what my plan might be for my kids if they got sick and realized i can count on these doctors and owed them a 5 star review.

due to covid-19 they are only taking video chat calls. i was having an unusual eczema outbreak, so i was in need of an appointment asap!

my experience with their dermatology department

1. you have to call their main line to get transferred to their dermatology department (they don't have a direct number). 
2. i spent 22 minutes on the phone from the  first initial call to the end of the call to book an appointment.
3. thankfully, i was able to book an appointment for the following day with dr. iris ahronowitz. 
4. you then are encouraged to test their telecare services through their app with their technical service team. you can test it through the usc telecare app or a link by using chrome, i have an apple phone, so the app was the much better option. side note, it is great they have the option to test the link before your appointment (i highly recommend you to do this, i have a very good understanding of technology, but for some reason it wasn't compatible with safari, so the tech support rep helped me through it (the testing of the link and compatibility on my phone took about 13 minutes)
5. my appointment was at 10:00 a.m., so i checked in through their app a few minutes before the appointment and i waiting until about 10:15 a.m. (the wait time seems to be the same as with any doctor's office in-person) 
6. i was then sent a text message to join the call with dr. iris ahronowitz at 10:14 a.m. and i waited another couple minutes until she joined the call. 
7. dr. iris ahronowitz is a total gem, i felt understood and heard by her. some doctors out there make you feel like just a number, which i felt that way to a certain extent at their pain center in los angeles, in san pablo street. after experiencing a wonderful experience with her, i wouldn't want to go to any other dermatologist! 
8. i was then contacted by a customer rep from dr. iris ahronowitz's team to schedule a follow-up visit for three weeks down the road.

overall, the experience i had with their dermatology department and dr. iris ahronowitz was a very positive experience! i can't recommend dr. iris ahronowitz enough! not only is she a great doctor, but when you speak to her, you feel like you are talking to a friend, so the awkwardness you get with most doctors is not something you would experience with her. i have to say i was a bit skeptical booking a video call because i felt my needs wouldn't be fully taken care of through a video call, but to a degree it was. i just wished she could have fully evaluated my skin and face, but they are prioritizing appointments to those with more pressing patient concerns. she did reassure me that we could always book an in-person appointment once covid-19 dies down.
address: 125 W Huntington Dr Bldg A & B

review:
i am so glad my personal training hasn't stopped during the covid shutdown.  for the past year i've done two  1/2 hour sessions per week at fitness by design.  the gym is remarkably well-equipped, spacious and well-run.  the trainers are as good as any i've had at various gyms and better than most.  training sessions cost no more than other gyms, with no monthly fee.  
my trainer, adam shadwick, was always prepared with a new workout so that i got the most out of my training time.  he challenges and encourages me in just the right mix.  although i strive for aerobic and strength sessions on my own between training sessions, those so often get pushed aside.  so, when the covid shutdown started, i knew i needed to do something to keep on track.
zoom to the rescue.  i showed adam what equipment i had, yoga ball, stretch bands, and some dumbbells, etc, he immediately went to work creating routines with body weight exercises and my equipment.  i set up my laptop and a smart phone at different angles, log on to zoom, and he coaches and checks my form from his home to mine.  same challenge, same encouragement.  and just as importantly, the same accountability to a schedule to keep me on track.

i have been with dr. bernadette for more than 6 years and she is a total professional. i am very grateful i found her practice. she is understanding, straightforward and caring. i have referred a number of people to her throughout the years and will continue to do so. i love the telemedicine option that she has integrated in the past few years. it has made my life easier (even before covid).

i've been seeing dr. durrani at prosperity for about 6 months now, and he has been great. understanding, knowledgeable, very receptive to patient needs and his office staff has been incredibly helpful. during covid-19, of course appointments are via zoom, and i've always been able to get a quick appointment without having to wait weeks like at other offices. while the office is in va, far from where i am in maryland, it's always worth the trip, even before the zoom appts were in effect prior to covid-19. his office staff at prosperity are incredibly helpful and polite, which you don't find everywhere.
fac_name: Prosperity Eating Disorders and Wellness Center

review:
dr. lenoir is nothing less than a life saver.
and a mild mannered, low key one at that.
nothing flashy-just knows his stuff, and gets the job done pronto.
(he is a nationally known expert, but you have to look into him to find that out.....he won't hand you a 4 color marketing flyer....he's a doctor, not a saleman.)

i spent 3 long years seeking someone (anyone!) who could think out of the box regarding a 5 month bout i had with an upper respiratory illness in 2019....after having a 2 month bout in 2017, and a 3 month bout in 2016. never been sick before like this (ie: needing to see a doctor-i am the tough it out type), in all my 60+ years.

i did everything, multiple evaluation visits with others (all great doctors), chest x-rays, blood work, you name it. no results! no hope.

after giving up in 2019-my gp said.....go see this guy. he's an allergist, you likely have an allergy, (not-didn't fit the pattern at all).

see him i did.....no 3 month torture wait. i got in the following week.

in 10 minutes, on the phone (covid19 req'd telemedicine), he diagnosed what i had as was similar to what he had had, and had treated hundreds of cases of beginning in 2016. (ka-ching!)

2016 was the first year i was afflicted.

did he try to panel me for an allergy test as my gp advised (expensive and painful and slow)?

nope.

long story short: he proscribed what i had begged others for: an unconventional drug regimen, which....surprise surprise-he had developed to treat novel coronoviruses that had first appeared to his practice in the bay area in 2016.....because he (correctly as it happens), surmised that was what i may have experienced this year.

5 day 3 point holistic drug regimen. very creative.  day 1, i felt miles better.  day 5, illness be gone! pure magic.

day 8, 80% back to normal. on day 8, he proscribed a finish up regimen to go the last 20%.

no bs, no pleading, just competence from a doctor that knew what he was doing right out of the gate.

dr. lenoir is not interested in putting you thru the ringer. he listens, he responds with a solid what he knows. he does this at speed.

i had seen 8 doctors spread all over northern california.
i spent a total of three years and a gazillion$.
this doctor nailed it in 10 minutes.

10 minutes!
seriously.
i will never lose his number.

if you suffer from: prolonged dry cough, shortness of breath, and extreme fatigue after being sick with flu like symptoms (all covid19 markers)....don't wait for the cdc report in 2021 that explains why....just call this doctor's office and give him a whirl.

as far as i am concerned-dr. lenoir is a miracle worker.

i only wish i'd found him in 2016.

cristina helped me with my shin and ankle pain. i was never a runner, recently in the last 6 months, i started running a lot. like 2-3 miles a day. additionally in my cross-training hiit style gym whenever i use to run sprints, i would feel pain in my shins for days. i was getting better at my sprints every-time so was the pain. at one point i had to take a break for a few months not only from sprints but from running altogether. this was frustrating as i have worked really hard to get better at running overall. i discussed this with cristina, who is recommended by my other gym friends, as they got great results working with her. i did a session with cristina in the gym where she spent an hour understanding different aspects of walking, running style. we tried different exercises to fix the form for running and walking. she came up with a list of exercises that will help strengthen my shins, ankle, and help my glutes fire when running and doing the exercises. cristina is very patient, friendly, and extremely professional in understanding your pain points and will create an exercise plan tailored to your problem. i also did a follow-up session using telehealth(virtual-visit) because of covid-19 this session was as effective as in person. cristina is excellent in following-up and does a periodic check-in on how i was feeling and need any other adjustment in my exercise schedule. i would highly recommend her! i am feeling much better in my running. i did 44 miles in month of april and targeting, even more, this month.

as an update and in celebration of #thankyouthursday, i wanted to post an update for polestar.

i am a continuing member of this amazing pilates organization.  i do want to emphasize again in my follow up that the professionalism and instruction provided at this facility are amazing.  before this covid situation took place and before anyone took this serious, the management and instructors went the extra mile.  they started distancing in their instruction, and the cleaning went above and beyond anything that was happening at the time. 

when the time came to shut down, they did, with heavy hearts of all involved.  to top it off, they immediately began zoom classes for those that were interested.  for those that didn't want to participate, they paused their accounts.  

i am looking forward to returning as i fully miss my weekly classes.  being away make me appreciate this amazing facility so much more.  

again, thank you!  #thankyouthursday
fac_name: Polestar Physical Therapy and Pilates Center

review: during this covid season i thought i will not be able to train at all, but i am amazed how marta was able to train me through zoom and facetime. she was working out with me and yet she was able to see all small nuances and mini angles that she immediately corrected. my workout was fun and i felt that she gave me all attention as if she was with me in the room. my workout was as always precise to my abilities, she was able to work through my sore muscles and warm them to the point, that i felt all great! can't wait for our next training session! cannot recommend marta enough!!

when moving to a new city where you don't know how or what to do when it comes to new doctors. that can be a pretty scary thing to look for. 

when we came across this place we were so thankful. sarah lindsay is one of the best doctors in town. she cares so much about her clients. 

in fact even during the covid 19 pandemic was able to "see her clients" via zoom to figure out what was wrong with them. even if we can't go physically to the doctors office to get a check up we can do it via zoom. now that's amazing! 

this physician group is known to be one of the best hospitals in all of naples! 

when i went to see her she informed me that they are not only there for annual check ups but they also have a gynecologist there as well so you don't have to worry or stress about looking for a gyno as well as a doctor.

my wife and i had an appointment to go to allcare to get a covid-19 test. when it was time for my in-office appointment (recommended by my primary care doctor), we were told that the appointment had been converted to a tele-health appointment. they sent links to upload my insurance card and for the zoom appointment. neither worked. when we called the office to inquire about the problem, the receptionist told us she didn't know what to tell us. she further stated that she couldn't do anything for us. when i became frustrated and asked to speak to a manager, she put me on hold. when she came back to the phone, she asked in a condescending tone "ready to figure out what we can do?" given her tone and attitude toward us, my wife suggested that we take a picture of the card and email it. she again placed on us hold, presumably because my wife was similarly frustrated. at that point, i went inside and set my card on the desk. the receptionist refused to help me.

it's astounding that during a pandemic, a health care provider would not know how to develop reasonable options (e.g., taking a photo of the insurance card and emailing it) and what's worse exercise, refuse to communicate with a patient (i.e., placing me on hold) and refusing to get me a manager.

i will fully admit that i probably wasn't my best self. i went in without my mask (it broke in the car while waiting). the idea that someone - a health provider - would treat a patient this way and act petty - it's astonishing.

don't go there under any circumstances if you can help it. the worst!

i do not recommend honorhealth to anybody. please read my full review as this is serious stuff. first and foremost, they did not take me seriously. i have been having health issues for months but was told it was "just anxiety" despite bloodwork, reoccurring infections, physical symptoms like swelling in my abdomen and lymph nodes & more proving it is not anxiety, besides the only anxiety i currently have is over my health because i have no clue what is wrong with me and haven't for months (not the other way around). was told i needed to get on cymbalta - by my nurse practitioner, who met me about 4 times in my life, didn't ask me about my history at all, and as a note my previous therapist said i did not need medication - instead of doing further medical testing. (then continues to treat me like i'm just overly anxious while i am anxious about my health since i have had 4 months of hell and no answers!)

then at the honorhealth virginia g piper cancer care center, where i went for hematology after the hospital found i had low iron, they scheduled me for an iron iv just a week after i started iron supplements for anemia, telling me my iron supplements "weren't working" without re-testing my blood levels. well, thank god i ended up going to the hospital for dizziness and chest pain, and they tested my iron levels and found out my iron pills were indeed working, my hemoglobin was at a normal level again and that iron iv could have given me iron poisoning which can be deadly! i hate to sound dramatic but honestly why wouldn't they test instead of just assuming?! besides it was a $4,000 procedure i was going to pay up front for, makes me wonder what their intentions actually were.

then there was the time i made an appointment for my husband to see a doctor at honorhealth for bloodwork he needed after his emergency surgery, his appointment was at 11:30am, we arrived at 11:20 and the woman at the reception desk (downstairs in suite 100, i want that clear as the ladies upstairs are very sweet) were extremely rude to him, saying his appointment was at 11:15 even though i had mychart pulled up that clearly said 11:30 as did the text and email confirmations for the appointment. she said because we didn't get there 15 mins early he didn't get to see the doctor. i have never had that experience and all of his paperwork was filled out already so what the hell was the point of that? she just took the most rude and inconsiderate attitude with him and was looking at him and talking to him like he was beneath her. i did not appreciate that at all and we walked out and i found him a new doctor. i should never have gone back after that but i did and i regret it. 

it's almost impossible to get through to the office to speak with your doctor about test results etc. i had an telemedicine appointment 2 weeks ago to ask for a referral as i had been to the honorhealth urgent care for swelling and pain in my lower abdomen/pelvis and they said i needed a ct scan. they called me the morning before my appointment and said it was canceled because they were only doing telemedicine. it was a telemedicine appointment. i couldn't get through. i ended up reaching out to the head manager who was very sweet and put me through the to someone who transferred me over to alexis, my doctor's assistant, who was extremely rude to me and was actually trying to argue with me over why i went to urgent care, saying i didn't go for swelling. like are you serious?! the doctor felt where i was swollen and said i needed a ct scan asap. not to mention all of the issues with scheduling with radiology we ran into because she gave me false information. 

i ended up getting a new doctor, but was going to go for my ultrasound anyway, but thankfully i looked at honorhealth's website before i went and found out they do coronavirus testing at thur facilities! that is great but no one informed me of that. i don't know where they do it and the urgent care and radiology at del lago share a waiting room so i just didn't go to my appointment. 

i will never come back here and i don't recommend it to anyone.

review: i am so happy i was introduced to dr. lorena lee. i have been suffering with tmj pain and due to the covid epidemic she was not seeing patients in her clinic but is offering video consults. the video consult that she gave me was beyond what i expected. she was able to give me such clear instructions on how to relieve pain and release tension through pressure points and massages. i am so grateful for her ability to find ways to still help people in these times of social distancing. dr. lorena was able to do so much for me simply by talking to me via zoom, i will be coming in to get acupuncture from here as soon as she begins seeing clients again!

moti has helped me overcome a long-term, painful hip injury. i can't say enough good things about them and their facility, and in particular fei, the therapist i've worked with for the last several months.

first, their location is convenient and walkable to most people in los feliz. if you need to drive, they have free parking. 

they run on-time and have never kept me waiting. in general, the staff is helpful and respectful. moti feels different than most of los angeles's medical offices.

their facilities are clean and hygienic. 

fei is a gem. she's determined and patient. she listens carefully so she can problem solve. she's evolved my treatment over months as i progress, neither making me go too slowly or too quickly. during the quarantine, we worked together safely over zoom. her attention never waived. 

fei and moti have legitimately changed my life for the better and allowed me to live pain-free again. there's no better review i can give than that.

oakton's jackson clinics staff members and their excellent patient treatment are second to none.  and how they are handling telemedicine during the covid-19 pandemic is a great example of how patients matter in their organization. first, the basics.  the front office staff is cordial, efficient, and make the process easy!  as for the level of care, i have seen orthopedists who have looked at my films more than they ever looked at my broken ankle. you won't be treated like that at jackson clinics. the pts get to know you and how your body works and they will tailor the very best pt time and exercise program to help you overcome your issue.  you spend a long time with the pts who really take the time and who are absolute experts in physiology and therapeutics. the exercise specialists also will demonstrate how to properly do the exercises that will increase your range of motion and lessen pain.  they give handouts as well and will help you as you learn these movements.  that has been true for me with my ankle recuperation and also when i was patient because of shoulder pain from a car accident.  you can trust the oakton group. i am finally writing today however because of telemedicine and how dr. chelsea mcnally has been so creative in my care. i didn't know if telemedicine would work for pt, but chelsea quickly changed my mind. she watches me as i exercise and she can give me a lot of feedback. i have had 2 telemedicine appointments so far and i can say that it has been such a relief to know that i won't lose my progress because chelsea and ashley (the clinic's exercise specialist) and everyone at jackson clinics in oakton are so talented and caring that they make it work. kudos to everyone at jackson clinics oakton for making this available and for professionalism and medical excellence ... even in times like this. believe me...you won't be disappointed with telemedicine or their regular in-office appointments, and you will definitely feel better and stronger soon!  they really are the smartest, most compassionate, most knowledgeable care givers i know.

i'm very disappointed in their handling of patients during this covid-19 crisis. my daughter had been see the dr. for a few months now prior to stay at home orders and while stay home orders in place she got a rash that eadnt going away. when i called for a telehealth visit, they wanted money upfront (even though i had no copay or other out of pocket through insurance). additionally, they wanted me to pay a telehealth vendor fee that i would not get refunded for. of course they said i could still go into the office, by i dont feel comfortable with that during these times. apparently this office is all about money and not care of patients. very unfortunate. we found another dermatologist telehealth visit that was able to see us, no cost upfront.

first of all, they changed my son's doctor without telling us so when his next appointment came up which was during this pandemic, i called to see if they are seeing patients and i told them his doctors name and they laughed and said she is not here anymore and gave me the new doctor's name.

second of all, they scheduled a telehealth appt. and were supposed to call between a certain time which i did not receive, then i thought oh maybe i am supposed to call them at that time, so i called them and they said oh no someone will call you at that time, i did not hear my phone ring but later checked and had a voicemail from them saying they would call within the next hour, but no one called.

tl;dr: doctors and therapist fine, very strict 72-business hour cancellation fee of at least $80 ($170 for initial intake) for any reason.

i have really bad luck with psychiatrists. one retired, one basically had a nervous breakdown and moved across the country, and one was murdered.

 i decided to go to hp because at the time they had a few psychiatrists/nps so i felt like i wouldn't have to move practices if one of them decided to quit snd join a cult or something. so far i've seen the same doctor and she's been very consistent so all good there  

my issue is that they have an incredibly strict cancellation policy. 72 business hours. that means you might need to cancel over a week ahead of time if there's a holiday weekend. last year i had a nasty flu and tried to cancel 24 hours ahead of time. they said that wasn't a good enough reason to cancel and they would still charge me if i cancelled unless i got a doctor's note. well, my doctor is literally in the same building as them so that seemed pointless. they did not understand this. if i was going to leave the house extremely sick, i might as well just go. i was feeling a little better 24 hours later, luckily, but it still probably wasn't safe.

whatever, but now in light of covid-19 i'm more angry about it. how many people went into their office this year unknowingly sick with the illness because they could not plan 72 business hours in advance when they'd get sick, and could not afford $80? 

fast forward to this year after many pefectly fine appointments and i missed my first telehealth appointment because frankly (like most of us) i am working from home trying to play teacher, social worker, and tech support, overwhelmed, stressed, and off medication because it took awhile to get an appointment. so, i misread the time. my fault at the end of the day, i totally admit it. i thought they might make an exception or lower the fee because i'm sure the telehealth situation is messing people up and well, you'd think they'd employ a little empathy right now considering there's a national mental health crisis and they are...*checks notes*...a mental health facility.

nope...an $80 fee. they were nice enough to split it up for me so i didn't have to pay it all at once at least. i'm losing my job at the end of may, otherwise not sure they'd have done that.

i get having a policy. i do, especially for repeat offenders. in normaltimes, i'd just paid it if i did not cancel within a reasonable time (say, 2 business days) and made a dumb mistake like that. but to have no give right now is crazy. 72 hrs is truly insane.  if you have spotty internet or no tech stills, you're screwed . and of course those things already affect the the poor more.

it's also basically impossible to talk to anyone on the phone there. that doesn't bother me too much as i prefer email but just an fyi.

i will keep going there because i like my psychiatrist fine and with my track record, i better stay. in normaltimes it's not as big of an issue. but go elsewhere if you can.

we love sheri! with covid going on we were not able to take birthing classes at the hospital as planned. sheri is awesome enough to be offering these same classes via zoom. there is so much helpful information offered and she takes the time to really go over it all. she allows time for plenty of questions and i leave the class feeling so well informed and empowered to make the right choices for me and my baby. i look forward to each and every class offered and would recommend her to anybody and everybody.

review: so i had something weird going on where my legs were twitching and i had tremors and even chills mostly at night. no one could figure out what was going on and of course this was all during covid time. i would wake up around 3:30 every morning with tremors and leg twitches and hadn't slept a whole night for almost 2 months. i had video chats with mary and anne several times and they were both very nice prescribed a couple things to try to help. finally i was able to go in the office and anne took her time probably spent an hour with me. she figured it probably had something to do with my nervous system and prescribed gabapentin. it was like a miracle i finally slept all night long woke up after 8 hours of sleep with no twitching and feeling amazing! i can't thank anne enough and everyone at pdq mary, pam and everyone there are amazing!

during this crazy time (you know, pandemic!) i have been really struggling with breastfeeding and am still working on it. sadly, since we're being extra cautious because of the little guy we didn't want to have anyone come to our home. which really makes it difficult when you have a newborn that isn't latching well, sore nipples, and 1,000 questions. long story long i found allison through the pump station and man i am forever grateful. i have had several video chats with her where we worked on everything from breastfeeding, pumping, nipple cracks & pain to napping and sleep issues. she has been a huge help and so responsive and patient with all of my first time mom questions and concerns. i will definitely be recommending her to any and all of my mom-to-be friends! thanks allison

review:

i look forward to my future sessions with dr. walker and would highly recommend him.

i was referred to dr. hwang by my surgeon, dr. rad.
from my initial call to schedule an appointment and speaking with cammy, i felt "at ease."    it's always hard going to see a specialist as you may not be sure they understand your concerns and feeling comfortable with the physician.  

my initial appointment was supposed to be a "telehealth" one due to covid - 19.  i wasn't really keen on it due to my issues but dr. hwang was highly recommend by dr. rad and i trust him implicitly and agreed to the "telehealth" visit.  

again, from my initial contact, i was thoroughly impressed.   calls were returned almost immediately as were emails.   

two days before my "telehealth" visit, i received a phone call saying dr. hwang could see her patients in person and was asked if i wanted to go in, i immediately said "yes!"    

when i checked in i was greeted by the most friendly, cammy!   i didn't have to wait long to be brought back to the exam room.  the nurse (i don't recall her name ), took my vitals and although i could not see her entire face due to having wear a mask, i could tell she was smiling as i could hear it in her voice and see it in her eyes.  

before i knew it, dr. hwang came in along with her nurse practitioner, richard.   dr. hwang made me feel at ease right away.   she was already knowledgeable about my health history - and it's a long one.    (many times i feel health records aren't always read).   i was impressed on how much she knew about me and felt like i was already an established patient!    

dr. hwang explained everything to me simply and really took the time to get to know me as a person!

she had prescribed a medication for me and there had been a problem with my pharmacy as they said they did not receive the new prescription.   i called dr. hwang's office back and literally within a half hour, richard, the nurse practitioner, resolved the problem and my prescription was actually ready!

i know this is a long review, but there are several people - people who offer their care to make it so!  

everyone i was in contact with was friendly, professional, and offered genuine care! 

i'm rest assured that i can trust my health care needs with dr. hwang and her staff.   i'm confident they will all make a great team in getting me to feeling better.  thank you to all.

during the pandemic, athletico - andersonville south worked with me to continue my pt while i've been stuck at home. i've been able to keep up therapy twice a week via zoom, it's not only helped my knee, but daresay my head as well. thanks so much!

my hip has been bothering me lately to the point where it was difficult to walk straight so i thought i should see a physical therapist but wasn't sure how i could with covid-19. i contacted christi at kintsugi pt and she scheduled a telehealth session. i didn't even know that physical therapy was possible through telehealth, but thought i would give it a shot. glad i did because i am able to walk straight with no pain. the session was surprisingly good. christi was able to diagnose my symptoms by asking me to do this and that and making me point out the part of my body that hurt. then she was able to teach me how to perform various stretches to help release the pain. and this was all done on my iphone in the comfort of my home. i guess physical therapy can be done through telehealth! i got great results after just one session! i highly recommend anyone needing physical therapy but not able to get to the clinic, especially in these times, to give telehealth a try. and i highly recommend seeing christi at kintsugi pt.

i agree with other reviews that the answering service is not great.  dr. tran has addressed this by using a patient app that allows easy communication via call/text.  it has been a huge improvement.

with the covid situation, i have been seeing him through zoom and haven't had any issues.

review: dr. bakshandeh is amazing!!!  she helped me with my child's skin issue.  she did a telemedicine consultation and i had all of my questions answered without having to leave my house during this quarantine.  she is kind, caring, patient, and thorough.  i can't recommend her enough!!!

i am so thankful that i was able to find dr. huang during this pandemic. he may have literally saved my life by making the correct diagnosis and getting me off the wrong medications that was prescribed by other doctors. 

in early february of 2020, i had an endoscopy done by a gastroenterologist, and about a week after, i started noticing some shortness of breath and also felt a swollen lymph node behind my ear.to make a long story short, fast forward to march of 2020, in the midst of the covid pandemic,i had difficulty breathing and a fever which led me to believe that i may have had been infected with covid19. ultimately, after my lab test result tested negative for covid but indicated klebsiella pneumoniae bacteria, i went to see a pulmonologist at ucla where an x-ray of my lungs were taken to rule out pneumonia. although, the pulmonologist from ucla did not listen to my lungs, he prescribed an antibiotic given the bacteria found in my nose, and asthma medication for breathing problems (even though i had tested negative for asthma couple of years ago by this same doctor) after my breathing condition did not improve, i reached out to a different pulmonologist in glendale who provided telemedicine consults. the second doctor prescribed more asthma medication and ultimately told me to take a repeated x-ray and repeat covid test after my condition did not improve. after the chest xray came out clean for the second time, the doctor in glendale told me he did not know what the problem was and told me to hang in there or go to urgent care. by this time, i had slept only 5 days out of the last 15 days and lost over 10 pounds because of severe breathing problems, sleep deprivation and no appetite. 

then out of desperation at 6:00 am, after having stayed up all night, i searched for another pulmonologist and fortunately found dr. huang on yelp and reached out to him by email. surprisingly, dr. huang got back to me right away and saw me the same day through zoom video conference. dr. huang patiently listened to my history regarding the onset of symptoms  and complaints and told me that if one of the asthma medication he prescribed did not improve my condition within the next few days, then he would see me to figure out what was going on. after symptoms did not improve, i went in for an evaluation and dr. huang actually listened to my lungs using a stethoscope and also conducted a lung function test himself. after a comprehensive evaluation and a lung function test, dr. huang told me that i likely had some form of upper respiratory infection before which may have caused breathing problems and fever, but at the time of his evaluation, my lungs sounded normal and i should not be having such severe breathing problems. he told me that what may be going on is that the asthma medication that i was prescribed was causing anxiety and panic attachs which was making my breathing problems worse - causing a vicious cycle - breathing problem so take more asthma medicine which causes more anxiety which makes breathing problems worse. 

after i was taken off the medication, my breathing problems improved significantly. although, it took weeks to deal with getting over the psychological component of having had breathing problems and panic attacks, i am now almost fully recovered. 

dr. huang was so patient, kind, and methodical in the manner in which he diagnosed my condition in the midst of the covid pandemic. it was so difficult to find a doctor who was willing to actually listen to my lungs during this covid pandemic and give me a correct diagnosis. i cannot thank dr. huang enough. had i gone several more days without sleep, i'm not sure if i would still be alive today.

in my experience, dr. parker is an extremely knowledgeable and compassionate professional. due to the current situation with covid-19, i needed to see him for a virtual visit for ear pain i have been experiencing. the telemedicine visit went extremely smoothly, and i do not feel in this particular set of circumstances, that i would have been any better served by an in-office visit. i highly recommend dr. parker!

due to covid19, i had a telemedicine visit with dr. lam.  i enjoyed being in the convenience of my home and not having to go into the office.  this should become a norm, especially if you don't need to check any vitals.  dr. lam provided the same type of courteous service that she provides in the office.  the televisit was less than 10 minutes. 

it was easier to log on via my computer via the link that was sent to me vs. trying to download the app via my iphone.  if you are using your phone, please make sure you know your portal username and password, otherwise it can take up to 24 hours to get this to you.

i had a wonderful experience with dr. jow. i had slowly increasing joint pain in my finger. what i really loved about the experience was the efficiency and effectiveness.

on the efficiency side, i was able to do everything online within minutes. they have easy-to-use online tools so i could book an appointment online, have a video conference, get detailed physical therapy instructions, and receive all the documents i needed for insurance reimbursement. 

on the effectiveness side, my finger is feeling great after 2 weeks of at-home physical therapy exercises. during the video call, dr. jow and her physical therapist were extremely patient trying to understand my life/behaviors and what might have caused the pain (likely additional computer/mouse use due to covid) and also recommended preventative actions.

i love the easy online tools to save time on bureaucracy and the longer in-person session where extra time, patience and understanding counts! they were willing to spend as much time as i needed to feel comfortable... far more than the 10 minutes you would usually get from a team associated with a large hospital system.

will definitely be going back! thank you dr. jow and team!
