i'd like to start by saying the owners are amazing people  who clearly care about helping addicts recover. they understand just how serious this disease can be, and i hope they're able to work out the kinks that are keeping avr from reaching its full potential.

that being said, it took my counselor a week & half before we first talked.... and that only happened, because i had to seek out which counselor was mine & approach him. he would sit in the office, on his phone, all the time. even when a client was sharing his last relapse to the group. it wasn't until 2 days ago, when i told him i had suggested he be let go, that he started to change.

the woman who worked to get me in, maddie, the 23 year old "house manager," was a completely different person than the one who advocated to get me in. she would come to work & spend 3 hours behind closed doors in the office, and ultimately ended up getting fired on 5/22 at the end of my 3rd week. how can one manage a house if they're hardly there?

along with her, katy, the "program director" was also let go the same day. i saw katy maybe 5 days in 3 weeks, because she has a medical condition. she said it was due to covid-19 that she couldn't be there more.... however; covid has been happening for more than 3 months & within 1 day of being fired from avr, they had their secondary director show up from san diego!!!why wait so long to get him in there? the house was clearly not being run properly by management. 

also, there was zero structure on the weekends (again because of covid), but what about adapting to family zoom meetings, therapy sessions, or 12 step meetings? nope, the therapist wasn't even there on sundays.... we literally sat around doing nothing recovery related. 

speaking of therapy: i was promised 1-2 sessions a week and, over 3 weeks, should have had an average of 4.5 sessions.... i had 2.  there was another client who had been there 5 weeks & also only had 2 sessions.

i wrote a 6 page letter to maddie & katy last tuesday 5/19, and both were let go by friday. i've been told it had nothing to do with my letter, but rather it was something that had been ongoing for sometime. they only opened last september, so that must mean since the beginning?!!! i kind of got the sense my letter was sent up the chain of command by a counselor i shared it with the day before our meeting (5/18), but that's just speculation:

we even had a client who was caught stealing from others & no reprimands were made. it was an ongoing theme of poor/addict behavior with him, and i was amazed it was allowed to continue.

another staff member would talk about his sexcapades, during the virus, and it only made me think of the risk he was putting us all in!!! was he wearing a mask & social distancing? (obviously not). the first day this staff member came in (following the two ladies being let go) his first comment was "ok, no more katy.... i guess that means staff can workout here again!!!" it's crazy that was his first concern.

they forced me to go to parks, and outings, during the pandemic. during which almost all of the clients chose not to wear the masks they had brought.... again, zero control. the reason i couldn't stay behind at the house was because of a 30 minute window with no staff on duty. at $1,000 a day (per person x 6).... they should be able to figure out those 30 minutes & so much more.

i had to remind staff, several times, of when sessions were supposed to start, and had to remind them that the office door (where meds are stored) was left open, once. they were also very relaxed about wearing masks around the house, and following the precautionary protocols shown on the website.

about 50% of employees are in their early 20's, with good recovery, but not well versed in running successful groups/managing people, or a rehab. they try to be your friend instead of the people in charge of helping to save your life. 

people go there because they couldn't make it on our own & are in need of professional help!!!! not one person was allowed to give us so much as an aspirin without first calling the advice nurse (not sure they even had any), so i'm not clear on what kind of "nurses" the website was referring to having onsite.

there is so much more i could go into, but you can message me if you would like. i'm happy to share the letter i wrote with anyone interested.

they are working on changing many things, and this place has the potential to be great. hopefully it will be someday, but there's a lot to do in order to get it there. i just don't have time to worry about them getting things together, while i'm fighting for my life, and the system is far from what i was promised.

i'll be sure to stay in touch with my housemates and, if they can confirm change, i will be more than happy to update this review. at this time i can only say my experience was less than what i had anticipated, but pray they will turn things around soon!!!

take this course! my fiancé and i attended the love made simple workshop this past weekend and feel more in love, happier, and closer than we ever have before.  
because of covid, our weekend retreat was moved online. to be honest, we were skeptical a "zoom" retreat would be as energetic, safe, and helpful. but, as soon as the workshop started, all our fears were calmed. gal and liron's love and energy burst off the screen and the online setting felt intimate and comfortable. 
gal and liron are loving and sensitive people; all participants were greeted with such warmth and kindness. they created an environment for couples to share, be vulnerable, and feel free of judgement. 
for us a huge highlight was being able to "break out" of the large group and speak 1 on 1 with a therapist. each therapist we worked with was zoned in; they truly wanted to help and, most of all, they gave my fiancé and me the encouragement and tools to "really" say how we were feeling in a safe way.

it absolutely warmed my heart and i have the couples center to thank. if you want a tune up, are struggling, are about to get married, or have been married for many years take this course. i couldn't recommend it more highly.

we were borderline  frantic as my husbands condition seemed to worsen.due to the covid19 outbreaks, the offices are only offering on line visits which i totally understand.somehow our appointment was cancelled due to a computer glitch and we were not notified. we waited all day for a callback from their office and decided  to call. understandably so, there was a long wait to speak to a staff member. in this case, the wait was well worth it. our prayers were answered when i spoke to james. he checked our records and deduced there indeed was a miscommunication and was able to fit us in to see a doctor  online! he was professional, reassuring and came through. james, if you see this, please know how much your efforts were appreciated! riverside medical management- please note the kind attention james bestowed upon us and what an exemplary employee he is.he restored our faith in the system. keep up the great work! another quick shoutout to gia and another  woman that called us and patiently  guided us  through the zoom app!be safe and thanks again james!!

well, telemedicine doctor said it's fine, she had contact dermatitis and it will go away, take zyrtec. so we did. today is thursday, i took her back to the doctors yesterday (urgent care) and low and behold she has an extremely contagious virus that manifest in a pox like skin infection and now the 6 month old has it too. 

thanks pediatric associates for being heartless and all about the money. i work in healthcare, i know they could have seen her and they were just trying to string arm me into give them my last few dollars. 

disgusted

as soon as i learned i was pregnant and had my first few appointments with my ob, i wanted to be as healthy and active as i could be. my ob recommended wellborn lifestyles and it has been the best thing i have done since getting pregnant! not only are the classes amazing, but it has given me a sense of community that i never knew i needed. i honestly don't know what i would have done through this pregnancy without them! rebecca and all of the teachers are incredibly supportive, loving and giving. since the coronavirus outbreak, they are doing all of their classes via zoom and continued to give us exactly what we need, right from our home. not only that, they are also considering everything else we need (meeting with pediatricians, talking to an ob about the situation etc..) and bringing it all online. i'm endlessly grateful for wellborn, thank you for everything!!!

i had such a top-tier experience with the neurology center this week. i had a virtual visit with dr. herzfeld earlier this week and testing with dr. cohen today. both doctors had the best "bedside manner" i've experienced in quite a while. i was already nervous about my appointments (no pun intended), but both doctors made me feel at ease/in great hands. i also had a great experience with the receptionist over the phone when making my initial appointment. i wasn't rushed and she was patient in taking my information. she even joked with me a bit. it's good to see that their office is maintaining good spirits during the pandemic. the medical tech that performed my emg test had such a warm spirit and walked me through every step (my first emg test). the desk receptionist took all pandemic-related precautions and was also pleasant. this type of great end-to-end service is rare. kudos to the k street office!
address: 2021 K St NW Ste 210 University Building

review:
hidef is amazing! mitch and dr.zach's holistic approach to health and fitness makes so much sense. they have a 3 step approach to ensure that you're at your best: personal training, nutrition coaching & physical therapy. more below about each program!

mitch handles personal training & nutrition coaching. as a trainer, he will uncover your personal goals and work with you on a weekly basis. you'll start out with modifications to your diet with the over all goal of achieving a healthy lifestyle that you will be able to maintain yourself. mitch is extremely encouraging and understanding of each situation. my weekly meetings with him were just what i needed with accountability & a healthy dose of positivity that i needed. 

on the personal training side, mitch has a wealth of knowledge and will write out at home workout programs for you to follow. if you want 1:1 coaching he provides video conference coaching which is motivating for me! knowing i would be working out in real time (via video) made me get up and ensure movement. mitch will make sure that your form is on point and the hour long sessions breeze by! 

we can't forget about dr. zach! he handles the physical therapy portion and has been a life saver since my string of injuries (#thisis30). i've found that even if you're not injured pt is so important to keep your body in the best shape it can be and is great for preventing injuries. i had a skiing injury and my inner knee area never got better even after a few weeks. decided to get it checked out and dr. zach to the rescue! after doing 4 stress tests he found that i had sprained my mcl's. he met with me weekly to get me back to normal and via the medbridge app i had home to follow along. 

then i sprained my ankle during covid and since it was an acute injury dr. zach was able to see me the day after it happened. honestly, this was the best thing i've ever done. i would have rested my ankle and not walked on it for a few days but i found out that you need to encourage movement back to the affected area. the manual adjustments and care dr. zach provides is top notch. i was able to run on a treadmill for 30 minutes *5 weeks* after this happened! he truly takes the time to explain why specific movements are important and what body parts they're activating. 

i cannot thank the hidef team enough. i 100% recommend their entire suite of services, check them out for a consult you won't be disappointed!!!

this medical office, in particular dr. mohindra does not respond to messages. doesn't matter how many times you call or how urgent the message is. she just doesn't bother. she doesn't care. 

my dad got shingles and was seen by dr mohindra. she filled a prescription, but sent it to the wrong pharmacy. a week later, he's still in a lot of pain and discomfort and asks for a refill. it's a saturday and the doctor's not in so we have to wait until monday. i reassure my parents that the doctor will call it in to the pharmacy and all will be okay. try to hold on. 

monday rolls around, and the prescription isn't filled. i call to follow up and leave numerous messages--a total of five. the ladies at the call center were great. very nice and had compassion for what we were going through. i don't want my dad to endure another day of pain from his shingles so before dr. mohindra clocks out at 5, i decide to drive the 40 miles to go to the office myself only to have dr. mohindra say "he's not my patient. have him see his primary care physician." really?? you couldn't just return one of my messages to say that? well here's my final message to you dr. mohindra: it's really rude and unprofessional to not respond to messages marked urgent. you really suck!!

i called his primary care physician who hasn't been in his office for the past 3 weeks due to covid-19. he's only taking appointments by zoom. you need either a computer, tablet or smartphone to do this. my dad is 85 years old. he doesn't own a computer, tablet, or smartphone! he is still suffering from shingles. 

here's what i learned: 1) when you call the number to an urgent care, you don't get the medical office, you get a call center. 2) urgent care offices in general don't do refills on prescriptions. 3) spare yourself the frustration and grief and don't see dr. mohindra!!

during the covid-19 crisis, dr howard led a group zoom call on "handling anxiety in uncertain times". her peaceful and thoughtful guidance was such a blessing in the midst of the crazy news articles and social media we've been reading. she gave concrete advice and tools for understanding how to dig deeper to where the anxiety is rooted and how to physically hold space for your emotions and in doing so release them. i have found that in the couple days since her session i've been able to be more aware of how i'm feeling and instead of resisting it- i've been able to acknowledge it and give myself grace. i am so thankful for her advice and wisdom. she is so approachable, non- judgemental, patient and caring. and most importantly she listens intently and gives you concrete tools for managing whatever hurdle you are facing.

covid dream team... we selected megan peterson as our doula before the pandemic started. she came recommended from a friend and learned that she partnered with rachel wilson to provide co-doula care. my partner and i were on the fence about obtaining doula services because i work in healthcare and we had attended so many newborn/birthing courses. i was very fearful of having a c-section so we explored the option. on our first meeting with megan and rachel we immediately knew we had to work with them. the empathy, warmth, candid conversations and "space holding" were exactly what we needed. the relationship and expectations changed quickly because of coronavirius. we had some hard conversations as in person birth support was taken off the table. changing our support plan to virtual was hard but both rachel and megan showed up. we prepped with zoom calls; private yoga; they dropped off a birth care package full of essential oils, candles, tea, postpartum sitz bath, etc.; the big day came and my husband received support via text, facetime and phone calls. i ended up not having a c-section and believe it was through their support we felt empowered to advocate our birth plan.

after birth support has also been amazing. they provided a lactation consultant to support breastfeeding which was initially very stressful. also had zoom calls, texts and a social distance walk.  i couldn't have been happier with my choice to have not only a doula but to work with megan and rachel. truly recommend!

this took me a while to write because i struggled to find the words for how amazing dr. mofid and his staff are. from the first time i walked into the door everybody was amazing and helped me feel incredibly comfortable about what i was going through. 

i spent about 4 months looking for and going to surgeons that perform a full body in both orange and san diego county. i settled on dr. mofid for his knowledge and explanation of what his plan was and why. 

i am now 4 months post surgery and i am over joyed. dr. mofid is a modern day michaelangelo. i look better than i could have ever imagined. i have 2 more procedures to go and i can't wait for the final result. 

his staff post surgery was great. this happened right around the time of covid-19. i got regular zoom calls and check in from them to make sure i was doing well. it was a level of care that extended far past what i was expecting. 

my surgery was extensive and my recovery was difficult but i felt safe and valued the whole time and that with the care i was receiving i would come out the other side. i did and better than i ever imagined. 

i can't recommend dr. mofid and his team highly enough.

this review is for dr. koutures whom i cannot say enough good things about. he truly is our hero! recently with all of this covid19 craziness, our daughter started a fever, i called the after hours line, did telemedicine visits, sent emails and he did a visit at our vehicle. i kept him informed on everything. on day 8 of her symptoms he referred us to a cardiologist after suspecting our daughter may have a rare pediatric disease. it was confirmed dr. koutures was right. dr. koutures called me from his cell phone while i was sitting in the er waiting to be admitted into icu to check on us. he followed up with us in the icu the next morning. without dr. koutures we wouldn't have caught this in time and our daughter could have ended up in really bad shape. our family is forever grateful for him and his knowledge. as my family would put it, never leave her pediatrician, he diagnosed our daughter over the phone! thank you dr. koutures!
fac_name: ActiveKidMd/Gladstien & Koutures Pediatrics and Sports Medicine

review:
dr. dezfoli is a caring, talented, young gastroenterologist who listens to his patients and their issues. 
he thoroughly reviewed and analyzed my problem (ongoing abdominal pain, ibs c etc.) and tries to find the cause and a solution. very often you are stuck with a diagnosis, but without any help or plan for improvement. i liked my prior gi as well, but it was difficult to get appointments and it's important that a doctor is accessible. i had an office visit with him, but he is also available by telemedicine, which was very helpful during the corona crisis. sometimes it requires out of the box thinking and detective work to get a patient with chronic issues on the right track. i am at the beginning of my journey with him, but i feel in good hands, and i like that he comes up with a treatment plan together with you. the office is nice and his nurse ty is very sweet and professional.
fac_name: Seper Dezfoli, MD - Beverly Hills Gastroenterology

review: i found the egoscue method quite by accident and have become a devotee. i only had one in office session before the virus restrictions were put in place. so i was hesitant about using zoom. i have to say, it has worked beautifully...probably because of the skill of my therapist, lisa. she is very observant and helpful. in fact, she's great to work with. i look forward to our in office sessions again.
fac_name: Egoscue of Santa Monica / Los Angeles

review:
like the therapists at this location, but have issues with main admin office. don't like that they require kids to come to the office and "prove" to the therapists that the child is actually sick and then can be allowed to miss the appointment. otherwise, if you call in it's considered an event and goes towards them taking your child's reserved spots away. it puts the therapists and all the kids that he/she has to see at risk for getting sick. and let's not forget about the parents who still bring their kids in all snotty and tell the therapists that it's "allergies" and don't care... they just want t break to play on their phones. i get it, it's stressful and every parent needs and deserves a break, but you are going to get everyone else sick. and this is their policy before covid19. 

during covid 19 you can bring the child in and therapist can send them home or you can only call out for 2 weeks or the child loses their reservation spots and they give it to someone else. not only is this wrong, but dangerous. we have family members who have underline health conditions and no matter if the facility "wipes" things down and makes people wait in their cars there are still lots of chances of the kids, therapists, and other staff could get sick. we don't know where other families go, if they truly abide the "stay at home" policy, or if their "allergies" are actually just allergies. know this might sound ridiculous to some people as they don't care or think they can't get sick... but think of other people who can. i understand that some kids need certain therapies more than others, but if the therapist could facetime or zoom or just put spots on hold, that would be safer not only for the children, but for the employees as well. they should not be threatening to take away reserved spots bc we are concerned for our families health. we are trying to be concerned for your employees... be more concerned for your patients!
fac_name: My Left Foot Children's Therapy - Centennial Hills

review:
tanghetti has taken care of my entire family (we have 5 children) for over a decade now. it saddens me to have to downgrade my recommendation however today i had an incident with dr tanghetti's assistant that was less than pleasant. not the type of customer experience you'd expect as a long time patient. or from a doctors office offering a stellar customer experience. 

we're in the midst of the international covid-19 crisis, we have a stay in place order and doctors are reducing services based on priorities, which is totally understandable. stress is high. 

i called for a refill authorization and was simply asking for him to pre-authorize a prescription i've used for years. the problem is, after the age of 35, insurance companies deem this medication "cosmetic" unless a doctor is treating you for acne.  

well, tanghetti's treated me and my family for acne for years. i've even undergone accutane treatment rounds twice, if you're familiar with accutane it's for very severe acne cases and typically only needed one time. this tells you how extensive my acne is. 

it puzzled me because i just had a refill two months ago. however for some reason he won't authorize it because there's a generic brand i can pay for?!?! 

my insurance will pay for it, they just need him to confirm that it's for acne not cosmetics. i'm not sure what having a generic has to do with anything.  i'll take generic or name brand. i just need something. 

i was also informed that i haven't seen the doctor since 2016. which isn't exactly accurate because i've had multiple laser treatments in past few years for the acne scarring and he always checks me before hand. 

i told his assistant i need this medication because my face is breaking out a lot right now. 

of course i'd be happy to go in and see him but we all know doctors aren't treating patients unless it's critical right now. as a matter of fact tanghetti just canceled an appointment my son had that was scheduled for this week. we're working to reschedule a virtual visit for him. 

it's a long story but to say the least i was very frustrated and quite disappointed. stress levels are already high enough, definitely not an issue i feel like i should have had to deal with right now. 

what was most disappointing though was when i got frustrated instead of working to help me by scheduling me a virtual visit or saying she'd talk to the doctor again, i was told to go to the goodrx app and see if i can find a place to buy it and they'd transfer the prescription if i needed it transferred. this made no sense to me. it frustrated me even more. i could hear her attitude and tell she was happy to hang up when i said ok i'll call you back if i can't find it for a reasonable price. 

it's already difficult enough dealing with adult acne. i just need dr authorization to refill a medically necessary prescription. but instead it's already been 3 phone calls back and forth and now i still have no medication and i'm left with a sour taste in my mouth with this type of customer service. 

i don't even know what to do at this point. all i know is it's created a lot of unnecessary work for my pharmacy, tanghetti's office and me and i'm still not done. sad to say it makes me not want to go back. which means it would affect my entire family.

dr. avanes has been our family doctor for several years and we have received the highest care possible every single visit. he is caring, kind, knowledgeable, current, dedicated, responsible, present, a great listener, with a great patient care manner and always taking the extra mile for his patients. at this time i am afraid to leave my house due to the virus, but that's not a problem with dr. avanes. i called in with a problem and right away i was scheduled a telehealth session with him. he listened, answered my questions, and gave his advise with outmost care and patience. his office manager, evana, and dr. gabrielyan and his entire office staff are always there to help out with a smile and a great attitude. god bless you dr. avanes!

it is only a 1 because i can't make it a zero.  my mom is 72 and needs to have a prescription for anxiety medicine renewed next week....she has an appt.  they are still making her come in so they can see her....that is where all of the sick people are told to go if they think they have covid-19 and they are making her come to them...told her to wear a mask...she laughed as no one has them, they told her to wear a scarf....what an idiot!!  get with the times...you could do a zoom meeting and only give them a small renewal ( only for a couple of months), but that is right.....you won't get your $$$ that way.....money grubbing pos"
i am no longer a patient and can't wait until my mom isn't either.  with their horrible reviews, i don't know how they are even still open!
fac_name: Dana Forte, DO - Forte Family Practice

review: blown completely away by the competence, compassion, and service i experienced working with anna marie and juanita at chicago family doulas! every step was made so easy for me and my husband and we were consistently learning from our sessions and felt very prepared for our labor and delivery. we were impressed with the rapid communication we received, especially once everyone's set plans changed due to covid-19. we were further supported after our son's birth and heavily relied on our chicago family doulas expertise throughout our process and having our doula available via text and phone and video conference during our entire 15 plus hour labor. i knew from the first minute i interacted with anna marie that chicago family doulas would be a great decision and i was consistently reminded that it indeed was. thank you anna and juanita for supporting us during such an important period in our lives!

let me start by saying how thankful i am that i have found these guys. i woke up with severe back pain one morning and barely could not even move or breathe and gave them a call and they were so kind to set me up right away. i have a herniated disc. due to the circumstances of covid-19 they offered me a telehealth appointment the same day. i have been in therapy with them for over a month and i have changed for the better tremendously. 
the care and love they have given me in this past month where i have been experiencing so much pain was endless. all exercises were supervised and doublechecked via telehealth!! so amazing! thank you assaf for being so great!! they work with great doctors in case you need a medical opinion from a surgeon or specialist and have great connections. so thankful for you guys!

i never would have imagined that the world would have turned upside down within only a year of my child's birth and that wright mommy would be the reason i didn't lose my mind completely while we were/are under a #stayathome order from a pandemic, along with worldwide protests against racial injustice, citywide curfews, plus looting a few blocks away.
when i was pregnant, a friend clued me into wright mommy and me as a great way to build community and learn all about my baby's development. the classes definitely served that purpose and continued to be a lifeline as everything moved to zoom. i was concerned at first that zoom would make it difficult to focus, but then classes were made so that we had a singing/play portion for the children in the morning and then an evening portion for moms.  my child loved the music portion and recognizes julia with a smile. she even started to recognize and wave to the other children. the evening segment was therapeutic, plus educational! i feel the group grew even closer through the zoom meetings.
julia kantor has given so much invaluable guidance, info, and support to me and the other moms. like a fairy godmother, she's helped me enjoy so wholeheartedly the experience of being a new mom. she helps filter out the multitude of well-meaning voices in your life giving advice about every possible thing. it has also been so critical to have her expertise on "baby-proofing" your marriage so that our relationship with our partners can also be fulfilling.  i can't say enough good things. i will miss the class and look forward to the day i can see my mom friends in person again and have our little ones play!!

great class, even on zoom! 

our teacher, synthia praglin, is personable, knowledgable, insightful, funny, and very passionate not only about child development but also about the parents' well-being. she is thorough and is always open to questions, encouraging conversations to flow naturally, shares her own anecdotes, and keeps things light when necessary and more serious when it calls for it. 

my husband and i started the class in-person when our baby was about 4 months old and moved to online due to the pandemic. now with our 7 month old, although it's obviously not the same, we are still learning so much from synthia and gaining the benefits of a community, getting to know other parents and their journeys, and seeing the babies grow and develop. 

especially during this time of isolation, we look forward to our sunday class and to synthia's warm energy, caring and positive attitude and vivaciousness. keeps us sane and in-the-know! thank you for keeping this class going!

we love our parent & me class! our teacher, synthia praglin, is thoughtful, knowledgeable, generous with her time, and supportive. we began the class prior to the pandemic and after a few weeks of pausing the class, many of us decided to resume via zoom. i'm so glad we did as we've built a camaraderie with the other parents and have benefited from synthia's wealth of information. we look forward to catching up on sunday's - singing songs with our babies and connecting on age-specific issues.

i attended wright mommy and me with my son tyler from summer 2019- june 2020.  both during our in person classes and when we went digital on zoom (due to stay at home orders surrounding the corona virus), wright mommy and me has been such a blessing.  we were not meant to raise our babies alone and wright mommy and me had provided that village for me and tyler.  these mamas (and our fearless leader julia) have been there for me every step of the way.  i am extra grateful that zoom was there for us to help us stay connected during the super isolation of quarantine.   julia did a great job moving the platform online (with little notice!).   i would recommend wright mommy & me to any mama who wants a village. you won't regret it!

as a new mom, wright mommy and me was my saving grace. navigating motherhood is never easy and it felt so good to just come to a place, with my baby girl, where she and i could both learn- from not only julia but from the other moms and their babies who were going through similar journeys. julia kantor, our instructor is incredibly gracious, kind and warm. she was always available via email and shared informative articles and links. theresa, the program's manager, was just as gracious and was quick to answer emails. when the coronavirus pandemic upended all of our lives and the session switched to zoom, i was very skeptical; i didn't think the same warm environment could be recreated virtually. i quickly realized when we had our first zoom session, that it became something so much more. i felt that tender community spirit was stronger- perhaps knowing that again, we all were now navigating the unknowns of toddlerhood compounded by the unknowns of a pandemic together made it feel as such. (i signed up for the next toddler session via zoom). we were singing new and familiar songs which my baby girl enjoyed and discussed pertinent topics on toddlerhood. thank you julia and wright mommy and me for just being there for us during these emotional and difficult times.

i can't speak to the services at rwj rahway hospital, itself, nor the quality of patient care you can hope to receive.  however, i can speak to the amazing community programs the hospital runs.  if the support groups run by the hospital are indicative of its patient care, i have to say the organization is truly invested in health.  

rwj rahway, at one of its namesake gyms, rwj fitness & wellness, offers community-based support groups.   i personally attend the fibromyalgia support group & i can only describe it as a "life-saver."  before the covid-19 pandemic, we were already a close-knit group who discussed the countless lifestyle/medication/nutrition/exercise changes we'd made to improve our situation.  but, when we all went into lockdown, we had unique issues.  

led by an rn who could not care more about us if she tried, our meetings are a mix of scientific information (some unfolding & yet untested) & anecdotal experience.  

i've seen an amazing increase in my health from (regularly) attending these community meetings.  but, & more importantly during this crisis, i've had the support from people who understand our special risks & needs.  people i'm proud to now call "friends."

during this time, rwj & mindy, our group coordinator, have made zoom support group meetings.  it has been a lifesaver, when we can't be physically close, to keep this sense of emotional community makes it seem less abnormal.
fac_name: Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital Rahway

review: customer service is so important, especially when dealing with vulnerable children. reliability and consistency, or the lack thereof, are critical for helping traumatized children to heal. sadly, lifeline has failed to deliver that. since the start of the pandemic, we've had telemedicine appointments with nearly a dozen providers, and though there have been occasional glitches, most of them do a good job. not so with lifeline. for the second time in 3 weeks, we were left sitting in a zoom meeting, alone, with no way to contact the company (except by leaving a voice mail).  this is very harmful for children who already have trust issues. the first time it happened, i contacted roxanne dalpos, the owner (via voicemail, of course), and she delegated the response to an underling. her response was, "who gave you my direct number?"  not, "how did we fail you?" or "what can we do better?" but peevishness about having to interact with an actual patient. after the second failure on their part, we finally gave up on this outfit altogether. there is an acute shortage of trained mental-health professionals, especially those willing to work with young people, and lifeline has the potential to be so much better.

i have been so impressed with 4c medical group!  my first time there was a few months ago, i had no problem getting an appointment that worked with my schedule! i was nervous about making an appointment during my lunch hour as i know most doctor's offices make you wait a very long time! i was pleasantly surprised with the efficiency of the office and how quickly i was seen! dr. kapur was friendly and made me feel so comfortable talking about my health concerns (something i personally do not like doing).  he was extremely knowledgeable and made me feel confident in his diagnosis and treatment options. the next time i saw him was during the covid-19 pandemic, i was able to utilize the telehealth service they have which made me feel so much safer in this scary time. i have to add, i was also very impressed with the ease of the telehealth service! it took virtually no time to set up, i was sent a reminder and was seen on time. thank you dr. kapur and 4c for making my health needs something i don't have to stress over! in today's world having a doctor that can ease your stress instead of adding to it is priceless!

i'm quite skeptical of therapy, but i felt that i needed to speak with someone. had been dealing with high levels of stress and slight panic attacks. she made me feel safe to speak, comfortable and at ease to talk about anything and she is not robotic like most of my past therapists. very good listener and will actually talk with me instead of the blank stare and clip board. unfortunately i was only able to meet with her in person a few times before covid19, but thankfully she offers video chat sessions. i miss the warming smells in her office, but she's been very helpful via video during this stressful time. her price is fair and she's been very helpful to me. she's also got a really cool dog that i also miss. he's great. 

definitely gonna continue utilizing her services.

i guess i should thank alliance mental health for giving me the motivation to join yelp, and reigniting my desire to tap into my journalism, truth-telling roots, so-to-speak. something i love (i'm being facetious) is when an already grotesque practice blames a natural disaster or pandemic or nuclear war on its grotesque practices. this practice was terrible for as long as i've been a patient, which was a full year before any viral pandemic, and, come on, let's be real, their solutions to telehealth are like if luddites were in charge of providing care to patients during a time of crisis, which is probably, true. my therapist's office, my gp, have no problem being communicative, e-mailing a simple link for telehealth, and already putting in efficient practices for re-opening. shock! therapists? i've struggled (unsuccessfully) with aud (alcohol use disorder) for 30-something years. finally, in 2014 i discovered sinclair method (https://www.the-sinclair-method.com/), which turned out to be a lifesaver. my drinking quickly went down to safe levels and i started to have alcohol free days several times a week. for 5.5 years i was a social drinker, a "normie" in aa speak. 

some life events led to me developing a serious depression and covid lockdown became the last straw. in the beginning of april i stopped taking my medication; from there, my drinking quickly escalated and turned into a heavy 6 weeks binge ending in er, icu and a 10 days detox. after i got back home on may 24, i wanted to make sure that sinclaire is still working (i still had some meds and started taking them right away); i had 3 drinks on the first day, then it went 1, 1, 0, 1, 0 - amazing, considering my condition before the detox. 

by then, i found an outpatient program (iop) at good sam behavioral. i was surprised to learn that dr cecil a. bradley, who prescribed me naltrexone all these years, is the medical director of this program. the program seemed very useful since a) it is in person, no zoom, b) i could address my underlying emotional issues and c) i could get an extended medical leave, since i was not ready to get back to work yet. on thursday, may 28 i was admitted; i was very open about what i've been doing before, what brought me there and about my intentions (go back on sinclaire, since it works great and aa stopped working for me at some point). everybody seemed to be open-minded, accepting and approving of my course of treatment. some even wrote down the name of my method and said they were curious and want to learn more about it. 

on friday noon dr bradley showed up, took me to his office and told me that their program is based on full abstinence and if i kept up the controlled drinking, i'd have to leave. he said there are alternatives to aa and suggested some other program - he just could remember it's name. he is in his 80s and seems to forget things. i promised to think about it over the weekend and tell him about my decision on monday. after all, at this point i could possibly refrain from drinking for the duration of the program.

however, on monday my case manager handed me a recovery plan with mandatory conditions: attend at least 3 meetings a week, find a sponsor and report progress at each morning session. i told her i don't do aa, and i was told to go talk to dr bradley, and again he gave me a dilemma: full abstinence and meetings or leave the program. "if you don't want aa, there is this other program - can't remember it's name... rational recovery?" "- smart recovery?" "- yes, this must be it". "- how is it better than aa?". "- i don't know. we require full abstinence and meetings". so i informed him that i'm quitting and went home.

this got me thinking: 1) why did dr bradley prescribe naltrexone all these years and even wrote me another 3 refills on that monday if he disapproves on sinclair method so much? 2) how does a doctor send a patient to some program can't even remember the name of? did he do any research or he really doesn't care? 3) why did they admit me at all, knowing full well my intentions and dr bradley's position and giving me false hope? 4) what kind of doctors put a patient into completely unscientific, faith-based programs with abysmal success rates and force him to abandon something that is proven to work for 80% and this patient in particular?

so i googled dr bradley and discovered that the medical board of california twice has suspended his license, once in 1990 and second time in 2007 (http://www.psychcrime.org/news/index.php?vd=32&t=california+disciplines+psychiatrist+cecil+bradley) he also was known to be sending referrals to life choices and working at red road recovery, two rehabs run by the same person, richard franko, who has no certifications and is a drug addict himself. life choices were reported to california's dhcs for "making parolees assist in human like slave duties as a condition of not sending these clients back to prison. dhcs investigators heard from people they interviewed that franko had indeed used clients for personal benefit and, in doing so, compromised their sobriety." (https://www.sanjoseinside.com/news/rehab-owners-who-lost-license-amid-shocking-allegations-deny-charges-get-back-to-business/)

makes you wonder, how does a doctor like cecil bradley ends up a medical director in well-respected hospital like good sam? i would not recommend going to good sam in- or outpatient behavioral programs until they replace him. the rest of the staff seems to be great, but there is nothing they could do to help me under current leadership.

i've been having some neck/back aches recently and was worried that it could be something more than just aches and pains. i was worried that it was going to be difficult to see a doctor before i had to go back to work because everything was closed from the corona virus. it turned out to be very easy to schedule a telemedicine appointment with dr boak. i was able to be seen quickly while waiting in the safety of my own home. my concerns were handled in a prompt, secure, and professional way. i was very happy with the service and very grateful that my doctor was readily available in this uncertain time.

thank you dr. qamar! what a fantastic experience from start to finish. it was my first time meeting dr. qamar and it felt like we already knew each other. extremely friendly, personable and of course professional. 
it was a 'telemedicine' appointment due to covid-19 but that didn't hinder the experience. 
throughout the appointment, in addition to getting to know each other, dr. qamar took the initiative to explain what drugs i was taking and why. the main point here, is the why. i haven't had the why explained to me before in such a manner that it engaged me to want to learn more and take action to do something about it (ex: the role the liver plays in cholesterol). and we put together a game plan moving forward since this was our first appointment together. 
not completely downplaying the professionalism of the doctors i have had in the past, they've been pretty good too, but dr. qamar was the best i have had. i engaged, learned and wrote down an action plan to get my health to where it can be and should be. 
to make things even better, he ended up saving me a lot of money by suggesting i check out certain sites for coupons that i was unaware of. turns out i was overpaying by a lot for the same medications that are way cheaper at different pharmacies using these coupons. i am excited to have such a great doctor/person be my primary care physician. 
thanks again dr. qamar, i look forward to the next appointment.

patrick toy is a great, easily accessible resource for anyone seeking physical therapy, especially in south seattle. a highly skilled, experienced physical therapist, patrick sees patients in his home office on a quiet cul-de-sac in our community of lakeridge. referred by my primary care physician, i first went to patrick for an injured shoulder. i couldn't lift my arm and was in pain. over the course of several weeks, through his hands-on care and assigned exercises, my movement returned and the pain vanished. in the midst of this, i was so impressed that i immediately emailed him when i hurt my hip lifting a box. i knew he would tell me what movements would shorten my recovery time, rather than just resting my hip and applying ice or heat. it was so wonderful having him as a go-to nearby resource. this second injury occurred during the pandemic, so patrick analyzed and prescribed exercises via telemedicine. as he had always done, he sent follow-up videos of the assigned exercises, but as an added help, at my request, i filmed patrick with my iphone, as he explained and demonstrated tools and exercises on my desktop screen. thus patrick became my exercise companion and personal trainer in my cell phone. 

when i first read reviews of patrick's work, they sounded almost too positive. but i can vouch for others now. patrick is a real find. he has worked with infants and past-100 seniors, and every age and condition in between. he listens. he has a wealth of knowledge about the human body. he is also kind, good-hearted, and simply fun to be around.

ester is an exceptional trainer. i live in new york so i am taking her classes via zoom since gyms are closed due to coronavirus. she is the most well rounded and knowledgeable trainer i have ever worked with. she knows so many varieties of movements and knows a great deal about the body and how it works. she is very special and professional and is a master in the world of fitness. i'm very glad i found her and i highly recommend her zoom classes.

review:
maxwell medical has impressed me since my first interaction with their staff. i had been going to another physical therapy office for a while that had inconsistent hours and fluctuating days when chiropractic care was available. i was getting off of the subway at bowling green and decided that i would accept one of the 'free medical massage' cards that people are always handing out over there. i called and was greeted by someone super friendly. i was able to quickly schedule my appointment. 
when i arrived i was really impressed by the cleanliness and overall first impression physically. i was escorted into a room for my free massage and the gentleman who provided it did a phenomenal job. i had been suffering from neck and shoulder pain for months and the only thing that would tame it was trigger point injections. this gentleman was able to specifically target the area of issue and without any prior knowledge asked if i had a dual-screen monitor at my desk -- in 10 minutes, he got to the root of my issue that i had been going to the other office for 2 years to seek treatment for. he was extremely well educated and was able to explain the way different muscles connect to each other. he was very professional. 
since that initial interaction, i have consistently been making visits. when the mandatory shut-down happened due to covid-19, maxwell staff contacted me once a week, sent newsletters, and provided telehealth options for people to continue their care at home. since returning to their office they have quickly adapted to ensuring that patients are safe in their environment. they offer masks, wipes, gloves, etc. their front staff feel like friends or family. they are always so friendly, welcoming, and accommodating. i always leave feeling well informed by the doctors and pt staff. 
one last thing, i have been receiving chiropractic care since i was 14. my aunt is a well-known chiropractor in indiana and i started receiving alignments at an early age. it takes a lot for me to feel comfortable with someone doing my adjustment, but their team of chiropractors do a phenomenal job. 
if you are looking for general wellness care for pt/chiropractics, do yourself a favor and check them out. you won't be sorry!

i absolutely love dwc!!!! the staff and the girls at the front desk are the best in modesto!!

 i have been attending dwc for aprox 5 years and my therapist is the best! she makes u feel so comfortable and she listens to you without judgement! she even makes me laugh.
  i love the fact that dwc is still open during the covid-19 outbreak!  their passion to keep going and provide services throughout this tough time is absolutely amazing!!! 
i love the tele-health option! 
this is where your therapist can call you or video chat with you!!! 
it is an amazing option to have!!

if you haven't found a place to work on you, come check out dwc!!! you will not regret it!!!

review:
during a pandemic with the covid-19 virus-
i had a phone visit scheduled with the dr. per their office request because there not seeing patients in person. i scheduled it on 3/17/20 for today 3/18/20. denise from the doctors office called me 1 hour before my appointment to tell me that due to my insurance there would be a $50.00 deposit or fee. because there not sure if there office will be reimbursed for the phone visit. i said to her that my insurance covers it and that they should call them to verify, because i did and the insurance rep me the office is supposed to bill the phone visit like an office visit. also the president and federal government announced on tv that all insurances will cover everyone during this time for those who have to do teladoc or phone visits. she started arguing with me and was very rude and said no one has sent them money or information on how to handle this. she needs to speak with dr. bernstein and who ever else is in charge to get this straightened out. dr bernstein there is no room in healthcare for employees that are rude or to tell there patients the money is more important than their health when they are sick. very disheartening i've been a patient  of this office for 15 years.

i scheduled my appointment in early march and the earliest appointment they had for a new patient was march 30. due to covid 19 i got a phone call on the thursday before my monday appointment telling me that it had to be rescheduled to april 27. i received a call today from kayla letting me know that my appointment was to be moved to may 27. i told her that i was extremely frustrated because this is a psychiatrist office. i told her i am fine but what about the people that aren't fine. just because we are new patients they cant be seen ( i know that there are video chatting with their other patients). kayla said the covid 19 was messing everything up and that they needed to be careful that they don't get the virus and die. many times i told her i know it wasn't her fault however i am just expressing my frustration and that mental health is extremely important. i said i have been trying to get in since the beginning of march and now i keep on getting pushed back. she said that kissimmee doesn't have a lot of psychiatrist and that maybe i should go somewhere else. i said what time is my appointment and she said the same time 11. i said ok and what's your name? (as i always do when i make an appointment or talk to someone over the phone) kayla hangs up on me. so i call back and no answer when i hear the answering machine and hear the name kayla i automatically remember that its the same girl that gave me my 1st appointment. she is the receptionist. finally i speak with someone else at the office that was extremely nice and i start telling her what happened and how she hung up on me. that is horrible customer service especially when i am calling for help. i said i just need to make sure that its kayla that i was speaking with and she told me yes that's who you spoke with and she will not make the appointment. i said ok so now you are refusing my service and she said i guess she is. i told her that it was fine i will contact headquarters. i will gladly fine a different place to go to. no one should ever be spoken to like this especially for the type of office that it is. i am sure all of the calls are recorded so they can go back and listen to the calls. i never yelled at her or called her out of her name. i was just voicing my frustration. i worry about how many people have also had to deal with this type of treatment while trying to get help. instead of listening to patients that are trying to be seen she is more worried about catching and dying from covid 19. this is completely unacceptable.

i wound up having a follow up appointment during the pandemic, and my doctor's office called me prior to let me know they'd be doing zoom or facetime (depending on your preference) appointments. i've done tele-appointments, but not with this office, so i was happy i didn't have to cancel my appointment and didn't have to go into the office.

i was given instructions a week prior to my appointment, asked about my preference (facetime or zoom) and they let me know someone would be calling an hour or so prior to the appointment to pull my chart, verify some information, prior to the doctor calling me.

all there instructions were spot on. i received a call about an hour prior to my appointment, where they verified some information.

then at my appointment time i received a facetime call from my doctor. she was as cheery as could be. she went over a few things, had time for questions, and once again, i didn't feel rushed, which is a plus.

she refilled my prescription, went over a few things, and said if i have any questions to give the office a call, as she's in the office monday - friday.

pros:
-easy and convenient feature
-ability to be in the comfort of your own home w/out having to go to the actual doctor's office
-easy to talk to and great bedside manner

cons:
-none

tips: i'm not sure if this will become a staple with this practice, but may be worth asking in the future after the pandemic eases up if you can have an online appointment versus in-person.

dr. vega has been such a blessing to our family. do to covid 19 my original obgyn had to cancel all his appointments to handle telemedicine patients. in dr vega's care, she had a wonderful warm bedside manner and was completely honest and straightforward with how my scheduled c section ( due to high risk) would proceed and the new protocols in place during the pandemic. our healthy baby girl is doing great and i definitely would recommend dr. vega at southwest medical associates in las vegas

i went in because i wasn't feeling well in the middle of covid-19 and was surprised none of the staff were wearing masks in the facility, including in the small patient rooms. the visit itself was good in that i got blood work and a chest x-ray which were fine but when i continued to feel bad 3 days later i spoke with them twice over the phone to get a covid-19 testing referral and never heard back and was finally told i had to do a virtual visit with their provider which costs $55 and requires setting up a new account with all of the information they already have. i would not recommend this place right now.

it's #thankyouthursday, and as part of it, i wanted to thank a medical provider, given everything that's going on. 

and kaplan barron is at the top of my list for this! 

my husband and i have been taking our son to this office since he was born last year. and throughout, we have been so impressed with their compassion, professionalism and knowledge. 

you can read my previous review for a lot of the nuts and bolts of this. and since i wrote that, we've had to take my son to this office on a few occasions, especially after he started daycare and inevitably got colds and minor sicknesses. 

each time, we were able to either get some answers quickly via the phone or get an appointment, usually the same day. they have also been on top of switching what they could to telemedicine during this pandemic and working to keep everyone as safe as possible. 

it's a relief to know that my son is in such great hands with dr. slone and the rest of the providers at this office.

i was tested for covid 19. your team registered me by phone and quick video conference. i drive 10 minutes to your clinic, parked in front and your technician came out within 2 minutes, took a saliva sample while i sat my car. she was very personable and efficient. the whole process from the time i first called until i was tested was just a little over an hour. very impressive. our family has visited the concord facility several times in the past and we are always treated extremely well. thank you

kelley is an amazing, effective, and compassionate pt. i started seeing her in person during my pregnancy and postpartum and found it so helpful. we switched to virtual visits during the pandemic and i am amazed by what she is able to assess over the camera. plus, it is a great opportunity to get feedback on posture and movement "in real life" like bending over the baby crib or carrying baby. what a difference it has made! the other thing that i really appreciate is she is so understanding of motherhood and life and there is no judgement when i can't do my exercises between sessions. it is so nice to feel supported.

horrendous process to try to get an appointment and know what i would be charged. the person who answered the phone gave me the biggest run around on how much i would be billed because "if the dr. hadn't seen my son in three years, they would normally bill it as a new patient visit." upon confirming that it had not been overt three years since my son had last visited, she said, " well it's getting close to three years so they might want to bill it as new patient visit."  when i asked if the policy was three years and over, yet it had not been over three years, why they wouldn't follow the policy, it boiled down to that they could bill for a higher amount if they used the 'new patient code' vs the code for a standard office visit. i pushed back and she finally agreed that the price should be for an office visit  given my son was under the three year mark (did i need to waste 10 min. of back and forth to ensure they didn't bill my insurance with a code that allowed them to charge more??  no!).  despite getting an email broadcasting that they were offering telehealth appointments during the pandemic (which prompted me to call), she then went on about not being sure how it would be charged because it was telehealth (not in-person standard office visit) and she "didn't have any codes for a telehealth visit."  i asked who would have the code so we could find out the cost, she said the "billing person" who wouldn't be back in the office for several days. i then asked to speak with the office manager and asked why they were email blasting advertising for telehealth appointments yet unable to tell me what i would be charged. he also tried to obfuscate with all kinds of gibberish and basically said that they won't know until after the appointment whether they would want to bill it as a 'level 3' or 'level 4' (gee, that clears it right up for me given i know what that jargon means for pricing implications).  even after i explained that i simply needed the dr. to look over the allergy blood test results that my son's gi dr. ordered to see if there were specific foods he was reacting to that might be triggering his inflammation, he refused to tell me if that would require 'level 3' or 'level 4' service.  basically, they wanted me to make an appointment, come in, and let them charge my insurance whatever they wanted afterward. i said no thanks  i'll move on to a dr. who is more transparent and straightforward with their costs.  thanks for wasting 25 minutes of time for nothing. in what alternate reality do the people running this practice live in that they think they don't need to tell customers the upfront pricing of their services?  would i take a pile of dry cleaning in and say, "here you go, just clean this and let me know afterward what your prices are, thank you."? no!  would i hire a builder, give them my plans, and then say, "build my house and just let me know when you're all done what that cost will be?"  the arrogance and duplicity of this office was astounding. 

update to original review:
