my company had a weird insurance and i'm more than blessed to have found mmp. dr. manrique, clinical director, was willing to see me immediately. this was in the beginning of quarantine order. offered in person or virtual visit. i was in crisis. i went from near daily visit and i'm still seeing him twice a week. he's amazing. his technique is intriguing and very therapeutic. as a social worker for 20, i've never trusted or connected with a therapist. michelle, the office manager is also amazing. i've since changed insurance and they're working with me to continue my treatment. i highly recommend mmp. again, more than blessed.

recently had an allergic reaction to an otc topical cream. a bad and painful reaction all over my face. i felt it was a bit of an emergency due to the discomfort and spreading so i was hoping they would be able to get me in within a day or two. no such luck. i called other derms and their appointments were far out too. when i again called derick, the second girl i spoke to said she just had a cancellation the next day. great. upon closing the appointment arrangement, the receptionist taylor asked me if i needed botox or filler. no i did not. 
i arrived early to my appointment to do paperwork. i wore a mask as did the staff due to covid-19. i also used hand sanitizer several times. i have a hearing impairment and read lips. after waiting 35 minutes later than my appointment, the receptionist came out to say their office manager said i would have to reschedule as they had no interpreter. i told her i don't know sign language (so no need for an interpreter)and they could write on paper if necessary. i let them know that if i had to reschedule b/c of this i would be very unhappy. they took me into the room. the om didn't even come out to see the situation. i explained at the time of making the appointment about my disability. the receptionist insisted this is "our policy". 
when bayley the pa saw me, i let her know how insulted i was. the questions i asked were if you are afraid of getting the virus from me then, how are you doing botox and filler if a patient has a mask on? if you are so afraid of getting the virus why are you even open and not doing solely telemedicine? 
i was the last appointment of the day and i guess they wanted to go home.  i have never been treated so poorly. my husband is a patient here too. i think it's time for us both to find a new dermatologist. they have gotten too big to care for the patient here anymore.

i have been waiting for my neurologist to call me back for over 3 weeks. this is unacceptable and i don't care about the covid19 excuse. there are not that many cases in hillsborough county. i guess this is the only virus that matters to them. i should get it on purpose to get a response because clearly they don't care about other emergencies at this point. telemedicine is a joke too no appointments really give me a break.

it's clear that this practicioner is in it for the money.  while the rest of the responsible world restricted non emergencies during covid, and used telemedicine, he's marching in anyone into his offices representing that the exam rooms are clean.  what about the last carrier who sneezed in the office?  taking temps does not screen asymptomatic carriers. anything to make a buck, right?  if you don't come in for the visit he won't renew your prescription.  ethics?

in my experience, dr. parker is an extremely knowledgeable and compassionate professional. due to the current situation with covid-19, i needed to see him for a virtual visit for ear pain i have been experiencing. the telemedicine visit went extremely smoothly, and i do not feel in this particular set of circumstances, that i would have been any better served by an in-office visit. i highly recommend dr. parker!
this clinic charges co-pays for telemedicine visits, in violation of cuomo's executive order about telemedicine during the covid-19 "pause".

i hurt my shoulder on a patient transfer a few months ago. i'm also a physical therapist, so i really take into consideration who i reach out to for help. due to covid and proximity, i live in texas now, i was able 'see' nikki for an evaluation via telehealth. of course, hands on assessment ideal, but i felt rise pt had the clinical knowledge and experience to guide me through my shoulder dysfunction, virtually. i would certainly recommend them to anyone in the area.

they had the whole "telemedicine" thing down before we were all forced into it! one medical was added to my company's benefits package this year and while i'd created an account, i had never tried any of their services until this past week. i've been dealing with an annoying little health issue over the past month or so, but it wasn't a big enough deal for an irl doctor's appointment during covid-19. i finally logged on and realized i could be on a zoom call with a doctor within the hour! i made my appointment, had a video call, and had a prescription called in to my pharmacy all within an hour or so. could it get any easier? 

love how easy their website is to navigate and schedule appointments. i was even able to send over my insurance information via their portal rather than filling out forms or calling in. they do have physical offices you can visit (it's not totally virtual) if that's your thing, but even once social distancing orders are lifted, i think this is a great option for people who are busy or dealing with common/minor health issues that shouldn't really require a big trip to the doctor's office. i'm personally much more likely to deal with a doctor's appointment if i can skip the commute, parking, and waiting room!

a combo of skiing and surfing left this middle-aged mom with a very painful shoulder this season.  i wanted to find a physical therapy clinic that had a lot of experience with treating surfing shoulder injuries.  this is the clinic, and when i called desperately on the day before shelter in place went in to place, they squeezed me in to their schedule that very minute.  i saw jake koch, and he was incredible, knowledgeable, professional, and empathetic.  jake even continued to see me over video telehealth when the clinic had to close due to the coronavirus.  he walked me through advancing exercises each week, and my pain diminished and i was able to get back in the water.  i am now seeing him for maintenance strengthening and stretching to make sure i don't reinjure it.  the clinic is beautiful, open and airy, and they are incredibly responsive both on phone and email.  they also take insurance.   

cannot recommend obpt and jake koch enough.

i love moti! clean, plenty of space, and plenty of parking. therapists are engaged and always up to date on the newest research and technology. front desk staff is friendly. pt "homework" is sent online which includes gifs or videos of the exercises you're supposed to do. 

when everything went crazy during the covid pandemic, moti was up and running doing telehealth appointments within, like, a week! it's obviously not the same as seeing a therapist in person but it has been nice to prevent back sliding in my recovery.

i have been going to moti for quite some time. 2018 i went to the los feliz location and as of 2020 i moved over to this fabulous new highland park location. i see ann. she has helped me tremendously healing my broken ankle. we transferred to telehealth when covid started and it worked out so well. it was amazing how she could explain exactly what to do via the phone. i am looking forward to going back to clinic. there is not one element that they cannot treat. i am so grateful.

moti is an amazing place. they have been so helpful in continuing my pt in the time of covid. i had been on my road to recovery when they had to close due to the stay at home order. they seamlessly switched to telehealth and i was able to continue on my path with weekly virtual appointments. it has been extremely helpful to be able to continue healing without a break in exercises. anne is wonderful and couldn't have been more helpful. thanks you for being there for me!  i look forward to continuing the process when you open again soon. until then,  i'll see you on the computer!

a few years ago, i tore 2 of my lumbar discs (that were already herniated) and couldn't handle the pain. having tried physical therapy before and it not being successful made me hesitant in going back into that routine. but, i decided to give it one more try. i wanted to find a new and more innovative group to go to, so i did some research and found moti. i am so happy that i did. it changed my life. working with dr. ann degrey has saved me from chronic lower back pain. she is super patient and really listens to my needs. their hands-on treatments and exercise programs allowed me to get back to my normal routine in just a few weeks. now, i go on a weekly basis to maintain my health and learn new ways to tone and heal my body. when the pandemic hit and i had to stay at home, their telehealth program was very helpful. i wasn't really sure how the program would work, but it's been really easy to follow and maintain. dr. ann not only modified my exercises so that i could use whatever i had at home to keep up with my routine, but she was super flexible with her time. if you're in pain, give this team a chance.

if you are looking for a professional pain management clinic - this is not it. although, dr. ding is nice enough - his office staff is the most unprofessional group of individuals we've ever encountered at a doctors office. 

when my husband (brain tumor patient) was first sent there we were never scheduled in to see dr. ding - but got his then pa. she prescribed a medication that my husband was immediately taken off of by his primary because it put at significant risk for a bleed because it was known to interact with his coumadin. 

our next issue was last winter after a snow/ice event. my husband is in a wheelchair. i called to make sure the handicap spaces were accessible. we were met with sarcasm on the phone. we were told that we would find out when we got there and that if we chose to cancel our appointment it would count against him. we showed for the appointment to find that the handicap spaces were never touched. 

yesterday was the last straw. on tuesday we received a call asking if we would be in the office for his scheduled appointment. after explaining that all his other doctors (including hopkins) were doing telehealth with him (because of covid 19) we were told that we would be contacted the next day via zoom. first of all, zoom is not considered a secure application. second, we were told that no telephone call would come prior to the zoom appointment - we would just have to watch our email account from 3 pm on and wait to be given a link. i told them that we couldn't sit and babysit an email account for an unspecified time. there was no resolution. so i downloaded zoom to my phone and took my husband with me all day in hopes that we would not miss that zoom appointment. we were never contacted by phone or email with a link. the next day around 10 am i was contacted on my cell phone to speak to my husband to check him in for his appointment. i explained to the girl that the appointment was the day before. she said she didn't know what happened, blew it off and continued like it wasn't an issue. i tried numerous times to answer her questions (without my husband there) and she got belligerent with me and said she needed to talk to my almost deaf husband or she would cancel the appointment. i reminded her that this wasn't even our scheduled time. she very sarcastically replied, "well, what would you like my to do, daaaaaaaaahlin?"  then she told me to hold on. she never put me on hold but told the other girl that i was refusing to cooperate. she came back to the line and reiterated that she needed to speak to my husband or i needed to bring him there. by this time - i was already driving home so i told her i would get him on the phone in 15 min. she hung up on me. when i got home i put him on the phone. he questioned the other girl as to why the call didn't come the day before and she said she didn't know. he asked for a call prior to the zoom link arriving by email. again, they refused and told us to monitor our email until....  until what???  they then hung up on him. we called the office for 15 minutes following that hang up ...and they would not answer the phone. 

we have never had another issue with a doctors office in the 10 years he's been sick. 

this is the most outrageous, unprofessional office we have ever encountered and he's been seen by a multitude of doctors and other medical professionals in 2 states for 10 years. we will never return to this office. the staff is incompetent, rude, and unprofessional. if it was possible to give zero stars we would!

this place is a joke. during a pandemic, requiring patients to come into the office, despite their being immunocompromised status, just to get a refill on medication they have been taking for years. (not a scheduled medication)
their refusal to provide telemedicine during this frightening and dangerous time shows they have little consideration for providing patient centered care. 
the providers in the office are putting their support staff at risk by requiring all patients come into the office for routine and/or sick care. the cdc has provided the data supporting the modifications needed to protect others and slow the spread, yet this practice is failing to do so. 
as a medical professional, i am very disappointed in the quality of care provided by this group. i am not a patient of this provider, but my sister is... i will be contacting those who provide oversight about this.

because of covid19 lgb was creative enough to adapt a virtual speed dating platform ,which is the best thing ever having also attended their previous speed dating events. other meetup group virtual dating events just put all the women into a zoom group together. there were no one on one introductions to connect you on a personal level like lgb nor levels of femininity or masculinity preferred, to select. the " breakout rooms" of lgb are the best feature for that reason. it eliminates cat fishing and fosters accountability in putting forth your true self. so get yourself together with your best rona hair doo, a little makeup, a bright smile , a private space with the best lighting , fill out your profile.....pic included and focus  on 5 mins of great conversation each round(s)! happy girlfriending....

i do not usually do reviews, but i wish i had read the reviews earlier than an hour before my appointment. all the negative reviews about this doctor were right. she does not come off as a nice woman. the reason i chose this office was because i needed immediate help and i'm new to the area. there office was the fastest one to get back in touch with me and schedule and appointment quickly. the doctor and i used the video chat because of the whole covid-19. dr. hasan seemed to keep getting aggravated with me when she couldn't hear me or see me clearly. she was asking a lot of questions which is normal when seeing a new doctor. when i go to explain my situation, she made me feel like i was dumb and didn't understand my own situation that i have been dealing with since 5th grade and i'm now 26. after the session was almost over, she didn't really give me an option to opt out of "counseling/therapy" just kind of said well you are going to do this next and scheduled the appointment. she was very cold and not compassionate for a doctor practicing psychiatry. i hope whoever reads this will listen to mine and everyone else's negative feedback to prevent them from a disappointing appointment. if you decide to go for it to see for yourself, i hope you remember this review and go "she was right".

disgustingly irresponsible, disorganized, and incompetent. 

the staff working at the front desk are so unreliable that i'm speechless. 

covid-19 story time:

on tuesday, the clinic called letting me know that i have to go in to get my third shot. i give them thursday and friday as my available dates, and they said they'll give me a call the day before to tell me to come in. thursday rolls around and i have yet to receive any confirmation from them, so i call to follow-up. they had no memo or recollection of needing to schedule an appointment with me. i had to remind them of why they called me in the first place. we ended up scheduling for friday at 11 a.m. 

on the day of my appointment, i arrive at 10:52 a.m. and see another person waiting outside decked out in masks and gloves under the glaring sun. i, too, am wearing masks and gloves. i see a sign telling patients to wait 6 ft apart and to call the clinic. i call to let them know i am here, and they have the audacity to say i didn't make an appointment with them. like.... are you seriously kidding me? 

i ask them what i'm supposed to do and they tell me to come back tomorrow. after yelling at them for wasting my time, they said they'll let me get the shot today but i have to wait. i ask them how long i'll have to wait, and they said they'll see me after the person who is waiting in front of me is done. i once again asked for an estimate of when that'll be and they said 12:30 p.m. so they were expecting me to wait outside for 1.5 hours wearing masks and gloves in the heat during a global epidemic without letting me know that it'd take 1.5 hours until i pressed them for an estimated time. thanks for wasting my time and my gloves and mask. 

i have no idea how long the person in front of me was waiting for but she was still standing there when i passed by 30 minutes later. how are you going to make appointments and not do your best to stay on time to prevent patients from waiting outside for a long time? especially when the appointments are limited right now, and not many people are actually visiting the doctor at this time. 

when i returned at 12:30 p.m., they saw me promptly and i was able to leave the place within 10 minutes. 

in the past, they've also promised to get my records from my former family clinic to see what shots i'm missing, but they have yet to do so. every time i go in, they ask me about my missing shots and i always tell them that they have to get my records. when they hear that, they just brush it off. 

however, i do like the doctors here. the female doctor with glasses is pretty friendly. one of the guy doctors is also very knowledgeable - my mom loves him. my mom video chatted him during the coronavirus about a new back problem and he prescribed her some medicine.

after a bad experience about a year ago when i ruptured a disc in my lower back. i had written treatment off and was actively living with consistent lower back and neck pain. with the quarantine in full effect i had the time
on my hands to start readdressing my issues .a friend of mine recommended dr. todd. i called and had a set up a telehealth visit for the next day. my first appointment was supposed to be a general intake and review. fast forward  an hour and we're talking specific stretches that work within my lifestyle and activity level. i appreciate how dr. todd would let me complain about all my aches and pains and  suggests stretches and mobility except uses  to kind of peel the layers away and expose the root issue. i've had 2 major break throughs in just a month of weekly telehealth visits. my neck and back pain are almost non-existent and through posture techniques suggested by dr. todd i've found a way to manage and alleviate migraines which i've suffered from my entire life. overall if you're looking for someone who will take their time assessing you and let you work out what's happening in your body in your own time. this is your guy. i plan to continue visits for the foreseeable future . 6 out of 5 stars.  also incredibly fair priced if that matters.

dr. tang has great bedside manners and really cares about his patients.  my mom was having severe sciatica and we had gone to several specialists to figure out why she was in so much pain and why the injection did not help.  luckily we were able to see dr. tang despite the covid-19 pandemic going on. dr. tang was very patient during our initial consultation meeting and spent time to explain in detail the mri to us in layman's terms and help us really understand the images (which no other doctor had taken the time to do so before).  unfortunately my mom did need the lumbar microdiscectomy but dr. tang  assuaged us by explaining the procedure in detail. 
on the day of the surgery even though i could not go into the surgical center because of covid-19, dr. tang call me on the phone prior to the procedure so i could hear the instructions with my mom and also called me after the surgery to let me know everything was ok.  when i went to pick her up he was also nice enough to walk out and say she did great during the procedure and he would call in the next day to check up on her. dr. tang is very good about post-operative follow up care, even when it was difficult with the pandemic which required telemedicine.
fac_name: Gordon Tang, MD - East Bay Neurosurgery & Spine

review:
just had a wonderful appointment with dr. lee over zoom due to covid-19 procedures. she was very attentive and got in touch with a physical therapist for me after i had dislocated my shoulder, not to mention i just called yesterday! incredible response time.

looking forward to more positive experiences as the need occurs. thank you!

i preregistered online. because there was no transparency with prices and i thought it would be cheaper to pay cash pay as i only wanted a covid test. their website said rapid testing and although i knew the antibody test was less accurate it would give me peace of mind before being around family on the weekend. i called on my way to ensure cash pay would be cheaper and was told to call my insurance. i called my insurance that said i'd have a small copay plus the cost of the test if it was antibody and free if pcr. when i arrived early as directed on the website, i had to repeat all my information because they have "2 systems". i then had to wait for a nurse to call and get my symptoms. no one collected my insurance card info. i was told to drive around to the side and wait to be tested. i did and waited another 10 min where i was asked to repeat my symptoms yet again and then was swabbed for flu and covid. i was told i could wait 15 min for the flu results but explained i had a phone meeting and zoom meeting coming up and had to start heading home and could i please be called with the results. i was told yes. i explained the insurance scenario and instead of taking my card before i left, i was asked to call with the info. i called the clinic 3 times before getting a generic number who reluctantly took my info down. i still don't know if they charged my insurance or credit card. i called the next day for my flu results and was told it would take 4-5 days. i said "not when she told me 15 min". he said well i don't know what to tell you when that's what the computer says. he said i will have a provider call you. i said "you all were already supposed to call me and that never happened, so can i speak to someone now?" and he said no. i said "so if someone doesn't call then what do i do, call again?" he said, "i guess so." so sure enough no one called and i still don't know my results. whole process took an entire hour, which isn't horrible, but i expect price transparency, more efficiency, and above all honesty. these are my medical records!

update: no one called that next day so i called and they said someone would call. no one called the third day either. finally i found out my flu was negative but the covid test that was being quoted as 2-5 days has now been 8 and no results yet. i did find out that they did charge my insurance

update 2:

13 days later no results so so called. before going to urgent care on the 21st i called my insurance to to verify my benefits and i was told that the pcr test would be paid for but that the rapid screen would not. today, the fifth call to the urgent care, they told me that they needed me to go to labcorp and get retested and that they would do the rapid screen. i explained that i am not going to do the rapid screen because it is less reliable and i refuse to go back and i would like a refund as they charged me for the covid test and i never received any results. they refused to transfer me to their billing department and said i would need to call the lab. she stated "i refuse to argue with you" and she hung up on me.

what is my recourse?

i've been dealing with shoulder pain for over a year and have seen one other chiropractor, a massage therapist, an accupuncturist and three personal trainers.  aside from not being able to do my normal workouts and yoga, i had finally had enough when the shoulder pain and my lack of mobility were preventing me from doing simple daily tasks like hooking my bra strap behind my back!  i reached out to dr. bockmann and described my situation over the phone...mind you, this was during covid lock down so no in-person appointments.  he said i was showing signs of "frozen shoulder" and immediately emailed youtube links that demonstrated stretches and exercises and asked me to follow up via email in a week with my results.  needless to say, the exercises and stretches were not fun, however, i noticed a 30% increase in mobility!  after my second (tele-health) session, more exercises and increased length of time for holding stretches, i started to see 50-60% improvement!  i finally met dr. bockmann in person after three weeks from our initial phone conversation for a desperately needed adjustment and some myofascial release (some things you just can't do over the phone or via a zoom call).   i left his office feeling rejuvenated and at least an inch or two taller! haha.
it has now been a little over a month and only three sessions with dr. bockmann (1 phone, 1 tele-health and 1 in-person session) and i can honestly say i have about 90% of my shoulder strength and mobility back.  i am confident i will be 100% soon!  dr. bockmann's dedication and commitment to truly help people recover from pain and injury without the sales pitch of weekly follow up visits and treatments speaks volumes of him and his practice!   i can't thank you enough dr. bockmann!  but i will try my best by posting this review and referring all my peeps who suffer from any pains or injuries!

would rather give a zero because they let their staff get away with being rude. although my doctor was knowledgeable and professional, the front desk person was never particularly kind, which i noted, of course, as going to a psychiatrist for depression, one would expect to be received with kindness, none to be found.  so, during the pandemic i broke my foot, fine, because its a remote visit, just like my other providers are doing, a few glitches with them, but no problem, just kindness and courtesy.  suffice it to say, with tms i was charged for a visit i was unable to access because 15 minutes prior to the online appointment the lovely front desk person called to tell me i hadn't filled out my forms. i told her sorry, i broke my foot, missed the email. i now have to create my profile on their portal and go to the tab marked forms to fill out the forms. (she only tells me about the forms, of course).the green tab marked forms had a list of three documents highlighted in blue. in this folder, off to the side in subtle gray lettering, there is a lengthy 20-30 hieroglyphics but looked nothing like the other codes i used. i noticed it but it had no wording associated with zoom. remember the tab was marked 'forms'. at no time did she mention i needed the code from this sub-file forms. once in a form it puts you through all three and then you hit submit.  then is says, completed.  they had texted me a day or two earlier asking me to log into zoom 15 minutes prior to the appointment, which i did. i sat waiting for 20 minutes and then called their office.  the front desk told me i could not talk to the doctor (now this is 5 minutes after the appointment), and she proceeds to say repeatedly "its on the portal", i repeatedly tell her i have the portal screen up and its not there.  she put me on hold mid-sentence, came back and i told her i was done with her condescending attitude.  she told me its my problem. i told her to f'off and hung up.  now, three hours later, i'm sitting comfortably in my bed and the manager calls. i'm thinking she's calling to apologize, but when, i'm sorry, i used the f word to describe the fact that i'm the f'ing patient who doesn't deserve condescension. she proceeds to tell me to be kind.  wow. are we at the office in front of others, or did you just call me at my home?  its called a disgruntled, mistreated client, using to one adjective to describe my experience when caught off guard by the manager's phone call while convalescing my broken foot.  so i say, "i don't need this, i'll look for another doctor, and good bye".  then they text me a message that i missed my and to schedule a new one.  then they send me a letter uninviting me as a patient. no "we're sorry that happened to you".  i'm sorry, did she not hear me?  i said i'll look for another doctor. then, to cap it off, they bill me for the missed appointment.  so much for treating clients as human beings.  not a problem though because all that really matters is i didn't stand for it and walked already before their rude letter came.  what an unpleasant mess they are. oh, by the way, i believe this is my second negative review so i wouldn't write this if i didn't truly want to make sure others can avoid feeling like an outcast at their psychiatrist's office.

i have a relative who is also a doctor suggested me to go to urgent care (instead of emergency) since i don't have health insurance.  so i picked cityhealth urgent care because the yelp rating.  i was happy with everything i've experienced.  1st, i need to call a number before i can walk directly into the door due to my fever and cough.  matthew was assisting me, he is very friendly.  i do think he should geared up more to protect himself because he's helping someone with fever and cough during this crazy covid-19 epidemic.  then sean talked to me via video chat.  i was extremely happy about this method because our health care staff should be protected as much as possible.  sean was very professional and efficient.  he quickly ordered 3 tests for me: x-ray, flu test, and covid19 test.  wow i can get covid 19 test!!!!!!  thank you sean!  x ray showing i have pneumonia; and sean prescribed me antibiotic and cough medicine.  my covid19 test result will be available in about 1 week.  tomorrow i will have a follow up video chat.  cross finger that i don't have covid19!!!!  one of the best things is that my bill is affordable!  thank god for the charges!  i thought i was going to pay a lot more (which can be very stressful) but their charge is reasonable and affordable.  
i recommend anyone without health insurance to come here for urgent care!
thank you sean, matthew, justine, and everyone who had helped me today.  i wish you all safe and healthy!
and thank you for working during this scary covid19 epidemic.

awesome personal trainer! currently offering zoom workouts during the covid pandemic. suitable for all fitness levels; she gives modifications to make exercises harder/easier if needed. friendly, laid-back environment!

melissa is a savior!! i was so traumatized by my 5 month olds nursing strike, and to make matters worse it was during the covid-19 shelter in place. i was hesitant that a virtual visit would be beneficial, but it was the best thing i could have done. not only did melissa comfort me in the fact that "more was going right than wrong", but she identified some digestive issues and reflux, acknowledges that pumping more was not a good choice for me, and recommended herbs to manage my postpartum anxiety. when our appointment was done, melissa continued to be in contact and was easily accessible when i had a question, concern, or even a hard moment. she truly repaired my relationship with breastfeeding! i could not be more thankful for her ongoing support.

i had my first endometriosis surgery in 2017 and my second endo surgery first thing 2020. i found bebe and my pt caitlin in mid 2019 and she helped me relieve pelvic floor pain before my second surgery and helped evaluate how everything was after my second surgery. she did internal and external pt work for me. it's always nerve racking at first for me going into these types of appointments, but caitlin is calm, educated and helped me learn how to do some self care. i'm lucky that bebe pt takes my insurance, but from what i understand they take several insurances, which can be extremely helpful. they extended their services to do virtual visits due to the covid19 outbreak and have virtual visits approved through insurance as well. from the nice and efficient front desk workers, to the staff keeping the place clean, to the pts and aids that help take you through stretch and exercise routines, i can't thank bebe enough for their excellent care.  one day when i'm able to get pregnant, i'll be excited to experience their prenatal care as well. keep up the great work!

i called city md to have a video chat instead of having to go into the urgent care.  i'm a senior citizen and im also in the group of people who are most susceptible to the covid19 virus so i was really disappointed when city md wouldn't take medicare.  they take every other insurance but they make senior citizens go into the facility because they don't accept medicare.  very nice.
fac_name: CityMD Farmingville Urgent Care - Long Island

review: i wish i could give 0 zero stars. the secretary is nice but this doctor only cares about getting paid; would not give my mother medication she needs refilled for something she tested positive for because she didn't have the capability to do a telehealth appointment. which is medical negligence. during such a horrible pandemic you would think people would be more accommodating. i work for a doctor's office and we wouldn't treat our patients like this. also when we spoke with him directly he lied and said he was already on video conference with my mom and asked who we were and why we were calling. my mother never spoke with him. go elsewhere if you want a healthcare provider who truly cares about your well being more than their own wallet.

i just had a telehealth visit which was necessary since my last physical visit was in 2017, well before the covid-19 crisis.  it was well worth it since i was able to renew a few prescriptions. the video connection failed and i ended up seeing myself for most of the call and then a call from my physician, came through, while i was speaking to her. however i'm confident the kinks will be worked out. the following day i received a follow-up call from my doctor's office asking if i needed any further assistance.  montefiore has provided me with one of the best medical service i've received in the bronx by far, on par with city md and mount sinai in manhattan.

terrible!!! takes multiple calls to get prescription refills. office has a policy to not issue automatic prescription refills and you have to call ever time. was a mistake ever choosing this place! you would think they would make accommodations  during covid19. no telemedicine option.

i've been seeing elizabeth here for a few months & i can say she has really helped me. i lost my mom in 2018 and went through a very toxic dating relationship for 6+ years, and my anxiety reached an unhealthy level. i decided that i needed help trying to better myself and elizabeth is showing me that path and walking it with me. she also referred me to a nurse practitioner in the woodlands to manage my anxiety medication. i have to say that i feel that elizabeth and danielle at houston family counseling came into my life at the right time, right before this covid-19 crisis hit so i'm handling it better than i might have without them. and they are continuing counseling visits on zoom remotely through this new world of social distancing. if you're struggling with anything, they can help you. don't lose hope, you're not alone. there is help out there.

this was the last facility we went to.  for this site we actually had a chance to meet one of the staff to personally thank her and the entire staff for what they do.  often times we tend to forget it's not just hospitals getting hit hard w/ shortages of ppe and surges of covid-19 patients.  

it was a proud moment that earlier on gavin' first class zoom meeting he spoke proudly of the things we have been doing to help the community.  remember that whilst things are hard now - don't stop your life/routine simply because you now have to improvise.

when you feel helpless, help out.

dr. moinuddin is fantastic. not only does he know his stuff, but he is also compassionate and personable, with a big smile that lit up the room when i visited in person and lit up my laptop screen when we met over telehealth. i have appreciated being able to meet over telehealth during the covid crisis, and greatly appreciated his input into whether or not i should return to work or continue to work from home. i have never felt rushed in an appointment with him and he listens well and asks good questions. 

the first time i met with him back in november 2019 (a month after i moved to the area), i felt i would be in good hands, and i was right! five stars all the way!
fac_name: Colorado Center For Arthritis and Osteoporosis

review: whether in person or remote, i cannot recommend amy enough! i first met with amy in person, and was nervous to transition our sessions to zoom due to the social distancing required for covid 19.  however, minutes into our first remote session any fear i had was wiped away. i finish each session feeling calm, rejuvenated and balanced.  this is a crazy time and my sessions with amy provide comfort and guidance. i am eternally grateful to have found amy and that we are able to continue our work together during these times.

more bad things to say. i left a message regarding my annual exam to this office. i stated i would like a telehealth session if possible, or to reschedule. covid , i guess they're not familiar with it. no response for 4 days. i called back yesterday and left a message begging them to get in touch with me so that i can get my much needed prescriptions. still no response. the message states that i should give them 72 hours!!!!

did you know that there's a difference between a dietitian and a nutritionist? i didn't. both consult on nutrition and can have advance degrees, but a dietician is board certified and must meet continuing professional education requirements each year to maintain board certification. they can design diets to treat specific medical conditions. emily has her master's and is a registered dietician.

as i'm getting older, my usual lifestyle and tricks weren't enough to keep the pounds packing on. i had some success with keto but the calorie count wasn't sustainable and i veered off course, like crash and burn off course. and i eat out. all. the. time. i don't find cooking relaxing or therapeutic. don't judge. i just needed someone to give me a meal plan. i went to emily, and in the end, she gave me so much more than a meal plan.

at our initial intake, she explained her philosophy - no fad diets, just real food, and you can have what you want in moderation. emily has lots of tricks up her sleeve and truly works a meal plan that fits your lifestyle.

more importantly, she is making me think about why and what i eat because if you are going to her, there's something you want to change. i thought i just wanted my macros and suggestions for meals that fit within it, but it turns out i needed more of a coach than a nutritionist.

she listens -- and makes an actionable plan for me.

she checks in -- to hold me accountable.

she's knowledgeable and i learn from her.

she has several flexible plans -- with meal plans, without, meet in person (prior to covid-1) or video conference.

and it's all working -- i've lost some pounds, i'm learning about myself and why i eat, how to stick to my stated goals, and yes, even cook a little.

i highly recommend emily!

terrible place.  i had two zoom talks with a doctor as a new patient and the dr. was great.  she was very honest with me and gave me great recommendations and ways to help my mental illness needs.  however, the office operations are horrendous.  i had to reschedule an appointment more than 24 hours in advance because i had to take my dad to a last minute doctor appointment and they charged me $150 because it wasn't within their 48 hour business day window.  for a company that is meant to help with mental illness, i don't see how causing even more stress to the patient by charging them full price of a visit helps, especially during this covid time.  i wouldn't recommend them to anyone.  stay away.

i want to just start by saying, i have never had a pharmacist make me feel the way elisa did tonight. it's not my fault that she (or her bosses) aren't up to date on the dea mandates, and didn't know you can have controlled substances called in. after an hour on the phone, she verified what we told her. however, she still wouldn't fill it. 

during the covid-19 pandemic, pcp have started seeing patients via video chat. and so the dea has lifted their limitations on certain meds, retiring a hard copy of the scrip, and allowing doctors to call in the script. then the doctor will mail in the script to the pharmacy. i heard her on the phone tell her manager, i know it's weird that she lives in huntsville, but sees a doctor in muscle shoals. like i'm some kinda drug seeker, going from doc to doc to get prescriptions. 

we recently changed from walgreens on jordan lane, because the customer service was awful, sadly this walmart hasn't been much better. so she told me that now isn't a good time to switch pharmacies, we switched about 3 weeks ago, before everything went in lockdown. and she had the nerve to tell me that maybe we should switch back to walgreens! you're going to get your wish next month, elisa! 

so she called walgreens and verified i get this script filled every month, then she questioned why the address on file at walgreens was in tuscumbia(i updated it to huntsville, when we changed to walmart). i told her this is my home of record, and parents address, and i lived with them when i got medically retired form the air force. she questioned me as to why i need these meds, so i had to give her my history about getting injured in the air force. 

so needless to say, we will be in search of a new pharmacy! she wasn't overly rude, it was just the accusations she kept making that upset me. i also don't appreciate that she or her managers, don't know these rules. this isn't a recent change, it's been at least a week since we were told about this. so if the doctors know about it, why don't the pharmacy? her excuse for not knowing, was because she hadn't had anyone come in with this yet. so i guess only then, they update their procedures.

due to world pandemic they offer face time with the dr. and depends what kind injury or sickness if you need to be seen for it or not. i did telemedicine. (facetime) and picked up a brace at the location. overall not so bad experience.
fac_name: Saint Agnes Urgent Care - Main Campus

review: i've been going to dr. cabaret for sometime now and there was a time when no one else had given me much hope on getting help to get off of oxycodone i had had a lot of surgeries in a short period of time therefore i got addicted to pain medication when i was lost and no one gave me hope dr. cabaret told me that he could free me of this evil demon well i was at the end of my route so i took a chance and he did just what he said he would do now i am still in recovery but i am much closer to living a normal life than i was years ago and i owe it all to dr. cabaret and his courteous and professional staff i greatly appreciate him taking the time to work with me and give me back my life i suggest anyone having similar problems come see him! just wanted to update my review since we've hit a difficult time with this coronavirus and everybody that's on medication i need to see a doctor monthly and probably run into some kind of snack or difficult situation i myself worried what would happen when my appointment time was due but i was pleasantly surprised that  laura schmeer one of dr. cabaret assistance took care of me via' zoom app this is where they do your appointment over the phone where they can watch you i was very happy to see things went according to plan and very thankful that there was no down or missed time with my meds, again the doctors office of joseph cabaret thanks again you and your staff are amazing!!!

i made an appointment with dr. fox and had such a great experience! due to covid-19, i was able to see dr. fox through telemedicine and the process was so smooth and easy! called the office in the morning and i was able to get an appointment in the afternoon. the office was professional, efficient, and answered my questions quickly. the ma was also incredibly nice and personable. what i liked most is that dr. fox was very thorough and did not seemed rush. he was able to find me a very affordable medication and gave us helpful tips. highly recommend!

it is with regret that the first yelp review i write is a negative one, and i am inclined to write it nonetheless. i first contacted holt counseling center in january of 2020 as a potential site for my mft practicum. i was met with nothing but rudeness and dismissiveness from the main coordinator, bonnie. i found her to be pushy, short tempered and irritable to put it nicely. in response to any of my questions, i was met with a tone of voice that made me feel like the dumbest person alive for even asking. regardless of how awful the phone call went, she surprised me with inviting me to a supervision group to get started with practicum...huh? no request for an interview, no request for a resume. just show up and we would be good to go. the result of this phone call gave many red flags and i decided not to pursue an internship with them. ultimately, i found two placements and have been happily working through practicum with them instead.  

fast forward to the covid-19 pandemic, and i received a phone call from bonnie regarding practicum yet again at the beginning of may 2020. she informed me many therapists were leaving and they were in search of new interns. she was pleasant during this conversation, and i began to think i had read our initial call incorrectly. i was asked to submit my resume, dl, ssc, and practicum agreement via email and was told about the in person meeting on may 31st (mind you, shelter-in-place has not been fully lifted.) the in person meeting struck me as odd, as i currently have two other placements who are fully telehealth and are not planning on resuming in person sessions, trainings or meetings any time soon. when i asked what safety measures would be in place, her response was "well people can wear a mask if they want to. our lodi office is definitely cleaner than our stockton one, haha." red flag #1,000,000,000.

two weeks after our early may phone call, i received a reminder call and spoke with bonnie on the phone regarding the meeting in which i told her i was still considering how i felt about meeting in person. we ended the call without incident, with bonnie reminding me of the date and time. 

today, may 31st, 2020, i received a missed phone call and a text from bonnie in the afternoon that was incredibly direct, rude and was riddled with false information. she texted me that she had tried to get a hold of me numerous times without hearing back from me...(um...no you didn't), and that she needed all of my info. and if i was still going to work for them (um...i already sent it to you weeks before). i called back and left a message, politely reminding her that all of my paperwork was already done and submitted per our conversation a couple of weeks earlier (and, in fact, i had not heard back from her). she called me back within 10 minutes. i asked if she received my message, and i was met with "hah, no i saw it but didn't listen to it so.." k.... i reiterated my message and she had the audacity to challenge me by saying, "actually, hon, i've called multiple times and you have not responded at all to any of my calls." in which i responded, "i'm wondering if there might be a mistake and if there is another cristina, because i did talk to you on the phone last week and submitted all of my information to you for practicum, as well as my interest and understanding of the in person meeting. i clearly remember the phone call." her response: "yeah actually no, i have not been able to reach you at all, but whatever, are you coming to the meeting or not?" as frustrated with this woman as i was, i managed to hold it together and respond with, "i will not be coming. i do not feel it is safe right now due to covid. i have a family and we made this decision in our best interest, however, i would be open and willing to attend the meeting via zoom as an option." she responded by talking over me and cutting me off with, "uh, yeah, no zoom is terrible and clients don't like that. we need to open, that's just what we are going to do." my response, "i have two other placements who are fully on zoom and it has worked beautifully for all supervision, trainings, and client sessions. i will not be coming today." resulting response from her, "this isn't the placement for you. click." 

really? do not challenge my integrity or honesty. do not gaslight me. do not imply that i am not an honest person. for anyone considering interning here, don't. i dodged a big bullet with this one. thank you, holt counseling, for reminding me i am unavailable for rudeness and disrespect. i'll be awesome someplace else.

bad time to have bronchitis.  april-may 2020.  i started with my regular drs at kelsey.  after 4 weeks of coughing and 2 telemedicine appts, i still didn't feel well.  my dil works at this facility, so i decided to try it out.  best decision i've made in a while!  i came in a side door, was given hand sanitizer, gloves and a mask and escorted to a exam room.  there were notes on the door telling me i could not leave the room, but if i needed to speak to a nurse or the front reception there was a phone in the room for me to use.  craig came in immediately, took quick history and gave me the intake forms.  next was dr nguyen.  i gave him a detailed history and he asked me lots of questions.  decided i needed chest x-ray and covid test.  both the quick antigen test by blood and the nose swab.  katie gave me the nose swab which was a bit unpleasant, however, she explained the procedure carefully, which made it not so bad.  she drew blood.  roger, radiology tech came in next and took me for x-ray.  dr nguyen delivered the news that i needed antibiotics for my lungs and the covid antigen test was negative.   craig came right in and gave me antibiotic shot which he explained would be sore over the next few days.  meanwhile i was still completing my intake paperwork and i had a question for the staff.  i called the reception assistant and she helped my with my question.  all the staff was so pleasant and friendly yet very professional.  i felt confident that they all knew exactly what they were doing and they made me feel safe and comfortable.  i actually enjoyed my appt which took less than 2 hours.  thank you physicians premier er for a great experience and much needed meds and peace of mind.
fac_name: Physicians Premier Emergency Room - Clear Lake City

review: first of all this place takes advantage of people knowing the crisis that is ongoing because of this pandemic, they are charging people 125 dollars (250 in total because i went with my husband)  for a video conference to review if people are sick before they get them tested, we have kaiser insurance and they didn't said anything about that they don't accept kaiser . i don't think it's fair that before you book a so called video appointment, they don't notify everyone that they are going to be charge 125 dollars when the appointment only took three minutes and we basically told them that we needed to take the test because we had the symptoms . i don't think is fair paying $250 for something that is free specially in this moments that we are trying to save as much as we can because my husband got laid off,  i can paid my utilities bills or i can buy my groceries for the week, we tried to explain our situation on sunday may 31 around 10:45am at the ellicott city clinic to the receptionist and she was extremely rude and unprofessional and she said '' nothing is for free'', we asked for her supervisor and she said that the supervisor can't help us and we have to paid $250.  i honestly will never go back to this place ever again and i will advice everyone i know to never use this place again. i hope this helps anyone out there.

this place is horrible. only good for yearly physicals. numerous times i have been disrespected and every time i call when my kid is sick or injured but should clog up the emergency room they offer an appointment 2 weeks out!! judy at the front desk is incredibly rude and hangs up on patients. my daughter had ocular cellulitis and her eye was swelling bad and needed eye drops and an antibiotic. we are in the covid pandemic right now and requested a virtual visit due to having to stay out of town to keep my parents safe. was told they needed to physically see her and said a nurse will call. i get a phone call at the end of the day saying they could maybe get us in for an appointment tomorrow. i was able to do a virtual appointment at cermak immediate care immediately when i called due to the severity of the situation and they handled it absolutely professionally!! need a place go to them!!! i wish new management took this place over as a resident of lagrange park i wish there was a nicer and more accommodating office/clinic available to us in our neighborhood with our insurance.

i've attended carolyn's classes in person prior to the covid-19 self-isolation era. since then, she has been doing online zoom classes. for the in-person classes, there are no real demonstrations, just her soothing melodic voice talking the class through each body movement, so not much is lost in an online/zoom class. 
i especially liked the shoulder and hip class from a recent session because it seems i am hunched over my ipad most of the day. and i can imagine many people now are using more electronic devices than before. but each class is unique and valuable and i always feel better when we are done. it's very relaxing and calming and we all need self-care.

pharmacy submitted for a refill for copd but it was rejected so i called dr office. was told my original prescriber was no longer there and since i haven't been there in awhile i would need to be seen. i'm also immune compromised. i've been out of my inhaler for two days. 
just had my appt, masks not required for public social distancing is not practiced or even encouraged by signs, tape. nurse and np were great and come to find out they offer telemedicine. wish i was told that before i was in the room. been a patient there since 2007 and will not be back.

i am really impressed with taylor & thornburg. after a stint with another pt service that didn't help at all, a neck specialist highly recommended t&t, and boy was he right! alexandra was able to do in-depth problem solving, listen to me, make the mind-body connection, teach me about small muscles i didn't even know i had, and correct course when needed. i'm so pleased with the tangible results of our work together. and when pandemic began, t&t was immediately responsive with telehealth services.

dr. buch was recommended to me by my primary doctors. so glad he did, dr. buch and his staff are wonderful. every time i have had pains or issues due to my ibs, he has helped me get better. i started experiencing pains again, not long ago, i was hesitant to leave the house due to covid-19, he and his staff accommodated me by having my visit via zoom. great doctor and great staff. thank you doctor for all your help.

i've been seeing dr. reingold for a couple years after i had a successful eye surgery with one of his colleagues and he was recommended to me.  i've been very happy, and today when i woke up after a week of very dry, irritated eyes, it felt like i had some sort of scratch or abrasion on my right eye.  i wasn't sure about reaching out since its the middle of the pandemic, and it was friday, and i doubted i'd hear back quickly anyway.  within an hour of the office opening for the day, i got a phone call from the receptionist melanie, who was very kind and set me up immediately to hop on a zoom call w/ dr. reingold.  we went through my records, my symptoms, he examined me as best as is possible on zoom, gave me some recommendations for care, and let me know when he'd be available for any emergencies in case something came up over the weekend.  overall a very easy, quick, positive experience, and it alleviated many of my anxieties.

there is nothing worse than dealing with an unprofessional physician when you are in pain, unless it is dealing with an ignorant, self-righteous, unprofessional physician when you are in pain and there is a national health crisis/pandemic at the same time!!!  if there was an option for "0" stars-that would be my rating for this man.

i met dr. reingold approximately 3-4 years ago when my husband recommended him.  he seemed to be a nice man and intelligent at the time.  i wasn't having any particular eye problems and only needed a ophthalmological yearly exam, testing of pressures, and contact fitting.  i was pawned off on an associate (no longer there that made quite a few of her own mistakes, not taking clear notes or keeping records of what she ordered for me, or even writing down my actual prescription, but that's another story).  i then switched back to him after many complaints regarding the ineptness of the associate and the actual optician (who also is no longer there due to inaccurate records, not returning calls and ordering the wrong prescription in contacts, too many times to count and doubling down on payments-thinking he wouldn't get caught)!

fast forward to last year, with me being so upset with the lack of "good patient practice," that i left yet another message (this time with brenda at the front desk-whom i adore, and is probably one of the only compassionate and knowledgeable people he employs, and would steal in a heartbeat for one of the practice's i manage) and she assured me the doctor would return my call asap.  dr. reingold did return my call, we spoke for quite some time that evening, and without boring you with all of the documented mistakes (photos and notes, time stamped and dated) made in my care, stated to me "it was very hard to find good help, that he paid lower wages-and the pool of whom he had to choose from we're not the best, thanked me for speaking with him and addressing the issues that had been made in my health care, and said he would like to start over, make it right, and be the one to see me going forward."  he thanked me for not writing a bad yelp review (as he had many and even asked me for help in taking them down), as that is part of what i do, and for giving his practice another chance.  he took money off contacts that had been ordered and were incorrect (the 3rd time by his optician) and even discounted my reading glasses as a "goodwill" gesture.  i, in turn, agreed to see him going forward (unless it was contact fittings, which he doesn't do, and was referred to another "new" associate that did the actual contact fittings).  i agreed to move forward and start over.  

this past year i haven't had to have much care but have ordered my monthly contacts with relatively not too many problems.  there was one mistake made again with my actual contact prescription, but was taken care of right away, (the optician that made the last mistake is the one i referred to earlier) and is no longer employed by dr. reingold.  

so imagine my surprise, when i phoned his office today to report that i was in pain, believed i had a corneal abrasion or perhaps the beginning of conjunctivitis (i was a certified ophthalmic tech and the daughter of an ophthalmologist, and am now a medical director here in la, so am aware of the various symptoms), which was why i chose to call and wanted to be seen by my ophthalmologist.  i was told by rosie, the woman that answered the phone (not brenda for the sake of letting the blame lay on the correct individuals) that the doctor had left for the day, was only seeing emergency patients but would email him my message and have him call me back.  i then received a call from another girl, i do not know her name, stating she was going to set up a conference zoom call for dr. reingold and myself.  i then stated to her that i didn't believe he would be able to see anything on a zoom call (he would need a slit lamp to ascertain if there was an abrasion), and that since my eye was not red-didn't understand how he could tell if i did have conjunctivitis.  i told her that i didn't agree that a zoom call was in my best medical interest, and i was frustrated.  then, low and behold, the good doctor was listening in on the call all along (which i had not been made aware of), and he began speaking, "why are you frustrated jana?" continually interrupting after asking me my symptoms and actually arguing with me that he could "see my symptoms on a zoom call."  and guess what????? he was in the office all along and had his office personnel lie to me. i didn't agree but gave my permission to be connected to zoom and after three tries on his office girl's part-connected me through zoom.  there he was, in

****please read the rest of my review below in photos.  there was too much text for the yelp format!

i was referred to center for vein wellness by a neighbor.  i have poor circulation in my feet and lower legs, which causes numbness, occasional pain and skin discoloration.  they did an ultrasound on my legs which the doctor said confirmed issues with the blood flow in my leg veins on both legs.  they later performed a laser ablation to close off part of a vein in my left leg.  the doctor said this would improve blood flow overall.  

it's been two months and i'm due to have the same procedure done on my right leg, but i've canceled the appointment.  i've seen no change whatsoever in how my left leg feels or looks.  they seem to market mainly to those with cosmetic issues, like varicose veins, but it doesn't seem to help pain or numbness.

in addition, i learned that they are still open and operating during the covid-19 pandemic.  at a time when i can't see my eye doctor, and can only see my md over video conference, how can they justify seeing patients for cosmetic procedures?  for this alone, i would not recommend doing business with them.

i also find it fishy that the only reviews on yelp for them are 6 years old.  what's up with that??

my mother has copd and is at high-risk for the coronavirus. in order to continue receiving medication for chronic pain she is required to go to this office and let them count her pills in person. we called to see if alternative arrangements could be made due to her high-risk condition in addition to being on prednisone which makes her at even higher risk for acquiring infection. 

we were told the *only* option was come and sit in a waiting room full of sick people or cancel her appointment. the front desk explained they are all super healthy and it's business as usual for them. 

what virus?! we're fine!

we asked if she could come directly in and wait in the back. no. can we come in one of the other entrances to avoid the waiting room? nope-- cancel your appointment and stop receiving treatment or come in and risk getting coronavirus so we can *count your pills*. no telehealth option. no photo option. no alternative entrance. no accommodations for the safety of their patients.

this is unacceptably tone deaf in the midst of a worldwide pandemic. countless businesses and government offices are changing the rules for the safety of everyone--but clearly advanced pain medicine associates knows better and it's "business as usual" for them.

we have access to patient plus through my insurance. we've made use of it several times, and have been pleased every time. we've never had to wait very long, and our medical issues have been addressed promptly. when the state stay at home order due to covid-19 first went into effect, i was able to get a telemedicine appointment within a very short timme. today my husband made the drive into baton rouge when our local urgent care, which was supposedly "open," said they were only making telemedicine appointments and then never returned his call to schedule one. he got in at patient plus quickly and got out with the prescriptions he needed to address his issue. we've been very satisfied with the service we've received there, and we'll go back when needed.

dr. sims saw me for a telehealth visit recently. i had an eye infection that was bringing me to tears and my family convinced me to go to an urgent care to get looked at. it was a saturday night and also with the covid 19 outbreak going on i didn't want to walk in anywhere and wait a really long time. i was pleasantly surprised that i was able to get a telehealth visit right away via zoom. i did my paperwork online and within 10 minutes i was connecting with dr sims on a video call. she took one look at my eye and knew i had an issue. she was very thorough in her questions she asked me before prescribing me anything. she sent 2 prescriptions to my pharmacy electronically and i was on my way. it was the most convenient dr visit i've ever had! it's been a full 24 hours on the antibiotics so i'm on the mend even though not 100 percent yet. i highly recommend doing a telehealth visit with this clinic. convenient, helpful, and quick.  thank you.

i was worried i had been exposed to covid-19, especially after i developed low grade fever, muscle aches, and sore throat.  i contacted this urgent care by phone.  everyone including the receptionist, the medical assistant who returned my call, and the doctor who interviewed me via telemedicine was helpful and knowledgeable.  they answered all my questions.  i felt very well taken of.
fac_name: Hoag Urgent Care Irvine - Sand Canyon

review: my both 3 ur old twin boys have asthma.  when they get sick they get fever, coughs and wheezing, unfortunately symptoms sounds like covid-19.  when they started getting sick, i was also had some cough and got the covid testing and came back negative, since we've been all home for a month, it was unlikely they have covid either.  tonight, one of the boys symptoms got bad.  he coughed so much he was breathing so rapidly, fever went up to 102.  since it was already too late for a regular dr visit, i called the hoag and they suggested telemedicine once i told the m the symptoms.  any normal healthcare would've told me to bring him in, obviously they need to listen to him.  they said it was up to me but to give them a call once i get there.  i parked right in the front, the place was empty, 2 nurses and the receptionist were sitting in the front talking, but i was advised to wait.  then i was suggested telemedicine again, really???  then they said the provider will come outside and exam him first.  we waited waited, 30 min has passed.  3 yr old in the car will not wait 30 min.  obviously they didn't want to see him.  so i just pulled out of the parking lot and drove away, then of course the "provider" called me. they were taking notes and discussing how to go about taking care about my boy, for 30 min.  yea no thank you.
fac_name: Hoag Urgent Care Irvine - Sand Canyon

review:
amazing workout before covid and during covid (and after covid too!)

the zoom classes are wonderful routines.  you feel great afterwards, see your fellow gym-mates, and have excellent instructors.  

pop have perfected the zoom workout!

i look forward to the workouts and the day after burn!

"pilates of pasadena" is an outstanding place to do pilates (i've been a student there for two years), but since the recent quarantine i have even more high praise to share!  maria jiménez-tierney (owner) and mirko turla (instructor) immediately offered pilates mat classes through zoom the very first week of quarantine!  throughout the past two months i've been able to continue my thrice weekly sessions (both classes and private lessons) with mirko turla. he is an exceptional instructor in the studio but he has really proved his mettle teaching via the internet -- providing excellent verbal cues and explanations that ensure his students are doing all movements correctly and are receiving the best possible workout. also, he really makes the sessions fun!  to be able to continue pilates has helped me to maintain my physical fitness and my mental health as well.  i am especially grateful to mirko turla and maria jiménez-tierney for persevering for their students -- so impressive and very much appreciated!

the good: 
super nice and professional staff. called to setup appointment, was able to get through quickly. everything was super nice, smooth. there's even music while you listen. they validate most parking costs (shockingly expensive without validation). mri is nice and open and roomy, even it's placement is excellent facing the street and giving an amazing visual of light emanating from the mri. they were fast, efficient, courteous. wow, perfect. this was great. suspiciously great actually. no really, something's wrong here. problem is management seems to be extremely hands on, and morally i don't feel comfortable with that. 

the bad:
